title: Paraspinal muscle radiomics from MRI alone or combined with CT for predicting outcomes after degenerative lumbar spine surgery: a scoping review.
abstract: Purpose Paraspinal muscle degeneration is increasingly recognised as a predictor of outcomes following lumbar spine surgery. This review maps studies that used paraspinal muscle radiomics, alone or within multimodal models, to predict postoperative outcomes in lumbar degenerative disease, and appraises their methodological quality and risk of bias. Methods This scoping review followed PRISMA-ScR. PubMed, Embase, Scopus and Web of Science were searched from inception to 10 April 2026. Eligible studies extracted radiomic or deep features from paraspinal muscles on preoperative MRI, with or without other tissues, modalities or clinical variables, and reported the discrimination of a model predicting a postoperative outcome. Data was charted with CHARMS-based items, quality was appraised with METRICS and risk of bias with PROBAST+AI. Findings were synthesised by clinical question, and MRI-only muscle models were presented separately from multimodal models. Results Six retrospective cohort studies were included, of which three addressed functional improvement and one study each evaluated recurrent disc herniation, radiographic adjacent segment degeneration and prolonged length of stay. Only two studies performed external validation: combined models achieved areas under the curve (AUCs) of 0.79-0.80 for functional outcome after open fusion and 0.835 for radiographic adjacent segment degeneration. Internally validated AUCs of final models ranged from 0.76 to 0.94 and depended on the resampling design. In the largest cohort, adding radiomics to clinical predictors significantly improved discrimination. In two others, incremental value was limited: radiomics added only a small gain over conventional fatty infiltration (AUC 0.922 to 0.936), and adding clinical and disc features did not improve a muscle radiomics model (0.814 vs 0.862; p = 0.083). Calibration was assessed in five studies, and none reported calibration slope or intercept. METRICS quality was good in four studies and moderate in two; under PROBAST+AI, five studies were judged at high concern or high risk of bias and one unclear. Conclusion Paraspinal muscle radiomics from routine preoperative imaging is a promising way to predict outcomes after surgery for lumbar degenerative disease, using scans that patients already have. However, the evidence comes from a small number of heterogeneous retrospective studies, mostly at high risk of bias, with limited assessment of calibration and inconsistent incremental value over conventional measures. The models remain investigational, but prospective multicentre studies with rigorous pipelines, standardised outcomes, clinical comparators, external validation, calibration and decision-curve analysis could move them towards clinical use.

title: Machine learning-based differentiation of congenital and adolescent idiopathic scoliosis using routine radiographic parameters.
abstract: Purpose Accurate differentiation of congenital scoliosis (CS) from adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) is important for appropriate diagnostic evaluation and subsequent imaging work-up. We evaluated machine learning models using routinely available demographic and radiographic variables to distinguish CS from AIS. Methods In this retrospective single-center study, 166 pediatric patients with scoliosis who underwent standing radiography and MRI between 2018 and 2025 were included. Etiological classification was based on clinical and imaging findings, including whole-spine MRI. Demographic and conventional radiographic variables were used to develop Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest, and k-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN) models. Model performance was assessed using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, F1-score, receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC-AUC), calibration analysis, decision curve analysis, and SHAP-based interpretability. Results Of the 166 patients, 96 (57.8%) had AIS and 70 (42.2%) had congenital scoliosis. Logistic Regression achieved the highest overall accuracy (79.4%), whereas Random Forest demonstrated the highest discriminative performance (ROC-AUC, 0.829). Pairwise comparisons using the DeLong test showed no statistically significant differences between the evaluated models. SHAP analysis identified Cobb angle, age, vertebral level, and Nash-Moe rotation grade as the most influential predictors. Calibration performance varied across models, while decision curve analysis demonstrated the greatest net benefit for Logistic Regression. Conclusion Machine learning models demonstrated moderate diagnostic performance in differentiating congenital scoliosis from AIS. However, their limited sensitivity and potential for false-negative predictions preclude independent clinical use. Larger studies and external validation are required before their potential role as adjunctive decision-support tools can be established.

title: Coronal alignment pattern of pelvic obliquity in degenerative lumbar scoliosis: a classification based on pelvic obliquity orientation and global coronal balance.
abstract: Background and objectives Few studies have investigated the relationship between pelvic obliquity (PO) and coronal balance in degenerative lumbar scoliosis (DLS). This study investigated the associations between PO and coronal balance in DLS and compared the radiographic characteristics and clinical outcomes of different PO orientations. Methods This study included 166 patients with DLS. Coronal parameters included coronal balance distance (CBD), main Cobb angle (MC), fractional Cobb angle (FC), and PO. Patients were categorized as Type 1 (PO oriented toward the convex side of the main curve) or Type 2 (PO oriented toward the concave side of the main curve). Based on CBD, patients were further classified as coronal balanced (Type A), coronal imbalance shifted toward the concavity (Type B), or coronal imbalance shifted toward the convexity (Type C). Paraspinal muscle (PSM) morphology was evaluated on magnetic resonance imaging. Clinical outcomes including the visual analogue scale (VAS), Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), and Scoliosis Research Society-22R (SRS-22R) were recorded at baseline. Results Of the 166 patients, 80 were classified as A1, 17 as A2, 28 as B1, 6 as B2, 24 as C1, and 11 as C2. Patients in Type 2 exhibited greater FC, vertebral rotation and lateral listhesis, as well as more severe and asymmetric degeneration of lumbosacral PSM. Patients in the C2 group tended to show a higher VAS-back score and lower SRS-22R function/activity and pain domain scores. In Type 1, PO was significantly correlated with MC (r = 0.467, p < 0.01) and MC-FC (r = 0.501, p < 0.01). In Type 2, PO was significantly correlated with FC (r = 0.390, p = 0.021). No significant correlation was found between PO and CBD in either type (both p > 0.05). Conclusion In patients with DLS, PO was associated with regional scoliotic deformity rather than global coronal balance. Background and objectives

Few studies have investigated the relationship between pelvic obliquity (PO) and coronal balance in degenerative lumbar scoliosis (DLS). This study investigated the associations between PO and coronal balance in DLS and compared the radiographic characteristics and clinical outcomes of different PO orientations.

Methods

This study included 166 patients with DLS. Coronal parameters included coronal balance distance (CBD), main Cobb angle (MC), fractional Cobb angle (FC), and PO. Patients were categorized as Type 1 (PO oriented toward the convex side of the main curve) or Type 2 (PO oriented toward the concave side of the main curve). Based on CBD, patients were further classified as coronal balanced (Type A), coronal imbalance shifted toward the concavity (Type B), or coronal imbalance shifted toward the convexity (Type C). Paraspinal muscle (PSM) morphology was evaluated on magnetic resonance imaging. Clinical outcomes including the visual analogue scale (VAS), Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), and Scoliosis Research Society-22R (SRS-22R) were recorded at baseline.

Results

Of the 166 patients, 80 were classified as A1, 17 as A2, 28 as B1, 6 as B2, 24 as C1, and 11 as C2. Patients in Type 2 exhibited greater FC, vertebral rotation and lateral listhesis, as well as more severe and asymmetric degeneration of lumbosacral PSM. Patients in the C2 group tended to show a higher VAS-back score and lower SRS-22R function/activity and pain domain scores. In Type 1, PO was significantly correlated with MC (r = 0.467, p < 0.01) and MC-FC (r = 0.501, p < 0.01). In Type 2, PO was significantly correlated with FC (r = 0.390, p = 0.021). No significant correlation was found between PO and CBD in either type (both p > 0.05).

Conclusion

In patients with DLS, PO was associated with regional scoliotic deformity rather than global coronal balance. Patients with PO oriented toward the concave side of the main curve demonstrated more severe lumbosacral coronal and rotational deformity, accompanied by more severe and asymmetric degeneration of the lumbosacral PSM. These patients also tended to show worse pain and activity-related outcomes.

title: The level of maximum compression and spinal cord motion readouts improve classification models of patients with mild versus moderate-severe degenerative cervical myelopathy.
abstract: Objective Degenerative cervical myelopathy (DCM) is the most common spinal cord dysfunction, leading to disability and reduced quality of life. Early clinical recognition is challenging, pathophysiological mechanisms are diverse, and routine imaging often fails to capture clinical severity. This study evaluated whether new magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) parameters improve machine learning classification of patients into mild vs. moderate-severe (modified Japanese Orthopaedic Association Score < 15 points) DCM. We hypothesised that incorporating measures of spinal cord dynamics would yield superior classification models compared to those based solely on static compression and conventional MRI findings. Methods We included 112 patients with DCM from a cohort of 171 patients in a prospective single-center study (Balgrist University Hospital, Zurich) recruited between October 2016 and April 2024. Classification in the first model employed the following radiological variables: cervical segment of the maximum stenosis, number of severe stenoses, presence of a T2w hyperintense signal within the spinal cord and adapted spinal canal occupation ratio (aSCOR) at maximum stenosis. Model performance was compared to a second model including the additional parameter motion displacement at maximum stenosis using Wilcoxon's signed rank test across 10 rounds of random 5-fold cross-validation. Results In this patient cohort, incorporating motion displacement at the site of maximum stenosis significantly improved model performance by reducing the weighted misclassification cost (p = 0.0039). Cross-validated classification accuracy also increased from 69.6% ± 3.2% to 73.7% ± 4.6% (p = 0.0059). The most significant single radiological predictor distinguishing mild from moderate-to-severe DCM was the maximum stenosis located at the C3/4 level. Conclusions Spinal cord motion displacement, as a biomarker of dynamic mechanical strain onto the cord, enhances the identification of moderate-severe DCM. The level of the maximum stenosis (i.e., maximum stenosis at segment C3/4, n = 15) emerged to impact DCM severity.

title: Artificial intelligence predictive medicine: geometric morphometrics in assisted scoliosis diagnosis.
abstract: Introduction Accurate scoliosis screening is essential for early intervention and to minimize unnecessary exposure to radiographic imaging. This study presents a landmark-based approach using Geometric Morphometric Methods combined with Elastic Net regression for the automated, non-invasive detection of adolescent idiopathic scoliosis from 3D torso surface scans. Methods A retrospective cross-sectional study was performed on 168 individuals (135 with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis and 33 controls) using automatic landmark extraction on surface meshes from previous studies. After dimensionality reduction via principal component analysis, the resulting shape variables were used to train a logistic regression model with regularization. The main outcome measures were Area Under the Curve, sensitivity, specificity and balanced accuracy to estimate the performance metrics of the Artificial Intelligence screening model. Results The model showed high discriminative ability on an unseen test dataset (Area Under the Curve = 0.926; 95% CI: 0.816-1.000). When a classification threshold derived exclusively from the training set was applied to the test set, sensitivity was 100%, specificity was 14.3%, and balanced accuracy was 57.1%. Conclusions In contrast to deep learning models, this approach offers an interpretable framework based on anatomical landmarks and does not require large datasets or extensive computational resources. The findings support further investigation of surface trunk morphology as a source of discriminative information for AIS detection. External validation in larger and more representative populations is required before clinical screening application.

title: Use of preoperative supine LEFT side-bending (LSB) radiograph in estimating the intraoperative lowest instrumented vertebra (LIV) tilt angle in Lenke 1 and 2 adolescent idiopathic scoliosis with lumbar modifier AR.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate radiographic outcomes of a patient-specific method for estimating the intraoperative LIV tilt angle using preoperative supine LEFT side-bending (LSB) radiographs in Lenke 1 or 2 AIS with lumbar modifier AR. Methods Fifty-six Lenke 1 or 2 AIS patients with lumbar modifier AR who underwent posterior spinal fusion with L3 as the LIV were included. The preoperative supine LSB LIV tilt angle adjusted for pelvic obliquity (⍺ angle) was used to estimate the target intraoperative LIV tilt angle (β angle). Outcomes included coronal balance distance (CBD), LIV disc angle, distal adding-on (AO), and persistent postoperative coronal imbalance (PCI). Results The median preoperative α angle was - 2.0° [-5.0 to 2.8], adjusted α angle was 0.0° [0.0 to 2.8], and the intraoperative β angle was 5.0° [3.0 to 7.0]. The LIV tilt angle decreased from 22.0° [19.0 to 27.0] preoperatively to 8.0° [5.3 to 11.0] immediate postoperatively and 5.4 ± 3.8° at mid-term follow-up (p < 0.001), remaining stable until final follow-up (5.0° [3.0 to 7.0], p = 0.917). The LIV disc angle and CBD improved from 9.0° [7.0 to 11.0] and 23.8 ± 14.9 mm preoperatively to 0.0° [-1.0 to 1.8] and - 1.0 [-8.0 to 0.0]mm at final follow-up, respectively (p < 0.001). Distal AO occurred in four patients (7.1%), while persistent PCI occurred in two patients (3.6%). Conclusion Preoperative supine LSB radiographs provide a reliable patient-specific reference (α angle) for estimating the intraoperative LIV tilt angle target, achieving a predictable and stable final LIV tilt angle with low rates of distal AO and persistent PCI.

title: Accuracy of anatomical landmarks for the pelvic C-clamp: a three-dimensional CT imaging study.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate the accuracy of three commonly used anatomical landmarks for pelvic C-clamp pin insertion using three-dimensional (3D) CT imaging. Methods From a cohort of patients undergoing CT angiography of the lower extremities, 3D bony reconstruction images were created. Three commonly used anatomical insertion landmarks-the intersection points described by Ganz et al. (point A), by Pohlemann et al. (point B), and by the DePuy Synthes Pelvic C-Clamp surgical guide (point C)-were drawn on the 3D CT reconstruction images, and their relationship with the SI joint surface was recorded. We additionally stratified landmark accuracy by SI joint surface morphology. Patient-level clustering was accounted for using generalized estimating equations (GEE). Results A total of 101 hemipelves were obtained from 51 patients (36 men and 15 women; mean age 61.56 years). In terms of accuracy, point A demonstrated 69.31% of points overlying the SI surface, recorded as 'IN', and 22.77% overlying the central quadrant of the SI surface, recorded as 'CENTER'; point B demonstrated 68.32% and 21.78%; and point C demonstrated 56.44% and 9.90%, respectively. Point A demonstrated significantly higher odds than point C for both 'IN' (OR 1.74, 95% CI 1.03-2.95; p = 0.0377) and 'CENTER' placement (OR 2.69, 95% CI 1.07-6.76; p = 0.0358), whereas the corresponding differences for point B did not reach statistical significance ('IN': OR 1.67, 95% CI 0.99-2.79; p = 0.0534; 'CENTER': OR 2.54, 95% CI 0.91-7.10; p = 0.0761). Anterior misplacement was the most frequent type of malposition for all insertion points. Sacral morphology did not statistically influence the accuracy of any landmark. Conclusion Point A demonstrated the highest observed imaging-defined accuracy and significantly higher odds of both IN and CENTER placement than point C after accounting for patient-level clustering. Point B showed higher odds than point C for both outcomes, but these differences did not reach statistical significance. These findings should be interpreted as bone-referenced, imaging-based estimates rather than direct evidence of biomechanical superiority or clinical safety. Fluoroscopic guidance remains advisable when clinically feasible. Level of evidence III Diagnostic Level III.

title: Surgical outcomes of single-stage posterior debridement combined with titanium mesh cage reconstruction and bone grafting for spinal infection after vertebral augmentation: a multicenter study.
abstract: Purpose To investigate the surgical outcomes of single-stage posterior debridement combined with titanium mesh cage (TMC) reconstruction and bone grafting in the treatment of spinal infection following percutaneous vertebral augmentation (VA). Methods A multicenter retrospective study was conducted, including patients who underwent surgery for spinal infection after percutaneous VA for osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures (OVCF) between January 2018 and December 2023. All patients received single-stage posterior debridement, TMC reconstruction, and bone grafting. Operative duration, intraoperative blood loss, and clinical outcomes-including preoperative, immediate postoperative, and final follow-up visual analogue scale (VAS) scores, Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), and local kyphotic Cobb angles-were recorded and analyzed. Results A total of 51 patients (17 male, 34 female; mean age: 68.35 ± 6.83 years) were enrolled, of whom 49 completed follow-up and were included in the final analysis; two patients died during follow-up and were treated as missing data. The average interval between VA and revision surgery was 7.51 ± 5.77 months. The preoperative American Spinal Injury Association (ASIA) grade was C, D, and E in 2, 40, and 9 patients, respectively. The average operation time was 201.33 ± 84.38 min, with a mean intraoperative blood loss of 900.98 ± 507.99 mL. Pathogens were detected in 31 cases postoperatively. The mean follow-up duration was 19.65 ± 4.56 months. At the final follow-up of the 49 patients, VAS scores, ODI, and local Cobb angles significantly improved compared to preoperative values (P < 0.05). Bony fusion was achieved in 45 of the 49 patients (91.8%), with an average duration of 5.44 ± 1.18 months. Conclusion Single-stage posterior debridement combined with TMC reconstruction and bone grafting was associated with favorable clinical and radiographic outcomes in patients with spinal infection following percutaneous VA.

title: Obturator internus muscle entrapment in posterior wall acetabular fractures: two cases with preoperative and intraoperative findings.
abstract: Introduction We report two cases of the rare presentation of obturator internus muscle (OI) entrapment in posterior wall fractures of the acetabulum. Although piriformis muscle entrapment has been previously reported, to the best of our knowledge, OI entrapment associated with posterior wall acetabular fractures has not been previously documented. Case presentation Case 1: A 38-year-old male presented with right hip and knee pain following a road traffic accident. He was diagnosed with a posterior hip dislocation, posterior wall and posterior column fractures of the acetabulum, and a posterior knee dislocation. During surgery, the OI muscle was found interposed between the displaced posterior wall fragment and the remaining posterior column. Case 2: A 43-year-old male sustained blunt abdominal trauma and a Pipkin type IV injury involving a femoral head fracture associated with a posterior wall acetabular fracture following a road traffic accident. After stabilisation of the abdominal injury with laparoscopic repair of the mesenteric injury, the patient underwent open reduction and internal fixation of the posterior wall fracture, along with removal of intra-articular fragments associated with an infra-foveal femoral head fracture. Intraoperatively, the OI muscle was similarly found interposed between the displaced posterior wall fragment and the remaining posterior column. In both cases, retrospective review of the preoperative CT images demonstrated OI interposition corresponding to the intraoperative findings. Both patients followed a standard postoperative rehabilitation protocol. At the one-year follow-up, both patients had satisfactory clinical outcomes, with Merle d'Aubigné-Postel scores of 16 and 17 and Harris Hip Scores of 92.7 and 93 for Cases 1 and 2, respectively. Neither patient showed radiographic evidence of post-traumatic arthritis. Conclusion These cases highlight the importance of recognising OI muscle entrapment as a potential cause of difficulty in reducing posterior wall acetabular fractures. Careful evaluation of preoperative CT images, particularly using soft-tissue window settings, may facilitate the identification of OI interposition. Intraoperatively, failure to identify the OI tendon between the superior and inferior gemelli, when both are clearly identified, should raise suspicion of entrapment. Meticulous identification of soft-tissue structures may help achieve anatomical fracture reduction and successful fixation.

title: Probe-mediated subcellular organelles translocation enabled ratiometric quantification of nitroreductase activity and microviscosity for hypoxia imaging and precise tumor delineation.
abstract: Quantitative assessment of hypoxia-induced nitroreductase (NTR) upregulation and pathological viscosity elevation offers a critical diagnostic parameter for precise cancer diagnostics.​ We propose a subcellular organelle translocation strategy for ultrasensitive quantification of NTR/microviscosity and subsequent precise evaluation of tumor hypoxia levels. The constructed NTR-sensitive probe Cy826 releases the fluorophore Cy468 upon NTR catalysis, accompanied by a significant fluorescence turn-on response (21.9-fold enhancement) and subcellular organelle translocation from endoplasmic reticulum (ER) to lysosomes, which effectively reduced local probe accumulation and significantly alleviated the aggregation-caused quenching (ACQ) effect and spectral crosstalk in quantification process. The cyclen-based hemicyanine Cy468 is a fluorophore distinct from our previously reported Cy496, with near-infrared (NIR) emission (~ 720 nm), lower logP, and lysosomal rather than mitochondrial targeting. Cy826 displays high sensitivity (LOD = 8.2 ng/mL) and excellent selectivity toward NTR, along with a strong fluorescence enhancement under high viscosity and molecular crowding conditions. The probe also facilitates real-time monitoring of viscosity changes in ER and lysosomes, and dynamically responds to endogenous NTR activity under varying hypoxia levels. Moreover, after administration of Cy826, the considerable tumor-to-background ratio (TBR > 12) enables high-contrast imaging of hypoxic tumors from early to advanced stages with favorable biocompatibility and metabolic characteristics. Our subcellular organelle translocation strategy proposed in this study offers a novel approach to mitigating ACQ effect in quantification assignment, and the high-performance NIR fluorescent probe drafted in this work provides a prospective tool for precise tumor diagnosis and intraoperative navigation via multi-parameter imaging of hypoxic tumor microenvironment.

title: Three-dimensional evaluation of maxillary sinus volume and nasal septal deviation after surgically assisted rapid maxillary expansion with and without pterygomaxillary disjunction.
abstract: Objectives This study aimed to compare changes in maxillary sinus volume and nasal septal deviation after surgically assisted rapid maxillary expansion (SARME) with and without pterygomaxillary disjunction (PMD) using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT). Materials and methods This retrospective study included 24 patients whose skeletal maturation had been determined during the preoperative orthodontic assessment based on hand-wrist radiography together with evaluation of midpalatal suture maturation on CBCT images, had undergone SARME, and had suitable preoperative CBCT scans and postoperative CBCT scans obtained 6-12 months after surgery. Patients were classified as PMD+ or PMD- according to the surgical procedure documented in the operative records (n=12 per group). Maxillary sinus volume was assessed by semi-automatic segmentation using 3D Slicer software. Nasal septal deviation was measured on coronal CBCT images. Preoperative-to-postoperative changes (T0 to T1) and between-group differences were evaluated using mixed-design ANOVA (p<0.05). Results Maxillary sinus volume increased significantly​ in both groups after SARME (p<0.001)​. Total maxillary sinus volume, averaged across the preoperative and postoperative measurements, did not differ significantly between the PMD+ and PMD- groups (p<=<0.171). However, the preoperative-to-postoperative increase (T0 to T1) was greater in the PMD+ group (time × group interaction, p<0.001). Nasal septal deviation decreased significantly in both groups after surgery (p<0.001). The time × group interaction for nasal septal deviation was not significant (p=0.535). Conclusions After SARME, maxillary sinus volume increased and nasal septal deviation decreased in both groups. The preoperative-to-postoperative increase in maxillary sinus volume was greater in the PMD+ group, whereas the change in nasal septal deviation did not differ significantly between groups. Clinical relevance These findings may contribute to treatment planning by clarifying the association between pterygomaxillary disjunction and postoperative morphological changes in maxillary sinus volume and nasal septal deviation after SARME.

title: Impact of preoperative skeletal muscle mass and body mass index on the prognosis of patients with oral squamous cell carcinoma.
abstract: Objectives Skeletal muscle mass (SMM) and nutritional status influence cancer prognosis. Cancer-related systemic inflammation may drive muscle atrophy and loss of SMM. In this retrospective study, we evaluated the prognostic impact of preoperative SMM and body mass index (BMI) in patients with oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). Materials and methods Overall, 150 patients with OSCC (excluding carcinoma in situ) who underwent curative surgery at our department between 2010 and 2019 were included. SMM was quantified by the sternocleidomastoid muscle cross-sectional area at the third cervical vertebra (C3), using sex-specific cutoff values. BMI was categorized as underweight (<18.5), normal (18.5-<25), or obese (≥25). General condition was evaluated using the Geriatric Nutritional Risk Index (GNRI) and HALP score (Hemoglobin, Albumin, Lymphocyte, and Platelet), and their associations with overall survival (OS) were analyzed. Results Overall, 32.6% of patients had low SMM. SMM was significantly correlated with BMI, GNRI, and HALP. SMM, reconstruction (present/absent), and a combined index of SMM and BMI were significantly associated with OS. Patients with low SMM and high BMI showed poorer survival. However, this subgroup comprised only five patients, and this finding should therefore be interpreted with caution. In univariable analysis, clinical stage, reconstruction, and SMM were significantly associated with OS. In multivariable analysis, SMM remained an independent prognostic factor. Conclusions Preoperative low SMM was independently associated with poorer OS in patients with OSCC and may provide additional prognostic information when assessed alongside BMI. Clinical relevance Preoperative assessment of SMM using routine computed tomography may improve risk stratification in patients with OSCC and help identify low SMM that may not be apparent from BMI alone.

title: Caries risk assessment support using artificial intelligence assisted panoramic radiography analysis.
abstract: Objectives Although artificial intelligence has shown promise in detecting dental pathologies on radiographs, integrating these findings into patient-level disease profiles and caries risk stratification remains challenging. This study aimed to address this gap by combining automated radiographic analysis with fuzzy logic. Materials and methods YOLOv11 based models were trained to automatically detect teeth and pathological findings (caries, restorations, missing teeth) in panoramic radiographs. The DMFT (Decayed, Missing, Filled Teeth) score calculated from the detections and a single anamnesis question regarding the patient's previous treatment history were incorporated into a Mamdani-type fuzzy inference system to generate a quantitative risk score and corresponding risk category (low, medium, or high). The developed model was evaluated using clinical panoramic radiographs from 200 patients. Results The YOLOv11l model achieved a recall of 0.936 in pathology detection. The resulting classifications showed agreement rates of 92.5% and 92.0% with the American Dental Association (ADA) and Caries Management by Risk Assessment (CAMBRA) protocols, respectively. Cohen's kappa values exceeded 0.87. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of integrating radiographic detections and patient information into a structured patient-level assessment. Conclusions The combination of automated image analysis and fuzzy logic provides a clinical decision-support framework for caries risk stratification based on panoramic radiographs. This approach offers an alternative way to integrate radiographic findings into a structured risk assessment process. Clinical relevance The proposed system integrates automated radiographic analysis and risk stratification into routine dental assessment without requiring additional procedures. It can support clinical decision-making and facilitate communication with patients regarding oral health.

title: Treatment strategies for primary intraosseous squamous cell carcinoma of the solid type in the mandible: a single-centre retrospective analysis.
abstract: Purpose Primary intraosseous squamous cell carcinoma (PIOSCC) of the mandible is a rare malignancy, and evidence regarding optimal management remains limited. This retrospective study aimed to evaluate clinical outcomes, explore potential clinicopathological associations, and assess the diagnostic performance of imaging modalities in patients with solid-type PIOSCC treated at a single centre. Methods Fifteen consecutive patients with solid-type PIOSCC of the mandible were retrospectively reviewed. Clinical variables, including peri-mandibular muscle infiltration and surgical margin status, imaging findings from computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance (MR) imaging, and fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (FDG-PET/CT), treatment modalities, and survival outcomes were analysed. Overall and disease-specific survival were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis. Results The 5-year disease-specific survival rate was 72.2%. For contextual reference, the corresponding 5-year disease-specific survival rate in surgically treated lower gingival squamous cell carcinoma during the same period was 75.5%. Infiltration of the peri-mandibular muscle, combined with close surgical margins, may be associated with poorer clinical outcomes. Among the various imaging modalities, fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET) showed the strongest correlation with the pathological maximum tumour diameter in this exploratory analysis. Conclusions This retrospective single-centre analysis suggests that peri-mandibular muscle infiltration and surgical margin status may be associated with prognosis in patients with solid-type PIOSCC of the mandible. FDG-PET may provide complementary information for tumour assessment. Further studies are needed to confirm these findings.

title: Rare parotid gland metastasis from colorectal cancer: a case report and review of the literature.
abstract: Metastasis of colorectal carcinoma (CRC) to the parotid gland is exceptionally rare, with only a few cases reported in the literature. We describe a 70 year old woman previously treated for sigmoid adenocarcinoma who developed a painful right parotid mass three years after hemicolectomy and adjuvant XELOX chemotherapy. Fine needle aspiration confirmed metastatic sigmoid colon adenocarcinoma through characteristic immunohistochemical markers, including CDX 2 and Villin positivity. A review of the 8 reported cases (including the current one) shows the disease occurs in patients at a mean age of 63 years (range, 34 to 83). There is no gender or side predilection. The overall features indicate that parotid metastasis from CRC typically occurs with widespread disease and carries a poor prognosis. Diagnosis is challenging because parotid metastases often mimic primary salivary gland tumours clinically and radiologically, making immunohistochemistry essential for distinguishing intestinal adenocarcinoma from primary salivary malignancies. Reported outcomes remain poor, reflecting advanced systemic disease at presentation. This case emphasises the need to consider metastatic CRC in the differential diagnosis of new parotid masses in patients with a history of colorectal malignancy. Early recognition, accurate diagnosis through imaging and histopathology, and multidisciplinary management are crucial. This case highlights the importance of considering metastatic CRC in the differential diagnosis of parotid masses in patients with a known primary malignancy.

title: Postoperative volume loss of microvascular free flaps - a three-dimensional analysis.
abstract: Objectives Microvascular free flaps are frequently used in the reconstruction of head and neck defects. Postoperatively, it can be observed that the free flaps especially for intraoral reconstructions decrease in their volume which has to be considered intraoperatively. This study aims to assess this volume loss on different free flaps. Materials and methods The volume of free flaps was recorded intraoperatively by the means of the displacement of a sterile Ringer's solution. Postoperatively the volume was determined by measuring flap sizes on the basis of MRI and CT scans after 3D segmentations of the free flaps. Statistical analyses were performed to detect differences between pre- and postoperative volumes. Results For this prospective singe-center study a total of 51 patients could be recruited and 36 patients could be included for further analyses with 28 MRI and 23 CT scans. Volume losses of ALT/ vastus lateralis flaps and RFF was about 50%, and of the lower leg perforator flap about 60%. Postoperative radiotherapy showed no significant influence (p > 0.05). Conclusion Soft tissue free flaps experience significant volume losses that have to be considered preoperatively. This study compares different free flaps among each other. The RFF shows volume losses of about 50% making it a predictable tool for reconstructions. The role of postoperative radiotherapy remains to be discussed.

title: Human assisted methodology for the creation of 3D depth maps from medical imaging: a maxillofacial application.
abstract: Purpose This paper presents a human-assisted methodology for the three-dimensional reconstruction of the facial surface from medical images, designed to provide an accessible and lightweight alternative to traditional workflows. The approach was developed with the goal of (i) generating 3D representations with quality comparable to dedicated commercial software, (ii) minimising the need for specialised operator training, and (iii) reducing computational resource requirements for large dataset processing. This study specifically evaluates the technical validity of the methodology regarding reconstruction accuracy. Methods A lightweight human-assisted pipeline is proposed for image cleaning, segmentation, and the extraction of depth maps representing the external surface. The resulting representations were quantitatively compared with those obtained using established commercial software to evaluate their geometric validity. Preliminary observations on operator training time were also recorded. Results No statistically significant differences were observed between the representations generated by the proposed methodology and those produced by the reference software, confirming high geometric fidelity. Initial testing indicated that basic operator proficiency could be achieved in under 60 min. Conclusion The proposed approach provides a favourable balance between reconstruction accuracy and accessibility. While further structured studies are required to quantify operator learning curves and large-scale processing efficiency, these results validate the methodology as a robust tool for high-quality anatomical modelling from medical imaging.

title: Ultrasound screening and secukinumab intervention for subclinical and clinical psoriatic arthritis: a prospective real-world study.
abstract: Background This prospective real-world study primarily evaluated clinical and ultrasonographic outcomes after 24 weeks of secukinumab treatment in participants with subclinical or clinical psoriatic arthritis (PsA) identified through a risk-based musculoskeletal ultrasound screening pathway. A secondary descriptive objective was to characterize the screening pathway and the identification of ultrasound-detected subclinical PsA. Methods Participants with psoriasis were enrolled at the Department of Dermatology, Tianjin Medical University, from September 1, 2022, to December 31, 2023. Participants considered at increased risk of PsA underwent musculoskeletal ultrasound assessment. They were classified as having subclinical PsA, clinical PsA, or no qualifying inflammatory ultrasound findings according to clinical and imaging findings. Participants who initiated secukinumab and completed 24 weeks of treatment and follow-up were included in the therapeutic outcome analysis. The primary outcome was the proportion achieving PASI100 at week 24. Secondary outcomes included PASI75/90 responses, ACR20/50/70 responses in clinical PsA, ultrasound changes, quality-of-life measures, and adverse events. Results Of 358 enrolled participants, 249 (69.6%) were classified as being at high risk of PsA based on the PEST score and/or prespecified clinical risk features. Among 194 high-risk participants who underwent musculoskeletal ultrasound screening, 159 had qualifying inflammatory ultrasound findings, leading to diagnoses of 42 with subclinical PsA and 117 with clinical PsA. A total of 38 participants completed a 24-week course of secukinumab. At week 24, 87.5% of subclinical PsA participants and 95.45% of clinical PsA participants achieved complete skin clearance (Psoriasis Area and Severity Index, PASI100). In the clinical PsA group, American College of Rheumatology (ACR) 20/50/70 response rates were 95.45%, 86.36%, and 72.73%, respectively. Ultrasound findings of synovitis and enthesitis improved descriptively in both groups. No serious adverse events were reported among the 38 treatment completers. Conclusion In this exploratory, single-arm real-world cohort, a risk-based musculoskeletal ultrasound pathway identified participants with imaging positive for inflammatory synovio-entheseal involvement compatible with subclinical or clinical PsA. Among the small group who completed 24 weeks of secukinumab, substantial descriptive improvements in skin outcomes, clinical measures, and selected inflammatory ultrasound findings were observed. These findings are hypothesis-generating and do not establish the diagnostic accuracy of ultrasound or demonstrate that secukinumab prevents progression from subclinical to clinical PsA. Key Points • In this exploratory cohort, a risk-based musculoskeletal ultrasound pathway identified imaging inflammatory abnormalities compatible with subclinical PsA in selected high-risk participants with psoriasis; the diagnostic accuracy of ultrasound was not assessed. • Among 38 treatment completers who received secukinumab for dermatologic indications, high PASI75/90/100 and ACR20/50/70 response rates were observed at 24 weeks; given the single-arm, uncontrolled design, these responses cannot be attributed specifically to secukinumab. • Inflammatory ultrasound findings of synovitis and enthesitis improved descriptively in both groups, supporting ultrasound as a complementary tool for monitoring treatment response rather than as a stand-alone diagnostic tes. • Enthesitis most frequently involved the finger flexor and extensor tendons, the quadriceps tendon, and the Achilles tendon; isolated structural entheseal abnormalities (e.g., bone spurs and calcifications) were common and were not interpreted as active inflammation.

title: Idiopathic inflammatory myopathies in Latin America: clinical diversity, diagnostic challenges, and unmet needs.
abstract: Idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (IIM) are a heterogeneous group of rare, systemic autoimmune diseases that remain understudied in Latin America despite the region's ethnic admixture, socioeconomic heterogeneity, and unequal access to rheumatologic care. This narrative review synthesizes the literature on IIM from Latin American centers, integrating single- and multicenter cohorts, national registries, and collaborative networks. Dermatomyositis is the most frequently reported subtype in most national series, although this may partly reflect differences in patient selection and classification, and regional autoantibody profiles show distinctive features, including a high frequency of anti-Mi-2 in Mexican cohorts and among Colombian patients in a multinational survey and emerging data on anti-MDA5-associated dermatomyositis in Latin American cohorts that diverge phenotypically from Asian cohorts. Anti-synthetase syndrome, immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy, inclusion body myositis, and juvenile dermatomyositis are characterized mainly through Brazilian series, complemented by Argentine data and multinational collaborations, alongside multicenter data on myositis-associated interstitial lung disease from Argentina, Chile, and Mexico. The COVID-19 pandemic further complicated regional care, prompting pharmacovigilance and vaccine-safety collaborations, including a Brazilian interventional trial of an inactivated SARS-CoV-2 vaccine. We highlight neglected dimensions of regional IIM care, including reproductive health. Persistent obstacles include diagnostic delay, restricted access to myositis-specific and myositis-associated autoantibody panels, heterogeneous availability of muscle MRI and biopsy, and inequitable access to immunosuppressive and biologic therapies across public and private health systems. We highlight priority actions, including expansion of multinational registries, harmonization of diagnostic algorithms, and investment in translational research reflecting the admixed ancestry of Latin American populations, which may help reduce diagnostic delay and improve long-term outcomes.

title: Clinical utility of dual-energy CT-guided gout management: a single-centre retrospective before-and-after study.
abstract: Background Dual-energy CT (DECT) can visualize monosodium urate (MSU) deposition, but evidence is limited regarding potential clinical benefits of DECT beyond diagnosis in gout. Objectives To evaluate potential clinical benefits of performing DECT beyond diagnosis in patients with gout. Methods We conducted a retrospective pre-/post-implementation study at the rheumatology outpatient clinic of Jeju National University Hospital, Jeju, Republic of Korea (May 2016-April 2020). DECT was introduced in May 2018. Among patients who underwent DECT, DECT positivity and disease-duration discrimination were assessed using ROC/AUC and cutoffs were explored. For prognostic comparisons, analyses were restricted to patients without clinically apparent subcutaneous tophi at baseline and compared the DECT-performed group with the no-DECT group using stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW). Results A total of 722 patients were included (no-DECT n = 506; DECT performed n = 216). Among DECT-performed patients, 110/216 were DECT-positive (50.9%). Disease duration showed limited discrimination for DECT positivity (AUC 0.626). In prognosis analyses (n = 645), IPTW-weighted flare outcomes were similar between groups (any flare: OR 1.26, 95% CI 0.87-1.83; flare count: IRR 1.37, 95% CI 0.94-2.01), and change in serum urate did not differ (β 0.01 mg/dL, 95% CI - 0.32 to 0.34). Renal outcomes favored the DECT-performed group (ΔeGFR β 2.39 mL/min/1.73m2, 95% CI 0.27-4.51; eGFR decline ≥ 10: OR 0.55, 95% CI 0.31-0.95; CKD stage worsening: OR 0.52, 95% CI 0.30-0.90). Conclusions Clinically occult MSU deposition was detected by DECT in approximately half of scanned patients, and disease duration alone had limited utility for identifying DECT-positive patients. In weighted analyses among patients without clinically apparent subcutaneous tophi, DECT performance was not associated with flare outcomes or serum urate change but was associated with more favorable renal outcomes. Key Points • Dual-energy CT (DECT) detected clinically occult monosodium urate deposition in approximately half of scanned gout patients (50.9%). • In IPTW-weighted analyses among patients without clinically apparent subcutaneous tophi, DECT performance was not associated with 1-year flare outcomes or serum urate change. • DECT performance was associated with more favorable 1-year renal outcomes, including greater ΔeGFR and lower risks of eGFR decline and CKD stage worsening.

title: Isolated body lateropulsion due to a paramedian mesencephalic stroke.
abstract: We report a 71-year-old man who presented with acute recurrent falls due to isolated body lateropulsion to the right, as sole neurological deficit. Brain MRI revealed a left paramedian mesencephalic infarction involving the interstitial nucleus of Cajal (INC) and medial longitudinal fasciculus (MLF). Isolated body lateropulsion is a rare clinical presentation produced by lesions affecting the graviceptive pathway, which processes gravitational input and body orientation relative to vertical in order to maintain upright posture and spatial orientation. Although internuclear ophtalmoplegia or abnormalities of vertical or torsional eye position have been associated with lesions of the INC and MLF, these were absent in our patient.The patient recovered fully within three months, consistent with the favorable prognosis of isolated lateropulsion due to stroke. This case highlights an under-recognized topodiagnostic pattern within the graviceptive pathway.

title: Navigated laser photocoagulation reduces injection burden and recurrence in diabetic macular edema: A 24-month real-world comparative study.
abstract: Diabetic macular edema (DME) requires frequent intravitreal anti-VEGF injections, creating substantial treatment burden. Navigated laser photocoagulation offers precise microaneurysm targeting, but its adjunctive benefit with anti-VEGF therapy remains inadequately documented in real-world settings. This retrospective comparative study included 87 treatment-naive DME patients followed for 24 months. Group A (n = 42) received intravitreal bevacizumab monotherapy; Group B (n = 45) received combination therapy (bevacizumab plus Navilas navigated laser photocoagulation). Primary endpoints were injection burden, recurrence rates, and hyperreflective dot (HRD) count as an inflammatory biomarker on spectral-domain optical coherence tomography. Combination therapy required significantly fewer injections over 24 months (4.6 ± 1.8 vs. 7.3 ± 2.1; p < 0.001), representing 37% reduction. Recurrence rates were lower in the combination group (17.8% vs. 33.3%; p = 0.03). Kaplan-Meier analysis showed significantly prolonged recurrence-free survival in the combination group (log-rank p = 0.016), with 24-month recurrence-free survival of 82.2% versus 66.7%. HRD reduction was superior with combination therapy (61% vs. 28%; p = 0.01). Baseline HRD count correlated with injection frequency (r=-0.54; p < 0.001) and recurrence risk (r = 0.48; p = 0.002). Visual acuity gains and central retinal thickness reductions were equivalent between groups. No serious adverse events occurred; 8.9% required repeat laser. Navigated laser photocoagulation combined with bevacizumab significantly reduces injection burden and recurrence in DME while maintaining efficacy, offering a more sustainable treatment approach. HRD count emerged as a clinically accessible biomarker for treatment planning.

Visual acuity gains and central retinal thickness reductions were equivalent between groups. No serious adverse events occurred; 8.9% required repeat laser. Navigated laser photocoagulation combined with bevacizumab significantly reduces injection burden and recurrence in DME while maintaining efficacy, offering a more sustainable treatment approach. HRD count emerged as a clinically accessible biomarker for treatment planning.

title: Endoscopic NIRAF-LSCI multimodal system with pseudo-color visualization for parathyroid autofluorescence localization and tissue perfusion assessment: preclinical validation.
abstract: Postoperative hypoparathyroidism remains a prevalent complication of thyroid surgery, primarily caused by unrecognized parathyroid gland (PG) injury or devascularization. While near-infrared autofluorescence (NIRAF) enables accurate PG localization, it provides no functional perfusion information; conversely, laser speckle contrast imaging (LSCI) offers label-free real-time perfusion assessment. Herein, we validated a multimodal endoscopic system integrating NIRAF and LSCI for simultaneous PG identification and vascular evaluation, focusing on LSCI perfusion performance and the clinical practicability of its pseudo-color semi-quantitative visualization. The system was tested in 8 Sprague-Dawley rats, where rat thyroids with homologous blood supply served as perfusion surrogates due to the minute volume of rat PGs. Imaging was performed under three strictly controlled in situ conditions: intact native vascularization, partial vascular occlusion, and complete vascular occlusion. LSCI pseudo-color visualization was generated via a standardized pipeline including temporal laser speckle contrast analysis (tLASCA)-based blood flow index (BFI) calculation, baseline-anchored joint 5th-95th percentile normalization, and Jet colormap mapping. Intraoperative probe-based quantitative NIRAF was used to validate NIRAF-visual signal foci. NIRAF clearly identified PGs with a fluorescence intensity of 149.8 ± 8.7 mV, significantly higher than thyroid (93.8 ± 8.0 mV), trachea (84.6 ± 9.1 mV), and muscle (66.3 ± 10.4 mV) (all P < 0.001), achieving 100% positive predictive value (PPV) and 100% negative predictive value (NPV), with zero false-positive findings among all NIRAF-visual foci. PPV was determined using both probe-based NIRAF and histopathology as dual validation references, whereas NPV was determined using postoperative histopathology alone as the reference standard. LSCI speckle contrast increased progressively with decreasing perfusion, with speckle contrast values mapped to a continuous blue-to-red real-time pseudo-color perfusion visualization. Histopathology confirmed all fluorescent tissues as PGs. This multimodal system targets two core clinical needs for intraoperative PG protection, and its standardized pseudo-color semi-quantitative workflow provides real-time label-free perfusion visualization. It shows potential to serve as an intraoperative adjunct to guide parathyroid preservation decisions and reduce reliance on delayed hormonal test results.

title: Proposal of modified gastric cancer RECIST (mgcRECIST): CT-based criteria for response assessment in metastatic gastric cancer.
abstract: Background In Western countries, many patients with gastric cancer (GC) are diagnosed at a metastatic stage, with a median overall survival (OS) of less than 12 months. Although imaging is pivotal for staging, restaging, and response assessment, RECIST 1.1 has significant limitations in metastatic GC, particularly for lymph node (LN) and peritoneal involvement. We aimed to propose modified gastric cancer RECIST (mgcRECIST) criteria that better account for these patterns of disease spread. Methods In the Italian multicenter prospective METAGASTRO registry, we identified 187 patients with metastatic GC who received at least one chemotherapy cycle and underwent both staging and restaging contrast-enhanced CT. RECIST 1.1 was assessed using three approaches to the primary tumor: D-max, defined as the maximum curvilinear diameter on multiplanar CT images, wall thickness, or exclusion. mgcRECIST integrated RECIST 1.1 using D-max with rPCI progression and persistent lymph nodes with short-axis diameter ≥ 15 mm. Overall survival (OS) stratification according to RECIST 1.1 and mgcRECIST was compared. Results RECIST 1.1 provided the clearest prognostic separation when the primary tumor was included using D-max (p < 0.001). At restaging, lymph-node persistence with SAD ≥ 15 mm and rPCI progression ≥ 6 points were associated with shorter OS. mgcRECIST yielded distinct prognostic categories, further subdivided RECIST 1.1 response groups, and improved OS concordance compared with RECIST 1.1 using D-max (C-index 0.737 vs. 0.719; p = 0.039). Conclusions The proposed mgcRECIST showed promising prognostic stratification and improved prognostic discrimination. If prospectively validated, it may provide a simple, CT-based tool for response assessment and risk stratification in metastatic GC.

title: Standard anterior temporal lobectomy using a retractorless technique in patients with drug-resistant mesial temporal lobe epilepsy: long-term seizure outcomes and predictors of postoperative seizure freedom.
abstract: Background Fixed brain retractors risk focal ischemia and cortical injury. Although retractorless dynamic retraction is established in skull base surgery, its role in epilepsy surgery remains poorly characterized. Objective To evaluate long-term seizure outcomes, safety, and reliability of retractorless standard anterior temporal lobectomy (ATL) in drug-resistant mesial temporal lobe epilepsy (MTLE), and identify predictors of seizure freedom. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 42 patients who underwent retractorless standard ATL for drug-resistant MTLE. Dynamic retraction used bipolar forceps and pressure-controlled suction. The primary outcome was seizure freedom (Engel Class Ia) at minimum 24-month follow-up; secondary outcomes were complications and resection adequacy on postoperative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Predictors were identified using multivariable logistic regression and Cox proportional hazards models. Results At a mean follow-up of 66.3 months, 69% of patients achieved complete seizure freedom (Engel Class Ia), and 83.3% achieved freedom from disabling seizures (Engel Class I). Postoperative MRI confirmed adequate resection in 95.2% of cases. Complications were uncommon and unrelated to retraction injury. Low preoperative seizure frequency (< 3 seizures/week) was the sole independent predictor of seizure freedom (odds ratio, 24.21; P = 0.026), while higher frequency (≥ 3 seizures/week) was associated with increased recurrence risk (hazard ratio, 7.34; P = 0.042). Conclusion Retractorless standard ATL is safe and effective for drug-resistant MTLE, achieving long-term seizure control while minimizing retraction-associated risks. Preoperative seizure burden was the dominant prognostic marker, supporting early surgical intervention.

title: Obstructive hydrocephalus due to posterior third ventricle pathology: One or two burr hole approaches for ETV and biopsy.
abstract: Endoscopic third ventriculostomy (ETV) and tumor biopsy is a frequent procedure for third ventricular tumors. While some authors favor one approach to achieve both goals, others support the selection of two approaches to avoid fornical damage and venous hemorrhage. Here the authors present their experience with both techniques. A retrospective analysis was conducted on cases which underwent an ETV and a tumor procedure in lesions of the posterior third ventricle from 2011 to 2025. Patient records, pre- and postoperative imaging and intraoperative video recordings were retrospectively analyzed. Twenty-six patients met the inclusion criteria: 13 were treated with one, the other 13 with two approaches. The surgical goal of ETV and tumor biopsy/resection was achieved in all cases. No procedure was abandoned. No postoperative complication was observed. Intraoperative forniceal injury was observed in 8/26 patients (31%). Intraoperative bleeding was found in 81% (21/26 cases). In 19% of cases (5/26 cases), intraoperative bleeding required a longer irrigation time but no switch to dry field technique or open surgery was needed. On follow up, three patients required ventriculoperitoneal shunt placement. Thus, ETV success scored 88.5% (23/26 cases). On 2D MRI, the mean intertrajectory angle was smaller in the one-burr-hole group than in the two-burr-hole group (41.8° ± 3.5° vs. 48.7° ± 5.4°; p = 0.001). Lesions of the posterior third ventricle causing obstructive hydrocephalus are ideal candidates for an endoscopic approach. The overall success rate is very high with acceptable surgical risks. In this cohort, larger intertrajectory angles were associated with selection of a two-burr-hole approach. The approximate 45° value was derived post hoc and requires external validation.

title: Deep learning MGMT promoter methylation status prediction in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma using multiparametric MRI: Benchmark vs. real‑world performance.
abstract: Preoperative determination of O6-methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase (MGMT) promoter methylation status is of major prognostic and predictive relevance in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma, yet currently depends on invasive tissue sampling. This study investigates deep learning-based strategies for MGMT prediction from multiparametric MRIs, with particular emphasis on robustness and generalizability under heterogeneous, multicenter conditions. A total of 949 glioblastoma cases were analyzed, integrating public benchmark data from the Brain Tumor Segmentation Challenge (BraTS) with multi-institutional private cohorts acquired across diverse scanners and imaging protocols. Four complementary experimental settings were designed to compare reproduced literature baselines, private-only training, whole-brain end-to-end models, and segmentation-guided region-of-interest (ROI) pipelines. Tumor delineation was performed using an nnU-Net framework with expert quality control, and multiple three-dimensional convolutional neural network architectures were evaluated. Model performance was highest on the homogeneous BraTS benchmark, where a whole-brain DenseNet121 achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.80. However, marked performance deterioration was observed when models were evaluated on independent held-out multicenter test set. In contrast, segmentation-guided ROI-based approaches showed a more stable performance profile in this preliminary independent held-out multicenter test. Explicit lesion localization was associated with reduction in false-positive classifications, suggesting a potential benefit for performance stability across heterogeneous datasets, although validation in external cohorts from institutions not represented during training is required. Collectively, these results demonstrate that upstream methodological choices, especially tumor segmentation and ROI definition, remain critical determinants of performance in MRI-based radiogenomic modeling. Future studies should emphasize prospective multicenter validation, domain-shift harmonization, multimodal data integration, and uncertainty-aware deep learning to enhance robustness and interpretability.

title: DANTE T1-SPACE MR imaging for visualization of inferior and superior petrosal sinus anatomy in cavernous sinus DAVF.
abstract: DANTE (Delay Alternating with Nutation for Tailored Excitation) is useful for investigating venous sinus conditions, including thrombosis, hypoplasia, and occlusions. The study aimed to assess the efficacy of the DANTE MRI sequence in visualizing the inferior petrosal sinus (IPS) and superior petrosal sinus (SPS) in patients with cavernous sinus dural arteriovenous fistulas (CSDAVFs). DANTE preparation provides robust suppression of flowing blood signal while preserving stationary tissue signal, which may improve delineation of venous sinus lumen and wall changes compared with conventional 3D TSE sequences. Fourteen patients with cavernous sinus dural arteriovenous fistulas were retrospectively analyzed. All patients underwent contrast-enhanced DANTE T1-SPACE MRI prior to endovascular treatment. IPS patency was independently evaluated on MRI and descriptively compared with digital subtraction angiography. Nine out of fourteen patients demonstrated occlusion of the ipsilateral IPS. Two had stenotic changes in the IPS. The IPS was identified in all patients, regardless of patency, and transvenous embolization was successfully performed via the IPS in all treated cases. In the SPS, lumen continuity between SPS and Cavernous sinus was confirmed in 5 cases. 78.5% of patients achieved occlusion immediately after treatment, with the remaining patients occluded during follow-up. Contrast-enhanced DANTE T1-SPACE offers high-contrast depiction of IPS/SPS by effective blood-signal suppression with preservation of static tissue signal, facilitating preprocedural anatomical clarification in CSDAVF. This information may be particularly useful in cases with suspected IPS occlusion, where preprocedural anatomical clarification is clinically relevant.

title: Endovascular robotic-assisted system for cerebral angiography (ERASE): Rationale, design, and protocol of a multicenter randomized controlled trial.
abstract: Neurointerventional therapy is a cornerstone in managing head and neck vascular disorders, with cerebral angiography serving as its fundamental diagnostic and therapeutic backbone. However, manual cerebral angiography is associated with several inherent limitations. While existing robotic-assisted systems have shown promise in mitigating some of these issues, they face challenges such as limited compatibility, lengthy setup times, and a lack of high-quality real-world evidence. The ERASE trial is a multicenter, prospective, randomized controlled trial (RCT). A total of 660 eligible patients will be enrolled from seven comprehensive stroke centers in China and randomized 1:1 to either the robotic-assisted group or the control group. Both groups use the Seldinger technique for femoral/radial artery access. Operators undergo standardized training on the robotic system. The trial adopts a prospective randomized open-label blinded endpoint (PROBE) design, with all imaging endpoints adjudicated via blinded review by an independent imaging core laboratory. All patients are followed up at baseline, end of surgery, 24 h postoperatively, and 7 days post-discharge. The primary efficacy outcome is the clinical success rate. The primary safety outcome is the incidence of perioperative/postoperative complications (e.g., vascular perforation, dissection, pseudoaneurysm), serious adverse events, and device malfunctions. Secondary outcomes include technical failure rate, overall procedural time, pre-puncture setup time, mean catheterization time per target vessel, super-selective technique success rate, DSA fluoroscopy time, participant radiation dose, primary operator radiation dose, contrast agent volume and instrument performance evaluation. A key safety endpoint is the rate of new asymptomatic cerebral infarctions detected via postoperative brain MRI-diffusion-weighted imaging. As the RCT focusing on the YDHB-NS01 Ver 2.0 system, the ERASE trial addresses critical unmet needs in neurointerventional practice and will generate high-quality evidence for robotic-assisted cerebral angiography. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07182188. TRIAL REGISTRATION DATE: 2025-09-18.

title: Intraoperative technology in skull base and vascular neurosurgery: a two-stage cross-sectional national survey.
abstract: Skull base and vascular neurosurgery rely on diverse intraoperative technologies, but contemporary data describing how frequently they are used at the level of individual operations are limited. On behalf of the Society of British Neurological Surgeons (SBNS) MedTech Committee, we aimed to establish a dated descriptive baseline of reported technology use across three operative paradigms. We conducted a two-stage cross-sectional survey of neurosurgeons in the UK and Ireland via the Society of British Neurological Surgeons (SBNS). Six MedTech Committee members compiled a pragmatic technology list. Respondents reported frequency of use for three exemplar procedures: transsphenoidal pituitary adenoma, retrosigmoid vestibular schwannoma, and pterional aneurysm surgery. Use was recorded on a four-point ordinal scale and analysed descriptively, with Kendall's tau-b used to explore the relationship between experience and reported use. Twenty-four responses from 20 of the 32 adult or mixed adult-paediatric UK units were analysed (11 units per index procedure). Reported use was strongly procedure specific. Neuronavigation was used always or almost always by 8/12 transsphenoidal respondents but infrequently elsewhere. Endoscopy had displaced microscopy in transsphenoidal surgery, whereas microscopy was used always or almost always by all retrosigmoid and pterional respondents. Indocyanine green and micro-Doppler were routine for aneurysms. Neurophysiological monitoring was universal for vestibular schwannoma but evenly divided for aneurysms. Exoscopes, intraoperative MRI and robotics were used infrequently or not at all; augmented reality was reported by 5/13 pterional respondents. No association was found between experience and reported use, though this was underpowered. Reported intraoperative technology use is strongly shaped by operative paradigm, with established technologies clustering around recurring procedural needs. Newer technologies were used infrequently. Because availability was not recorded, non-use cannot be distinguished from lack of access. These data provide a dated baseline against which future change can be assessed.

title: Surgical versus conservative management of acute subdural hematoma in elderly patients: a systematic review of functional outcomes and prognostic factors.
abstract: Management of acute subdural hematoma in the elderly requires nuanced clinical decision-making. While the Brain Trauma Foundation incorporates clot thickness and midline shift in their ASDH management guidelines, they do not quote an age bracket cut-off. Evidence to date suggests the elderly see disproportionately high morbidity and mortality regardless of surgical or conservative management. To systematically review the evidence comparing surgical evacuation versus conservative management of ASDH in elderly patients and assess the impact of patient factors on outcomes, a systematic review was conducted examining six observational studies (n = 812) comparing surgical and conservative management of traumatic ASDH in patients aged 60 or older. Outcomes included in-hospital mortality, 6-month mortality, and functional outcomes. MEDLINE, Embase and CINAHL were searched up to December 2025. Risk of bias assessment was performed using the Newcastle Ottawa Scale. Results were presented descriptively and synthesized narratively by outcome timepoint as clinical and methodological heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis. Surgery was not consistently associated with improved mortality nor improved functional outcomes. Surgical patients presented with worse clinical and radiological severity. In-hospital mortality analysis of three cohorts demonstrated substantial heterogeneity, with relative risks ranging from 1.37 to 13.63, favoring conservative management. Six-month mortality showed even greater heterogeneity with directionally inconsistent findings. Functional outcomes, when reported, either favored conservative management or were neutral. Current evidence does not establish a consistent mortality or functional advantage for surgical evacuation of ASDH in elderly patients. Patients with poor neurological status demonstrate high mortality regardless of intervention, while those with mild neurological impairment may not derive meaningful benefit from surgery. Future prospective studies should standardize frailty assessment alongside clinical and radiographic parameters to identify where true clinical equipoise exists and establish guidelines in this distinct patient population. No funding was received for this review.

title: Comorbidity burden and radiographically significant interval rebleeding after supratentorial intracerebral hematoma evacuation: a single-center cohort study.
abstract: How the association between comorbidity burden and postoperative rebleeding varies with the imaging definition remains incompletely characterized. This single-center cohort included 111 patients undergoing intracerebral hematoma evacuation (2016-2025), with retrospective ascertainment and prospective study-specific data collection after ethics approval. We compared 0-1 versus ≥ 2 documented comorbidity categories. Rebleeding required a visually confirmed new or increased hemorrhagic component between early and second postoperative computed tomography scans, with interval volume increase > 20 mL and > 25% of preoperative volume. Analyses also used alternative volumetric thresholds. Primary rebleeding occurred in 2/78 patients (2.6%) with 0-1 category and 9/33 (27.3%) with ≥ 2 categories: conditional odds ratio (OR) 13.84, exact 95% confidence interval (CI) 2.62-140.31; p < 0.001; absolute risk difference 24.7% points. Associations were weaker under alternative thresholds: OR 2.84 (95% CI 0.89-9.18) for an increase > 25% of preoperative volume and OR 1.54 (95% CI 0.61-4.03) for ≥ 6 mL or ≥ 33% of the early postoperative volume. Excluding five patients with intervening residual-clot revision yielded a similar primary association (n = 106; OR 14.47, exact 95% CI 2.72-147.36). Eight of 11 patients with primary rebleeding underwent revision. Median intensive care stay was 10 versus 6 days. Anticoagulant exposure was associated with rebleeding in crude analysis and overlapped with multimorbidity. Documented multimorbidity was associated with large interval rebleeding under the study definition, but the association depended on the volumetric threshold. The small event count, incomplete neurological assessability, documentation-based exposure ascertainment and residual confounding limit causal and predictive interpretation.

title: Volumetric cadaveric study of transorbital neuroendoscopic vs transcranial approach for anterior clinoidectomy: a pilot study.
abstract: The anterior clinoid process is a crucial anatomical landmark of the anterior skull base that obscures the visualization of key neurovascular structures. While the transcranial extradural approach is the standard for anterior clinoid process resection, the transorbital neuroendoscopic surgery approach has emerged as a minimally invasive alternative. This pilot study aims to perform the first head-to-head volumetric comparison of anterior clinoid process resection between transorbital neuroendoscopic surgery and the transcranial approach in a paired cadaveric model. Six fresh-frozen cadaveric heads (12 sides) were used in a paired control design. Each specimen underwent a standard pterional extradural anterior clinoidectomy on one side and a transorbital neuroendoscopic surgery anterior clinoidectomy on the contralateral side. Pre- and post-dissection computed tomography scans were analyzed to quantify the volume of bone resection. The mean anterior clinoid process resection rate was 91.5% for the transcranial approach and 87.1% for the transorbital neuroendoscopic surgery approach. The mean volume of resected bone was identical in both groups (206 mm³). Statistical analysis revealed no significant difference in the percentage of bone resection between the two techniques (p = 0.494). Transorbital neuroendoscopic surgery is a feasible and effective technique for anterior clinoidectomy, achieving bone resection rates statistically equivalent to the transcranial standard. Its inferolateral trajectory enables safe, direct optic strut disconnection without brain retraction.

title: The LNHR-AVM Scale: A multimodal radiomic, angioarchitectural, and dosimetric system for outcome prediction and personalized treatment planning in AVM Radiosurgery.
abstract: Background Existing AVM grading systems incompletely capture the imaging, angioarchitectural, and dosimetric heterogeneity that influences outcomes after Gamma Knife radiosurgery (GKRS). We developed the Learning Neurovascular Hazards through Radiomics-AVM (LNHR-AVM) Scale, a radiosurgery-specific grading and treatment-planning system. Methods We retrospectively screened 2,000 patients and included 600 with clinical, MRI, angiographic, dosimetric, segmentation, and outcome data. Radiomics were extracted from FSPGR/T1 + C, T2, T2 CUBE/Volume, FLAIR, SWAN, and anteroposterior and lateral digital subtraction angiography. The primary endpoint was favorable outcome, defined as complete obliteration without post-GKRS hemorrhage, permanent symptomatic adverse radiation effects, or permanent neurological deterioration. Models were developed in 480 patients using nested 5 × 5 cross-validation and tested in a locked temporal cohort of 120 patients. Separate modules estimated obliteration timing, hemorrhage, injury, dose, and staging. Results Median age was 39 years, median nidus volume was 2.8 cm 3 , median prescription dose was 20 Gy, and median follow-up was 76 months. Favorable outcome occurred in 59.3%, complete obliteration in 65.7%, and post-GKRS hemorrhage in 6.3%. The integrated model achieved a locked-test AUROC of 0.884, average precision of 0.901, Brier score of 0.118, calibration intercept of 0.01, and calibration slope of 0.97. The integer score retained similar performance (AUROC, 0.873) and outperformed Spetzler-Martin, modified RBAS, and the Virginia scale. The obliteration module achieved a C-index of 0.861 and 7.2-month median timing error. Dose and staging recommendations agreed with expert consensus. Conclusions LNHR-AVM provides an internally validated, interpretable framework for AVM risk stratification, outcome prediction, and radiosurgical planning. External multicenter validation is required.
