title: PINet: A Pediatric Intussusception Network with Dual-Scale Guided Attention for Auxiliary Diagnosis Task Using Ultrasonography Images.
abstract: Ultrasonography (USG) is the primary image modality for diagnosing pediatric intussusception, yet automated identification remains challenging due to severe bowel gas artifacts, acoustic reverberation, and edematous boundary blurring. Moreover, diagnostic uncertainty is exacerbated by the scarcity of large-scale clinical cohorts and ubiquitous acoustic speckle that frequently obscures critical pathognomonic landmarks. To address this gap, we propose Pediatric Intussusception Network (PINet) via a dual-scale guided attention to feature fusion trained on a large real-world pediatric intussusception dataset (RPID), which is used to predict anomalous classifications and improve lesion area learning. PINet integrates three complementary modules: (1) a position-attention module (PAM) to model concentric topological priors and suppress isolated gas artifacts; (2) a dual attention feature fusion (DAF) module combining strip pooling attention with dynamic alignment for multi-scale context aggregation; and (3) an informative context enhancement (ICE) module for low-contrast boundary refinement. It was trained on a largest reported dataset using 9871 USG images from 4026 patients. The result of PINet achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance with 87.44% balanced accuracy and 98.09% area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). The clinical utility of the proposed PINet is demonstrated through robust performance across lesion sizes, accurate localization despite anatomical noise, and effective boundary delineation in low-contrast regions.

title: ConvFormer3D: A Hybrid 3D-CNN-Transformer Front-End for Cine cMRI View Classification Pipelines.
abstract: It is vital to reliably identify the views of standard cine cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (cine cMRI), since each determines which cardiac anatomy will be observed and undergo quantitative analysis. If the view is incorrectly identified, whether by a human observer or by an automated system, errors can propagate into subsequent analyses that give rise to the volumetric assessment, strain analysis, evaluation of the valves, and thus diagnostics. Accurate classification remains a challenge due to clinical variation between scanner manufacturers, differences in acquisition protocols, and motion artifacts. This study presents ConvFormer3D, a hybrid spatiotemporal architecture that includes a Kinetics-400-pretrained 3D residual encoder (R3D-18), modified to handle single-channel cine input, combined with a lightweight temporal transformer and attention-based token pooling. The convolutional stages supply local anatomical and motion priors, while the temporal transformer captures time dependencies throughout the cardiac cycle at full temporal resolution. The network is trained using deep auxiliary supervision, label smoothing, an exponential moving average of the parameters, and mixed-precision optimization. The model's predicted probabilities are then calibrated by temperature scaling. To prevent data leakage, the different partitions are created at the level of the individual patient, and all reported metrics are recorded at patient-clustered bootstraps at the 95% confidence interval, together with formal paired significance testing between the various models. On a separate patient-level test partition, ConvFormer3D achieved an accuracy of 0.983 and an expected calibration error of 0.003 after temperature scaling.

title: PanPrompt3D: A Prompt-Guided SAM-Based Framework for 3D Pancreatic Segmentation Across Multi-Sequence MRI.
abstract: Accurate three-dimensional pancreatic segmentation is important for pancreatic assessment, treatment planning, and quantitative follow-up. However, most existing segmentation methods have been developed primarily for computed tomography, and their performance across clinically used magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) sequences remains less well characterized. We propose PanPrompt3D, a prompt-guided 3D segmentation framework adapted from SAM-Med3D for pancreatic MRI. PanPrompt3D combines a hybrid Transformer-CNN encoder, 3D triplet attention, volumetric prompt encoding, a 3D mask decoder, and a volume-aware hybrid loss incorporating explicit volumetric consistency. The model was evaluated on public T1-weighted (T1W) and T2-weighted (T2W) MRI data and an in-house cohort of 285 water-sequence examinations. With five-point prompts, PanPrompt3D achieved Dice scores of 81.66%, 85.03%, and 85.07% on water-sequence, T1W, and T2W MRI, respectively. Compared with SAM-Med3D under the same prompting protocol, paired Dice improvements were 4.70, 5.80, and 4.99 percentage points, respectively, with all three comparisons remaining statistically significant after Holm correction. PanPrompt3D also achieved R 2 values above 0.9 between predicted and reference pancreatic volumes. Leave-one-sequence-out experiments showed reduced performance on unseen sequences, while external validation on CrossPan and AMOS demonstrated transfer to independent public MRI data, with a clear performance decrease on the unseen out-of-phase contrast. These findings support PanPrompt3D as a practical prompt-guided framework for multi-sequence pancreatic MRI segmentation while highlighting the remaining challenge of generalization to unseen contrasts.

title: VCon-Net: A Cerebral Artery Segmentation Network with Enhanced Topological Connectivity.
abstract: Precise segmentation of cerebral artery from computed tomography angiography serves as a fundamental prerequisite for the clinical evaluation and morphological analysis of cerebrovascular diseases, particularly stroke. However, oversegmentation and undersegmentation routinely compromise topological connectivity and accuracy. This study aims to develop a novel deep learning network to mitigate these challenges, enhancing topological connectivity and accuracy. To enforce topological connectivity, we propose a novel skeleton points distance loss that combines skeleton points with a 3D Euclidean distance field to penalize oversegmentation and undersegmentation via interskeleton point distance constraints. Built upon the U-Net architecture, VCon-Net integrates an axialdynamic convolution module and a multiattention mechanism to enhance the perception of slender arteries and capture spatial-channel-temporal features. A total of 202 cases were included in this study, with 141 cases utilized for model development, 35 for independent testing and performance evaluation, and the remaining 26 analyzed as special clinical cases. On the independent test set, VCon-Net achieved a Dice of 0.8552, a Jaccard of 0.7513, a precision of 0.8568, a sensitivity of 0.8645, with HD 95 reduced to 3.16 mm, and β 0 error reduced to 2.85. Compared with existing segmentation methods, the proposed framework yields favorable performance. VCon-Net achieves cerebral artery segmentation with enhanced topological connectivity, providing a reliable morphological foundation, which offers an essential morphology basis for downstream clinical evaluations.

title: Assessment of Vestibular Schwannoma Growth After Radiosurgery: Variability in Clinical Decision Thresholds and the Role of Artificial Intelligence.
abstract: Purpose To quantify expert interobserver variability in longitudinal vestibular schwannoma growth assessment after radiosurgery and evaluate AI segmentation performance relative to human variability. Materials and methods Retrospective review of patients with sporadic unilateral VS treated with stereotactic radiosurgery (2001-2023). Manual and AI segmentations were compared across the cohort. A growth-enriched subset of 24 tumors underwent additional expert assessment. Agreement was evaluated using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), Fleiss and Cohen κ, Bland-Altman analysis, and Dice similarity coefficients. Results The cohort included 170 MRI examinations from 85 patients (45.9% female; median age, 66 years; median follow-up, 53 months). Human interobserver agreement was excellent for baseline volume (ICC, 0.95), follow-up volume (ICC, 0.98), and percent volume change (ICC, 0.89), but decreased for ≥ 20% growth classification (Fleiss κ, 0.52). Eleven of 24 tumors met the strict-majority growth definition. AI-expert agreement was excellent for baseline and follow-up volumes (ICC, 0.99 and 0.97), but lower for percent change (ICC, 0.83). AI achieved 83.5% binary agreement (Cohen κ, 0.47) and median Dice coefficient of 0.85 (IQR, 0.77-0.90). Bland-Altman analysis demonstrated a mean bias of + 6.64 percentage points (95% limits of agreement, - 53.33 to 66.60). Conclusions AI-human agreement for absolute tumor volumes was comparable to human interobserver agreement. However, longitudinal growth assessment and binary classification demonstrated greater variability, emphasizing the importance of benchmarking AI performance against human variability when applying clinically relevant growth thresholds.
originalAbstract:
Purpose

To quantify expert interobserver variability in longitudinal vestibular schwannoma growth assessment after radiosurgery and evaluate AI segmentation performance relative to human variability.

Materials and methods

Retrospective review of patients with sporadic unilateral VS treated with stereotactic radiosurgery (2001-2023). Manual and AI segmentations were compared across the cohort. A growth-enriched subset of 24 tumors underwent additional expert assessment. Agreement was evaluated using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), Fleiss and Cohen κ, Bland-Altman analysis, and Dice similarity coefficients.

Results

The cohort included 170 MRI examinations from 85 patients (45.9% female; median age, 66 years; median follow-up, 53 months). Human interobserver agreement was excellent for baseline volume (ICC, 0.95), follow-up volume (ICC, 0.98), and percent volume change (ICC, 0.89), but decreased for ≥ 20% growth classification (Fleiss κ, 0.52). Eleven of 24 tumors met the strict-majority growth definition. AI-expert agreement was excellent for baseline and follow-up volumes (ICC, 0.99 and 0.97), but lower for percent change (ICC, 0.83). AI achieved 83.5% binary agreement (Cohen κ, 0.47) and median Dice coefficient of 0.85 (IQR, 0.77-0.90). Bland-Altman analysis demonstrated a mean bias of + 6.64 percentage points (95% limits of agreement, - 53.33 to 66.60).

Conclusions

AI-human agreement for absolute tumor volumes was comparable to human interobserver agreement. However, longitudinal growth assessment and binary classification demonstrated greater variability, emphasizing the importance of benchmarking AI performance against human variability when applying clinically relevant growth thresholds.

title: A Fixed Budget Value Analysis of Few-Shot Medical Vision-Language Model Adaptation.
abstract: Selecting between visual-only and language-informed adaptation is a moving target imaging informatics decision. The same scarce target labels train both the candidate strategies and provide evidence for choosing between them. We introduce a fixed budget, policy value framework for evaluating whether this choice is worthwhile. Four medical vision-language models (BiomedCLIP, PubMedCLIP, MedCLIP, and MedSigLIP) were evaluated across chest radiography and seven MedMNIST tasks at 1-16 shots per class, with external multilabel validation on NIH ChestX-ray14. We compared visual and language-anchored probes and evaluated label-free, support-informed, cross-validated, and held-out meta-selection rules. Policy value was defined as the macro-AUROC gain over always using the visual probe at the same annotation cost. At one shot, language anchoring was superior in 31% of encoder-task combinations, yielding an optimistic oracle opportunity of at most 0.026 macro-AUROC. No deployable selector demonstrated a practically meaningful positive held-out value. Selector value was non-positive at one shot and at most + 0.002 at four shots, with aggregate hierarchical confidence intervals including zero, with the external test demonstrating the same pattern. Harmful language choices were more frequent and larger than beneficial choices, so selection accuracy did not translate into policy value. Controlled class description interventions changed the sign and magnitude of the language effect, demonstrating a genuine yet encoder- and task-dependent opportunity. Under the evaluated fixed budgets, direct visual adaptation was the most dependable use of target labels. Imaging informatics evaluations should report policy value, negative transfer severity, and annotation cost, rather than only selection accuracy.

title: Reducing Demographic Bias in Medical Imaging Using Siamese Representation Learning.
abstract: Deep learning models for medical imaging often exhibit demographic bias, leading to performance disparities across protected groups such as age, gender, and race. This study proposes a debiasing framework to reduce such disparities while maintaining diagnostic accuracy. We propose a Siamese neural network trained using triplet loss, where demographic attributes are incorporated into triplet selection to encourage separation by disease class while promoting within-class similarity across demographic groups. The method was evaluated on pleural effusion detection using chest X-rays (109,005 images from 41,063 patients) and Alzheimer's disease classification using brain MRI (1494 scans from 348 patients). Performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), precision, and true positive rate, along with equalized odds difference. The proposed method significantly reduced demographic disparities while maintaining or improving overall predictive performance compared with baseline and existing debiasing approaches. In pleural effusion detection, true positive rate gaps were reduced by 32% (race), 8% (age), and 22% (gender). In Alzheimer's disease classification, the true positive rate gap was reduced by 41% (age). Model interpretation indicated clinically meaningful imaging features were used for decision-making. Demographic-aware triplet sampling within a Siamese framework can effectively mitigate demographic performance disparities in medical imaging models while maintaining competitive overall diagnostic performance, suggesting potential for more equitable and clinically reliable deployment of medical imaging AI systems.

title: GC-ResNet: Interference-Resistant Fine-Grained Classification and Robustness Analysis of Highly Similar Anatomical Structures in Nasal Endoscopy.
abstract: Accurate recognition of anatomical structures in nasal endoscopic images is challenging because of high inter-class morphological similarity and common imaging interference, including specular reflections, bubbles, blur, and abnormal exposure. To address these issues, we present GC-ResNet, an improved ResNet-34 framework for fine-grained nasal endoscopic image classification. GC-ResNet integrates squeeze-and-excitation (SE) modules into residual blocks to adaptively recalibrate channel responses and introduces a bottleneck-style global feature refinement module after the final residual stage to refine high-level contextual representations. Experiments on 6706 unique nasal endoscopic images from eight view categories use a fixed image-level split with separate training, validation, and test sets. Across five training seeds, GC-ResNet achieves a test accuracy of 95.58% ± 0.40% and a weighted F1-score of 95.59% ± 0.39% (mean ± standard deviation), maintaining competitive clean-image performance among the compared models. Stress tests suggest improved accuracy retention relative to ResNet-34 under selected synthetic specular-reflection and bubble-interference conditions, with unadjusted paired 95% confidence intervals for the accuracy differences excluding zero. These results support the potential of GC-ResNet for robust fine-grained recognition in nasal endoscopic images.

title: Prediction of Postoperative Neurological Function Recovery in Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy Using MRI-based Delta-Radiomics Combined with Interpretable Machine Learning Model.
abstract: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy (CSM) presents progressive neurological deterioration and highly variable postoperative outcomes, while existing prognostic assessment methods have inherent limitations. This dual-center study developed an interpretable MRI-based delta-radiomics model for individualized CSM postoperative prognosis evaluation. A total of 237 CSM patients from Center 1 and 96 patients from Center 2 who underwent decompression surgery were retrospectively enrolled. The Center 1 cohort was stratified by clinical outcomes and randomly divided into training (n = 165) and internal testing (n = 72) cohorts at a 7:3 ratio, while the Center 2 cohort served as an independent external validation set (n = 96). Radiomic features were extracted from pre- and postoperative T2WI MRI images, and delta-radiomic features were calculated. LASSO regression and spearman correlation analysis were applied to screen core radiomic features, and clinical-routine imaging features. Three prediction models were constructed via five machine learning algorithms. Model performance was evaluated using AUC, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and F1-score, and pairwise comparisons performed via the DeLong and McNemar tests. Calibration curves and radar charts were generated to determine the optimal algorithm for each model. Decision Curve Analysis (DCA) and Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) analysis were performed to assess clinical benefit and model interpretability. Baseline data were well balanced. 16 preoperative radiomic features, 15 delta-radiomic features, and 5 clinical-routine imaging features were finally selected. The XGBoost-based delta-radiomic model achieved the highest numerical AUCs in the internal test (0.899) and external validation (0.802) sets, demonstrating a statistically significant improvement in AUC compared to both the preoperative radiomic model and the clinical-routine imaging model. The model maintained a balanced performance profile across cohorts. This model maintained a higher clinical net benefit across wide threshold ranges. SHAP analysis identified wavelet-domain texture features as risk factors for poor prognosis, while gradient-domain kurtosis features showed bidirectional regulatory effects. Overall, the MRI-based delta-radiomic model effectively predicts long-term neurological recovery in CSM patients. The delta-radiomic model exhibits a more balanced performance profile and statistically better generalizability. By utilizing routine short-term postoperative MRI (within 7 days), this interpretable model holds promise as an objective tool for early prediction of 12-month postoperative neurological recovery.
originalAbstract: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy (CSM) presents progressive neurological deterioration and highly variable postoperative outcomes, while existing prognostic assessment methods have inherent limitations. This dual-center study developed an interpretable MRI-based delta-radiomics model for individualized CSM postoperative prognosis evaluation. A total of 237 CSM patients from Center 1 and 96 patients from Center 2 who underwent decompression surgery were retrospectively enrolled. The Center 1 cohort was stratified by clinical outcomes and randomly divided into training (n = 165) and internal testing (n = 72) cohorts at a 7:3 ratio, while the Center 2 cohort served as an independent external validation set (n = 96). Radiomic features were extracted from pre- and postoperative T2WI MRI images, and delta-radiomic features were calculated. LASSO regression and spearman correlation analysis were applied to screen core radiomic features, and clinical-routine imaging features. Three prediction models were constructed via five machine learning algorithms. Model performance was evaluated using AUC, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and F1-score, and pairwise comparisons performed via the DeLong and McNemar tests. Calibration curves and radar charts were generated to determine the optimal algorithm for each model. Decision Curve Analysis (DCA) and Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) analysis were performed to assess clinical benefit and model interpretability. Baseline data were well balanced. 16 preoperative radiomic features, 15 delta-radiomic features, and 5 clinical-routine imaging features were finally selected. The XGBoost-based delta-radiomic model achieved the highest numerical AUCs in the internal test (0.899) and external validation (0.802) sets, demonstrating a statistically significant improvement in AUC compared to both the preoperative radiomic model and the clinical-routine imaging model. The model maintained a balanced performance profile across cohorts. This model maintained a higher clinical net benefit across wide threshold ranges. SHAP analysis identified wavelet-domain texture features as risk factors for poor prognosis, while gradient-domain kurtosis features showed bidirectional regulatory effects. Overall, the MRI-based delta-radiomic model effectively predicts long-term neurological recovery in CSM patients. The delta-radiomic model exhibits a more balanced performance profile and statistically better generalizability. By utilizing routine short-term postoperative MRI (within 7 days), this interpretable model holds promise as an objective tool for early prediction of 12-month postoperative neurological recovery.

title: Cross-View Constrained Encoder and Cross-Modal Semantic-Hierarchy Fusion Network for Congenital Heart Disease Identification.
abstract: Congenital heart disease (CHD) is a common structural birth defect, and early screening is important for improving prognosis. Clinical cardiac ultrasound combines brightness-mode (B-mode) and color Doppler images from multiple standard views to assess cardiac morphology and hemodynamic abnormalities. Existing case-level models remain limited in modeling information exchange among standard views within each modality and cross-modal fusion between B-mode morphology and Doppler hemodynamics. The proposed Cross-View Constrained Encoder and Cross-Modal Semantic-Hierarchy Fusion Network (CVCE-CMSHFNet) addresses these limitations through two complementary components: a Multi-View Constrained Encoder (MVCE) and a Bidirectional Progressive Semantic-Hierarchy Fusion (BiPSHF) module. MVCE models relationships among the eight standard views within each modality. Sinkhorn-constrained transport and a parallel gated transformation update the view representations. Training-time Intra-Modal View Covariance Diversity Regularization (IVCDR) separately penalizes covariance similarity among B-mode view representations and among Doppler view representations. BiPSHF performs bidirectional cross-modal interaction at the view, view-group, and case levels. The view-group level organizes the eight standard views into four study-specific groups based on anatomical relationships and clinical assessment roles. CVCE-CMSHFNet aims to support clinical diagnosis by providing a case-level CHD probability for physician reference. Evaluation included 384 complete eight-view dual-modality cases from a 506-subject single-center echocardiography database. CVCE-CMSHFNet achieved 95.64% accuracy, 95.23% F1 score, 97.05% AUC, 94.44% sensitivity, and 96.67% specificity.

title: Physics-Informed Implicit Neural Networks for 3D Coronary Artery Reconstruction.
abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction of coronary artery geometry from computed tomography angiography (CCTA)-derived segmentations is challenging because of thin vessel walls, tortuous trajectories, and small distal structures. We propose a physics-informed implicit neural network (PIINN) for case-specific reconstruction of paired coronary surfaces from pre-segmented CCTA-derived lumen and outer-wall geometries. For each coronary segment, a single network is optimized independently to represent the luminal and outer vessel-wall surfaces using dual signed distance fields (SDFs). The objective combines supervised SDF regression and boundary anchoring with Eikonal regularization and geometry- and anatomy-informed soft constraints on surface ordering, enclosure consistency, and local wall separation. A three-stage curriculum progressively adjusts the spatial sampling, learning rate, and constraint weights. The framework was evaluated on 15 coronary artery segments. The PIINN (256 × 6) achieved a near-surface RMSE of 0.26 mm and a sign accuracy approaching 90% for the outer SDF. Mesh reconstruction achieved an inner-surface ASSD of 0.166 mm and an HD95 of 0.455 mm, compared with the ASSD values of 0.290 mm for Vanilla INR and 1.057 mm for DeepSDF, with statistically significant improvements across the evaluated cases (p ≤ 0.003). Component-wise ablation further demonstrated distinct contributions from Eikonal regularization, anatomical constraints, region-based sampling, and curriculum optimization. These results support PIINN as a constrained continuous representation for case-specific coronary reconstruction from CCTA-derived segmentations; direct reconstruction from raw CCTA and generalization to unseen patients were not evaluated.

title: Language-Guided Visual Feature Reconstruction: A Parameter-Efficient Tuning Strategy for Medical Vision-Language Models.
abstract: Medical vision-language foundation models such as BiomedCLIP offer a promising basis for medical image classification, retrieval, and computer-aided diagnosis. However, local adaptation in healthcare institutions is constrained by data governance requirements, limited computational resources, and the need for maintainable model updates. Full fine-tuning is resource-intensive, whereas conventional parameter-efficient methods may not sufficiently preserve semantic consistency between image features and diagnostic concepts. We propose multimodal semantic reconstruction (MSR), a lightweight adaptation framework for BiomedCLIP with frozen image and text encoders. MSR uses learnable text context vectors, a language-guided visual prompt coupling matrix, weighted multi-level visual feature aggregation, and a learnable contrastive temperature to align visual representations with text-based class prototypes. Its training objective integrates cross-entropy classification with mean squared error and in-batch contrastive alignment losses. We evaluated MSR and six parameter-efficient baselines on ten public medical image classification datasets spanning multiple modalities using three random seeds, with zero-shot BiomedCLIP as an additional reference. Using the full training splits, MSR achieved the highest mean accuracy (89.42%) and macro F1 (87.53%) across the ten datasets among the evaluated methods, with 49,177 trainable parameters. In the few-shot evaluation, MSR did not consistently outperform the compared methods, particularly VPT. Category-level analyses and qualitative visualizations characterized model behavior and residual errors among visually similar classes. These findings suggest that language-guided visual feature reconstruction may provide a technical basis for lightweight, locally maintainable adaptation of medical vision-language models.

title: A Deep Learning Framework for Retrospective Motion Detection and Conditional Correction (MDCC): Application to Multi-Gradient-Recalled Echo Quantitative MRI.
abstract: Multi-echo gradient-recalled-echo (mGRE) MRI supports quantitative neuroimaging by enabling voxel-wise T2*/R2*/R2t* mapping for quantitative assessment of tissue damage and magnetic susceptibility imaging. Subject motion degrades these acquisitions by introducing inconsistencies due to phase-encoding steps collected at different head positions. Although the gradient echoes associated with a given phase-encoding line are acquired at practically the same head position, differences in contrast, signal-to-noise ratio, and B0 field-dependent phase evolution cause the resulting artifacts to appear differently across echoes and can bias downstream parametric maps. Existing learning-based retrospective correction approaches often discard complex phase information, treat multiple gradient-recalled echoes independently, and apply correction indiscriminately to both motion-corrupted and clean data. We propose Motion Detection and Conditional Correction (MDCC), a retrospective image-domain pipeline that couples a complex-input volume-level Multi-Echo Motion Detection (ME-MoD) model and a complex-valued Multi-Echo Motion Corrector (ME-MoC) in an iterative detect-correct-re-evaluate loop, where correction is invoked only on volumes flagged as motion corrupted. ME-MoD reweights each echo with a phase-preserving paired complex gate, followed by a shared residual slice encoder, and a selected volume-level aggregator. ME-MoC is a fully complex-valued, factorized U-Net with echo-axis multi-head self-attention at the bottleneck, trained with a T2*-consistency physics loss. ME-MoD attained an AUC of 0.95 and sensitivity of 0.91 on the held-out detection set. At the cohort-level analysis, ME-MoC improved downstream R2* fitting results relative to the motion-corrupted input and 2D U-Net and achieved the lowest numerical R2* root-mean-square error (RMSE) among the evaluated methods, including modest numerical improvement over baseline.

title: Mandibular Bone Microarchitecture and Cortical Characteristics in Amelogenesis Imperfecta: A Fractal Analysis and Multi-Index Radiomorphometric Study.
abstract: Amelogenesis imperfecta (AI) is a hereditary enamel disorder that can present with altered dental morphology, while its relationship with mandibular bone structure remains unclear. This retrospective cross-sectional study aimed to evaluate mandibular trabecular pattern and cortical bone morphology in individuals with AI using fractal analysis and radiomorphometric indices on panoramic radiographs. The study included 48 patients with AI and 48 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. Fractal dimension (FD) analysis was performed in five mandibular regions. Cortical bone morphology was assessed using the mental index, gonial index, antegonial index, and panoramic mandibular index (PMI), as well as the Klemetti index. Statistical analyses included independent-samples t-tests, mixed-design ANOVA, chi-square tests, and McNemar tests (p < 0.05). FD values in all evaluated regions were significantly lower in the AI group than in the control group (p < 0.05); the mean symphyseal FD value was 1.29 ± 0.07 in the AI group and 1.37 ± 0.06 in the control group (p < 0.001). The mental index, PMI, gonial index, and antegonial index were also significantly lower in the AI group (p < 0.05). For the gonial index, the right-side values were 0.60 ± 0.25 in the AI group and 0.86 ± 0.30 in the control group, whereas the left-side values were 0.65 ± 0.29 and 0.80 ± 0.28, respectively. After Holm adjustment, no significant right-left differences were observed for any quantitative cortical index, and the side × group interaction for the gonial index did not remain significant (adjusted p = 0.054). Klemetti index distributions differed significantly between the groups (p < 0.05). The Klemetti classification showed a discordant pattern, with C2 cortices less frequent in the AI group than in controls despite lower quantitative cortical indices; group differences persisted after adjustment for age, dentition stage, and scanner type. After Holm adjustment across indices, group differences were retained for all four quantitative cortical indices. Individuals with AI showed differences in both trabecular and cortical mandibular bone parameters compared with healthy controls. These findings establish radiographic group differences but do not determine their underlying functional or genetic mechanisms. Panoramic radiographs may provide useful supplementary information for evaluating mandibular bone structure in patients with AI.

title: Eye-Tracking-Guided Tri-View Learning for Fine-Grained Medical Image Classification and Segmentation.
abstract: Fine-grained medical image analysis involves two core tasks: image-level disease classification and pixel-level border delineation, both requiring intelligent models to capture subtle lesion-relevant visual cues. We investigate a shared gaze-guided multi-view design principle through separate task-specific classification and segmentation models. For classification, gaze heatmaps are used to derive point prompts and construct global, lesion-core, and peri-lesional views, enabling the model to integrate whole-image context, lesion-dominant details, and surrounding tissue information. In addition, a dual-path diagnosis module is designed to combine direct prediction of disease classes with hierarchical lesion-dominant subtype refinement. For segmentation, we introduce Tri-view Gaze-prior Input (TVGP-Input), a plug-and-play input-level module that introduces eye-tracking-derived spatial priors to segmentation backbones without modifying their encoder-decoder structures. Experimental results show that the proposed framework achieves an accuracy of 0.8680±0.0236 , a macro-F1 score of 0.7255±0.0425 , a weighted F1 score of 0.8531±0.0195 , and macro- and micro-averaged areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.8968±0.0358 and 0.9668±0.0199 in five-fold cross-validation on three-class medical image classification. In segmentation experiments, the proposed TVGP-Input enhanced tri-view segmentation model achieves a Dice score of 0.9285±0.0109 and an intersection over union of 0.8694±0.0144 . These results support gaze-guided learning within the evaluated breast ultrasound classification and prostate magnetic resonance imaging segmentation settings.

title: Prospective Validation of a Doppler-Enhanced Multimodal Ultrasound-Clinical Model for Predicting Clinical Pregnancy After IVF/ICSI Single Embryo Transfer.
abstract: We developed and temporally validated a Doppler-enhanced multimodal ultrasound-clinical model for predicting clinical pregnancy after single morphologically high-quality embryo transfer. This single-center study included 795 participants undergoing autologous in vitro fertilization or intracytoplasmic sperm injection. The retrospective development cohort included 534 participants (427 for training and 107 for internal testing), and 261 participants with prospectively collected data formed the temporal validation cohort. B-mode and Doppler videos acquired 1 day before transfer underwent automated endometrial segmentation and feature extraction. A four-branch gated-attention network combined feature- and branch-level gating with self-attention to integrate imaging features, short-sequence descriptors, clinical variables, and embryo developmental stage. The locked model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.829 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.728-0.918) in internal testing. In temporal validation, the AUC was 0.771 (95% CI, 0.661-0.874), with an accuracy of 0.747, sensitivity of 0.780, and specificity of 0.703. The Brier score was 0.187 and the calibration slope was 0.947. Modality and architectural ablation analyses showed numerically higher AUCs and accuracies for the complete model in both cohorts, with statistically significant AUC differences in selected comparisons. Decision curve analysis suggested potential net benefit over part of the evaluated threshold range. These findings suggest the potential of the Doppler-enhanced multimodal model for individualized prediction of clinical pregnancy after embryo transfer.

title: On-Premises Open-Weight Large Language Models for Classifying Epilepsy Brain MRI Reports: A Retrospective Study.
abstract: Free-text reports limit the use of imaging data for research cohort screening. This study evaluated whether locally deployed open-weight large language models (LLMs) can classify brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) reports in epilepsy without external data transfer, and which forms of domain knowledge improve classification. In this single-center retrospective study, 1210 epilepsy-protocol brain MRI reports were labeled by a board-certified neuroradiologist for abnormality status and primary imaging finding (eight classes). A held-out test set of 206 reports was classified by a biomedical (OpenBioLLM-8B) and a general-purpose (Qwen3.5-9B) LLM on a single 24-GB graphics processing unit, with and without a rule set and example retrieval, and compared with a fine-tuned radiology-specific BERT model, an independent neuroradiology fellow, and a same-base control model. The primary outcome was the macro-averaged F1 score for the primary finding. Without task-specific training, the general-purpose model achieved a finding macro-F1 of 0.63 (95% confidence interval (CI), 0.53-0.70), comparable to the fine-tuned BERT model (0.59; difference, - 0.04; 95% CI, - 0.13 to 0.07) and to inter-reader agreement (0.61; κ = 0.59). A rule set stating institutional category definitions improved the biomedical model (difference, 0.23; 95% CI, 0.11-0.33) without significantly reducing performance in any model, whereas biomedical fine-tuning conferred no advantage over the control model and example retrieval did not help. Residual errors concentrated where the readers disagreed. Locally deployed LLMs performed comparably to inter-reader agreement, which may support human-verified cohort screening; in this institution-specific task, explicit category definitions were more useful than biomedical specialization.

title: Harmonizing Fidelity, Utility, and Privacy in Medical Data Synthesis: A Dual Approach via Survival-Aware CVAE and XAI-Guided DDPM.
abstract: Strict data privacy regulations severely constrain the sharing and secondary use of clinical datasets in biomedical research. Generative artificial intelligence offers a viable solution by synthesizing realistic medical data devoid of original patient identifiers and augmenting existing cohorts. This study introduces two distinct modality-specific generative pipelines tailored for medical tabular synthesis and class-aware medical image generation that share a common design principle-the clinically decisive variable (event status or diagnostic class) is an explicit, controlled condition of the generator-and are assessed with a common fidelity-utility-privacy protocol. For tabular synthesis, a Conditional Variational Autoencoder (CVAE) was trained and benchmarked on the METABRIC, GBSG2, and WHAS500 datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that the conditional architecture effectively mitigates the event-collapse phenomenon prevalent in conventional VAE frameworks. For class-conditional medical image synthesis, an explainable AI (XAI)-guided Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model (DDPM) was developed and trained on chest X-ray and CT modalities using a stepwise strategy incorporating low-frequency, edge, and density-based anatomical regularizers. The stepwise XAI guidance coupled with anatomy-preserving constraints increased independent class consistency, whereas its effect on downstream classification was modality-dependent. Across five random seeds and six dataset-regime conditions, the CVAE achieved a mean SDV-style quality score of 0.931 ± 0.001 and a Train on Synthetic, Test on Real (TSTR) C-index of 0.739 ± 0.004, with no exact record matches and a mean distance-based membership-inference AUC of 0.555 ± 0.009, i.e., modestly above the 0.5 chance level. Across three seeds, the XAI-guided DDPM reached 98.1 ± 0.1% independent class consistency on chest X-ray and 86.1 ± 2.9% on COVID-CT; however, on COVID-CT its TSTR F1-score (0.639 ± 0.019) was lower than that of the unguided DDPM baseline (0.776 ± 0.017), indicating that the benefit of XAI guidance is contingent upon imaging modality and sample size. Rather than claiming universal superiority, the study contributes explicit event control with a characterized fidelity-privacy trade-off for survival tables and a systematic component analysis of when XAI guidance helps and when it harms image synthesis.

title: Image-Level Splitting Inflates Apparent Performance Through Repeated Patient-Level Variables in Breast Ultrasound AI: A Patient-Grouped Study of Intraductal Papilloma.
abstract: To quantify how image-level rather than patient-level fold assignment inflates the apparent performance of breast ultrasound models, using a clinical task without demonstrable discrimination as a negative control. This retrospective single-centre study included 250 women with intraductal papilloma (IDP; 553 B-mode images; 184 colour Doppler images in 144 patients), 47 (18.8%) with associated atypical ductal hyperplasia (ADH) or ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS). Radiomics, clinical-variable, and deep-learning models were evaluated with patient-grouped nested fivefold cross-validation, permutation nulls, and repeated partitions. The same models were then evaluated under image-level fold assignment, and the source of inflation was examined with matching, perturbation, and synthetic-variable controls. Discrimination above chance was not demonstrated: patient-level AUCs were 0.490-0.563, every 95% confidence interval included 0.5, and no upper limit reached 0.70. Changing only fold assignment increased the radiomics-plus-clinical AUC from 0.506 to 0.788 (ΔAUC 0.282; patient-clustered 95% CI 0.209-0.351), and averaging predictions per patient did not remove the inflation (0.504 versus 0.800). Across 20 partitions, mean inflation was 0.363 for age plus lesion size, 0.226 for radiomics, and 0.109 for a B-mode network trained to fit its training data. Random variables held constant within each patient produced similar inflation (0.415), whereas variables varying across images produced none. In a cohort without demonstrable discrimination under patient-grouped validation, image-level fold assignment generated substantial apparent performance. Patient-constant variables acted as identifiers, and patient-level aggregation did not correct the leakage.

title: LIVSEG: A Cloud-GPU Web Application for Automated Future Liver Remnant Estimation.
abstract: Accurate estimation of the future liver remnant (FLR) is essential for planning hepatectomy and portal vein embolization (PVE), yet conventional calculation relies on manual segmentation that is time-intensive and dependent on specialized workstations. Thus, LIVSEG was developed as a single-page web application that streams DICOM or NIfTI imaging to a cloud GPU running TotalSegmentator nnU-Net models for automated Couinaud-segment and hepatic-lesion segmentation, with an integrated editor for human review. In a cohort of 60 patients (38 living liver donors, 22 PVE patients; 82 scans), the absolute difference between automated and manual FLR was 3.24 ± 2.69 percentage points (pp) in donors and 4.49 ± 5.14 pp across PVE scans, and the two methods were statistically equivalent within a ± 5 pp margin in all cohorts. Using institutional FLR thresholds, LIVSEG and manual volumetry yielded concordant classifications in 79 of 82 scans (96.3%). Inference was completed in two minutes per case at a GPU cost of $0.014-0.026 per study. LIVSEG allows models to reach clinical workflows while retaining human oversight.

title: Radiomics-Based Differentiation of Enchondroma from Atypical Cartilaginous Tumour and Chondrosarcoma: A Systematic Review and Appraisal.
abstract: The objective was to systematically review radiomics models that differentiate enchondroma from atypical cartilaginous tumour (ACT) or chondrosarcoma and to appraise their methodological quality and readiness for clinical use. PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials and Scopus were searched from inception to 24 October 2026 for radiomic, machine learning or deep learning models applied to CT, MRI, radiography or bone SPECT/CT (PROSPERO registration number withheld for blinded review). Performance was synthesised descriptively, not pooled. Quality was appraised with PROBAST + AI, TRIPOD + AI, the Radiomics Quality Score and METRICS. Fourteen reports representing 13 retrospective cohorts (1447 participants, including 79 control scans) were included; two probably overlapping reports were counted once. Eight cohorts used MRI, three CT, one both and one bone SPECT/CT; three reports evaluated deep learning. Eight reports supplied an exact or derivable 2 × 2 table for one of two clinical targets. Sensitivity ranged from 0.800 to 0.935 and specificity from 0.727 to 1.000; preferred areas under the curve (AUC) ranged from 0.801 to 1.000. Development quality concern was high in all reports, and all 22 diagnostic evaluation datasets had high risk of bias. One study used geographically external validation; none was prospective or reported decision curve analysis. Median complete TRIPOD + AI reporting was 48.3%. Reported discrimination was promising but methodologically preliminary and does not establish clinical usefulness; prospective assessment and independent multicentre external validation are required.

title: A Deep Learning Framework Integrating Multi-Region Radiomics and Clinical Features for Improved Breast Ultrasound Lesion Classification.
abstract: Breast cancer poses a substantial global burden on women's health, making accurate early differentiation of benign and malignant breast lesions essential for improving prognosis and reducing healthcare costs. Although deep learning methods have been widely developed for breast ultrasound lesion classification, most rely on imaging information alone. Existing approaches incorporating peritumoral information often use empirically defined regions, while clinical characteristics are rarely integrated into end-to-end frameworks, limiting the use of complementary diagnostic information. To address these limitations, we propose Multi-Source Information Fusion DenseNet (MSIF-DenseNet), an end-to-end framework for breast ultrasound lesion classification. It jointly integrates intratumoral ultrasound images, peritumoral regions, and structured clinical information. Specifically, a dual-stream convolutional architecture with separable convolutions independently learns representative features from the intratumoral and peritumoral regions, while a multi-layer perceptron branch encodes patient clinical characteristics. The resulting imaging and clinical features are subsequently fused through a Compact Bilinear Pooling (CBP) module to capture high-order interactions among heterogeneous information sources for benign-malignant classification. On a private dataset comprising 500 breast ultrasound images from 500 patients, MSIF-DenseNet achieved an AUC of 84.21%±3.52% , F1-score of 83.81%±3.40% , and accuracy of 80.00%±3.90% under five-fold cross-validation. Compared with the imaging-only dual-stream baseline, integrating clinical information increased AUC and F1-score by 4.13 and 2.69 percentage points (pp), respectively, while integration of multi-region information increased AUC and F1-score by 9.86 and 6.09 pp, respectively, over the best single-region model. These results support the effectiveness of combining multi-region ultrasound information with clinical data for breast ultrasound lesion classification.

title: Generative Adversarial Networks in Medical Imaging: A Scoping Review of Applications, Translational Readiness, and Evidence Gaps.
abstract: This scoping review maps the recent applications of generative adversarial network (GAN)-based methods in medical imaging from 2021 to 2025. The aim was to provide an evidence map of recent original studies, focusing on methodological categories, imaging modalities, anatomical targets, application domains, translational-readiness evidence, and trustworthiness gaps. The scoping review was conducted and reported in accordance with the PRISMA extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). PubMed, Scopus, and IEEE Xplore were searched, supplemented by manual screening of reference lists and related articles. Original full-text articles published in English between 2021 and 2025 were eligible if they used adversarially trained GAN-based methods for medical imaging tasks. A total of 112 studies were included after duplicate removal and two-stage screening. GAN-based methods were most often applied to disease diagnosis support, image reconstruction, image quality enhancement, cross-modality translation, anatomical segmentation, and training data expansion. Evidence reporting differed substantially across the five assessed domains. External validation was clearly reported in 17 studies (15.2%), prospective evaluation in 2 (1.8%), and clinical workflow integration in 3 (2.7%). Privacy assessment was not clearly reported in any study, with only one (0.9%) partially addressing this domain. In contrast, hallucination or failure analysis was clearly reported in 32 studies (28.6%) and partially reported in 74 (66.1%). These findings indicate widespread technical experimentation but uneven documentation of evidence relevant to clinical translation. Further external and prospective evaluation, explicit privacy assessment, more comprehensive failure analysis, and clinician-centered workflow studies are needed to support the responsible clinical implementation of GAN-based medical imaging methods.

title: Agreement of CT-Based Renal Volumetry Using Automatic and Semiautomatic Segmentation Tools.
abstract: Renal volume is an important parameter in the follow-up of chronic kidney diseases and surgical planning. Today, software providing three-dimensional (3D) segmentation is widely used in clinical practice. This study aimed to compare the semiautomatic and automatic segmentation methods of 3D Slicer and ITK-SNAP software in terms of renal volume measurements and to evaluate the agreement between these methods. In this retrospective study, abdominal computed tomography (CT) images from 102 individuals were analyzed. Right renal volumes were measured using semiautomatic segmentation with ITK-SNAP and 3D Slicer, and automatic segmentation with TotalSegmentator. Semiautomatic segmentations were performed twice by each of two observers at different times. For Observer 1, a statistically significant difference was observed between the methods in all pairwise comparisons except for the comparison between TotalSegmentator and semiautomatic 3D Slicer segmentation. For Observer 2, statistically significant differences were observed in all pairwise comparisons. Intraobserver and interobserver agreements were high. Regarding segmentation time, statistically significant differences were observed in all pairwise comparisons (p < 0.001), with TotalSegmentator showing significantly shorter segmentation times. This indicates that, although the methods yielded statistically different volume estimates, the measurements showed a consistent pattern across individuals. Overall, the evaluated methods provided consistent renal volume measurements across individuals, although some systematic differences were observed. The findings highlight the importance of considering both agreement and measurement efficiency when selecting a renal volumetry method.

title: AI-Assisted Multimodal Imaging Integration for Individualized Transseptal Puncture Planning During Atrial Fibrillation Ablation.
abstract: Transseptal puncture (TSP) is a critical step during atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation, and accurate anatomical understanding of the interatrial septum is essential for individualized procedural planning. Intracardiac echocardiography (ICE) provides real-time visualization of septal anatomy but is limited by its two-dimensional representation and operator dependence. This study developed an artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted multimodal imaging framework integrating preprocedural computed tomography angiography (CTA) with intraoperative ICE to provide patient-specific three-dimensional (3D) anatomical guidance for TSP planning. This single-center study enrolled 700 patients undergoing AF ablation. An AI framework was developed using data from 500 patients to perform automated segmentation, 3D reconstruction, and CTA-ICE multimodal image integration. The framework was evaluated in an independent temporal validation cohort of 200 patients. The primary outcome was the influence of AI-assisted anatomical information on individualized TSP planning, assessed by changes in puncture strategy following AI-assisted assessment. Secondary outcomes included decision confidence, planning time, interreader agreement, and procedural feasibility. The AI framework achieved an overall Dice similarity coefficient of 0.854 for automated anatomical segmentation and a Dice coefficient of 0.862 for 3D left atrial reconstruction. title: Evaluation Design and Reported Accuracy of Deep Learning Mandibular Canal Segmentation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Reported accuracy of deep learning mandibular canal segmentation varies widely, and studies differ in how it was evaluated. This systematic review estimated accuracy under explicit validity criteria and described how it varied with evaluation design. Five databases were searched to May 2026 (PROSPERO CRD420261403406). Dice similarity coefficients (DSCs) from three-dimensional, patient-level-partitioned cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) or CT test sets were pooled by random-effects meta-analysis on the logit scale. Public benchmark results were analyzed separately, and test sets whose reference was generated by the evaluated model were not pooled. Fifty-four studies were included. Pooled DSC across 15 studies was 0.826 (95% confidence interval 0.752-0.881; 95% prediction interval 0.444-0.966), close to three previous reviews with different inclusion rules (0.80-0.84). The 16 CBCT studies ineligible for pooling, mostly for two-dimensional slice-level segmentation or fewer than 10 test patients, reported a higher median DSC (0.860 versus 0.803). Two systems on the official ToothFairy test set had a pooled DSC of 0.751. Internal and external estimates did not differ significantly (P = .974), but five external studies cannot establish equivalence. Pooled 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance across seven studies was 1.15 mm, with a prediction interval extending to 6.11 mm. Risk of bias was unclear or high in 14 of 15 pooled studies, and certainty of evidence was very low. Average accuracy is consistent across reviews, higher median values came, descriptively, from less constrained evaluations, and external evidence is too limited to show that performance transfers to new settings. Expert verification and prospective external validation remain necessary.

title: Multimodal Integration of Imaging and Pathological Features for Postoperative Outcome Prediction in Liver Cancer.
abstract: This study aimed to construct and externally validate a multimodal radiopathomic fusion model for predicting postoperative recurrence in patients with primary liver cancer (restricted to hepatocellular carcinoma, excluding intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma and mixed-type hepatocellular-cholangiocarcinoma) after curative hepatectomy, and to explore its independent prognostic efficacy and clinical utility. A total of 280 primary liver cancer patients from two centers were retrospectively allocated to a training cohort (n = 182) and an independent validation cohort (n = 98). Radiomic features were extracted from preoperative abdominal MRI, while pathomic features were quantified from H&E-stained whole-slide images. Eight machine learning algorithms were screened via fivefold cross‑validation for unimodal model development. The optimal random forest classifier was applied to construct unimodal radiomic‑only and pathomic‑only models, whereas the final multimodal fusion model was built using logistic regression with concatenated pre‑screened radiomic and pathomic features. ROC, SHAP, Kaplan-Meier survival, and logistic regression analyses were conducted to assess model performance, risk stratification, and independent predictors. Baseline characteristics were comparable between the two cohorts. We extracted 3390 MRI radiomic and 1039 pathomic features and then built single-modal and fusion models. The fusion model outperformed unimodal models (AUC = 0.894 training, 0.858 validation). It stratified patients into low-/high-recurrence risk subgroups (HR = 9.93 and 5.32). Multivariable analysis confirmed Fusion_Risk score (HR = 18.73) as the strongest independent recurrence predictor, superior to routine clinicopathological biomarkers. The radiopathomic fusion model showed good calibration and satisfactory net clinical benefit. Compared with unimodal models, it exhibited a trend toward improved predictive performance, suggesting potential value as an independent prognostic tool for individualized postoperative recurrence surveillance in patients with primary liver cancer after curative resection.

title: DiCoNet: Diagnosis-Conditioned Report Generation for Retinal OCT via Pseudo Semantic Embedding.
abstract: Retinal optical coherence tomography (OCT) report generation faces two major challenges: the scarcity of paired image-report data and the inherent semantic gap between visual representations and clinical concepts. Under such low-resource conditions, conventional vision-driven encoder-decoder models are prone to representation degradation and pathological hallucination, which cause semantic drift and make generated reports deviate from true clinical diagnoses. Inspired by the diagnostic workflow in clinical practice, where diagnosis precedes description, we propose a diagnosis-conditioned network, DiCoNet, which reformulates medical report generation from direct image-text mapping into a diagnosis-conditioned sequence generation task. DiCoNet adopts a two-stage progressive training strategy. It first learns robust and discriminative visual representations from a large-scale diagnostic classification dataset and then performs partial fine-tuning on limited report data. To bridge the gap between visual representations and diagnostic semantics, we design a pseudo semantic embedding (PSE) module that injects continuous diagnostic priors directly into the visual prefix, guiding report generation without increasing the prefix length. We further introduce an auxiliary diagnostic supervision branch to maintain feature discriminability during decoding and enable end-to-end autonomous inference without external labels at test time. Extensive experiments on a real-world clinical OCT dataset show that DiCoNet achieves the best scores among the evaluated methods on most automatic evaluation metrics, with a ROUGE-L score of 0.420 and a CIDEr score of 0.951. Expert evaluation and an OCT-specific clinical error analysis further support the accuracy and completeness of DiCoNet-generated reports, highlighting its potential for assisting OCT report drafting.

title: Unleashing the potential of saturation-transfer MR fingerprinting (ST-MRF) in neuro-oncology: quantitative molecular CEST and MTC mapping.
abstract: Neuro-oncology biomarkers allow probing tissues beyond anatomical or relaxation contrast. However, new techniques are needed to achieve mechanistic elucidation and effective therapeutic interventions. Quantitative MRI techniques, such as T 1 , T 2 , diffusion, and perfusion imaging, provide insights into tumor biology, infiltration, microstructure, and hemodynamics, and have been implemented clinically, but are limited in probing cellular and molecular changes. Saturation transfer (ST) MRI methods, including magnetization transfer contrast (MTC) and chemical exchange saturation transfer (CEST), exhibit enhanced sensitivity to semisolid macromolecular content, mobile proteins, tissue metabolites, and acidosis. Despite these advantages, ST-MRI techniques typically have been qualitative or semi-quantitative, time-consuming, and impractical for clinical implementation. However, emerging ST-MR fingerprinting (ST-MRF) represents a significant analytical advancement by integrating RF saturation preparation into a pseudo-randomized MRF acquisition framework with a deep learning-based reconstruction. This approach enables simultaneous, clinically realistic, quantitative mapping of bulk water relaxation properties (e.g., T 1 and T 2 ), semisolid macromolecular parameters, and exchangeable solute dynamics (e.g., pool size ratios and exchange rates). We provide a comprehensive background, methodological principles, and evolving clinical applications of ST-MRF in neuro-oncology. We explore current advancements, strengths, limitations, and future possibilities for clinical translation into neuro-oncology workflows, including tumor characterization, treatment response monitoring, infiltration mapping, and biomarker development.

title: MORSE-PI: flexible and artefact-free image reconstruction for structural and functional QSM and other phase-critical imaging applications.
abstract: Purpose Phase imaging applications such as QSM are highly sensitive to noise amplifications, phase singularities, and other artefacts, particularly in challenging scenarios such as ultra-high field (7 T), under-sampled or single-echo acquisitions. We present a novel image reconstruction method, MORSE-PI, designed to produce high-SNR, artefact-free, and singularity-free phase images for both structural (SWI, QSM) and functional (fQSM) phase-based brain imaging. Methods MORSE-PI extends our previous approach, MORSE, by introducing a Virtual Reference Coil (VRC). The VRC is constructed as a linear combination of coil sensitivity maps, with correlations enhanced between coil elements using the noise covariance matrix. Such a VRC ensures robust signal support across the entire brain and is used to correct phase offsets in the MORSE-derived coil sensitivity estimates, resulting in artefact-free, high-SNR phase. Results Compared to GRAPPA with ASPIRE phase correction, MORSE-PI demonstrates greater robustness to artefacts such as noise amplification and aliasing, and shows improved reproducibility in structural imaging at both 3 T and 7 T. Unlike ESPIRiT and GRAPPA combined with adaptive coil combination methods, MORSE-PI yields singularity-free phase maps. MORSE-PI enables high-SNR reconstructions even for the most challenging scenarios, such as single-echo EPI at 7 T. Its efficient, containerised implementation using the Gadgetron framework supports deployment on the MRI scanner console during measurements. Conclusion MORSE-PI offers a flexible and computationally efficient solution for generating high-SNR, artefact- and singularity-free phase images in both single- and multi-echo GRE and EPI acquisitions. This makes it particularly well-suited for structural and functional QSM, as well as other phase-based MRI applications. Its robustness and rapid computational time facilitate efficient deployment on scanners across field strengths.

Conclusion

MORSE-PI offers a flexible and computationally efficient solution for generating high-SNR, artefact- and singularity-free phase images in both single- and multi-echo GRE and EPI acquisitions. This makes it particularly well-suited for structural and functional QSM, as well as other phase-based MRI applications. Its robustness and rapid computational time facilitate efficient deployment on scanners across field strengths.

title: Observer agreement in sonographic glandular tissue component classification and sonographic breast density assessment: a multi-institutional study.
abstract: Purpose The sonographic glandular tissue component (GTC) is a potential imaging biomarker for stratifying breast cancer risk in women with dense breasts. This study evaluated the reproducibility, reliability, and clinical applicability of GTC classification and GTC-based sonographic breast density assessment in a multicenter observer study. Methods Fifteen readers (nine physicians and six sonographers) from 12 institutions independently assessed 100 paired ultrasound images twice, 1 month apart, with the dataset rearranged for the second reading. GTC was qualitatively classified into four categories according to its estimated proportion within the fibroglandular tissue (FGT): minimal, mild, moderate, and marked; minimal/mild were grouped as low GTC and moderate/marked as high GTC. Sonographic breast density was categorized as sonographic dense breast (high GTC), sonographic non-dense breast (visible fat lobules), or intermediate, with intermediate cases further divided into high or low categories using an FGT-to-FAT (subcutaneous and retromammary fat) ratio cutoff of 1. Interobserver and intraobserver agreement was evaluated using κ statistics. Results Substantial interobserver agreement was observed for the four-class GTC classification, the two-class GTC classification, and sonographic breast density assessment. Intraobserver agreement was moderate for the four-class GTC classification and substantial for the two-class GTC classification and sonographic breast density assessment. The majority-vote sonographic breast density assessment showed substantial agreement with the mammographic ground truth, whereas individual-reader assessments showed moderate concordance with mammographic breast density both overall and in intermediate-density breasts. No significant differences in agreement were observed between physicians and sonographers. Conclusion Substantial interobserver agreement and moderate-to-substantial intraobserver agreement support the reproducibility and reliability of GTC classification and GTC-based sonographic breast density assessment.

title: Spatially Resolved 3D Mechanobiological Model of Rat Femoral Fracture Healing Integrating Mechanics, Vasculature, and Cell Migration.
abstract: Fracture repair arises from the interaction of mechanical, vascular, and cellular processes whose spatial organization remains difficult to predict. We developed an image-derived three-dimensional mechanobiological framework that couples finite-element mechanics, strain-regulated vascularization, progenitor-cell redistribution, and tissue differentiation within a controlled rat femoral osteotomy-and-fixation construct. Model outputs were compared regionally and temporally with ex vivo micro-computed tomography (μCT) and histology over a 6-week healing period. The simulation reproduced several experimentally observed spatial features, including early peripheral/periosteal mineralization followed by later fracture-centered consolidation. Using a calibration/evaluation framework in which day 35 was used to map simulated regional stiffness to μCT bone area and days 14, 21, 28, and 42 were withheld for evaluation, the combined migration formulation showed the strongest overall held-out model-experiment correspondence (Pearson r = 0.57, Spearman ρ = 0.78, MAE = 0.70 mm 2 , RMSE = 0.88 mm 2 , R 2 = 0.30). Correspondence was weaker for diffusion-only, mechanically guided only, and no migration control. Thus, the migration formulation influenced downstream predictions of regional mineralization, with the combined diffusion and mechanical-guidance formulation showing the strongest correspondence with held-out μCT measurements, although substantial regional error and imperfect absolute calibration remained. Data-driven analysis of simulated element-wise stiffness trajectories identified reproducible computational trajectory classes that exhibited distinct anatomical distributions. Early simulated mechanobiological features were also associated with later simulated stiffness; because this analysis operates entirely within the simulation, it characterizes internal predictive structure rather than independent biological outcome prediction. Together, these findings demonstrate the feasibility of coupling image-derived 3D geometry, mechanics, vascularization, and progenitor cell migration to study spatial heterogeneity during fracture repair in a single, well-controlled construct. Validation across additional geometries, fixation environments, and independent experimental datasets is required before broader biological or clinical generalization.

title: Agreement between fully automated artificial intelligence and cardiac radiologists for coronary stenosis and plaque assessment in an asymptomatic screening cohort.
abstract: This retrospective single-center study evaluated segment-level agreement between experienced cardiac radiologists and a research AI platform for coronary stenosis and plaque assessment on coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA). Asymptomatic individuals undergoing CCTA at a health screening center were studied, excluding those with prior revascularization, coronary anomaly, or total occlusion. Stenosis grade and plaque composition were independently assessed by the AI platform and two cardiac radiologists at the segment level, with disagreements between the two radiologists resolved by consensus. Agreement was evaluated using Cohen's κ, quadratic weighted κ for ordinal grading, observed agreement, and positive and negative agreement for dichotomized significant stenosis. The cohort comprised 172 participants and 2,582 segments. Significant stenosis was uncommon (18/2,582, 0.7%), with moderate agreement (κ = 0.412; observed agreement 98.5%; positive agreement 0.418; negative agreement 0.992). Agreement was fair for ordinal stenosis grade (κ = 0.397; quadratic weighted κ = 0.573; observed agreement 84.0%) and plaque composition (κ = 0.330; observed agreement 81.8%). Stenosis-grade agreement was lower in plaque-containing than plaque-free segments, an exploratory finding given marked differences in subgroup size and prevalence. Myocardial bridging and image quality were not major descriptive determinants of discordance. In this low-prevalence cohort, AI-based CCTA analysis showed high negative agreement for radiologist-defined significant stenosis but limited concordance for grading and plaque characterization. Reflecting low prevalence and few positive cases, the findings do not establish independent rule-out performance but support prospective evaluation of AI as an expert-supervised pre-reading or triage adjunct, with positive, ambiguous, or plaque-containing findings requiring expert review.

title: Discriminatory value of non-contrast CT coronary artery calcium radiomics for major adverse cardiovascular events in patients with coronary artery disease.
abstract: To evaluate whether radiomic features derived from non-contrast coronary artery calcium (CAC) CT provide incremental discriminatory information beyond conventional CAC measures for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). This study retrospectively analyzed 208 patients with coronary artery disease (CAD) who underwent coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) from 2014 to 2022. Radiomics features were extracted from each coronary artery segment on non-contrast CT images. Six predictive models were constructed using logistic regression with least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LR-LASSO): (1) clinical model; (2) conventional CAC measures model; (3) radiomics-only model; (4) radiomics combined with conventional CAC measures model; (5) radiomics combined with clinical model; and (6) comprehensive model integrating radiomic features, clinical features, and conventional CAC measures. Model performance was evaluated using area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC) analysis, and assessed using the DeLong test with false discovery rate (FDR) correction. In this study, a total of 104 patients with MACE and 104 non-MACE patients were included. The radiomics combined with conventional CAC measures model achieved AUC of 0.830 and 0.825 in the training and testing cohorts. Compared with the conventional CAC measures model, its discriminatory performance was significantly improved in both cohorts (p < 0.001 and p = 0.008). However, further incorporating clinical features into this model did not result in a significant additional improvement in predictive performance (p > 0.05). In this cohort, adding radiomic features to conventional CAC measures improved MACE discrimination, whereas adding conventional CAC measures to radiomics did not significantly improve discrimination.

title: Accelerated aortic stenosis progression is associated with greater CT-derived extracellular volume.
abstract: Rapid progression of aortic stenosis (AS) is associated with adverse outcomes, yet the myocardial changes accompanying faster progression remain incompletely characterized. We evaluated the association between the rate of AS progression and myocardial fibrosis assessed by computed tomography (CT)-derived extracellular volume fraction (ECV), and the impact on clinical outcomes. We studied 134 patients with classical high-gradient severe AS who underwent pre-transcatheter aortic valve implantation cardiac CT with a delayed dual-energy acquisition for ECV quantification and had at least two echocardiograms ≥ 6 months apart. Progression was defined as the annualized change in peak aortic jet velocity. Rapid progression was defined as an increase > 0.30 m/s/year. Patients were followed for a composite of cardiovascular hospitalization, urgent aortic valve replacement, or death. ECV correlated with progression rate (Spearman ρ = 0.33, p < 0.001). In multivariable linear regression, faster progression remained independently associated with ECV (β = 2.52, p = 0.001). Rapid progressors had higher ECV than slow progressors (31.5% vs. 28.3%, p < 0.001). Over a median follow-up of 16.2 months, 36 patients (26.9%) reached the composite outcome. Patients with both rapid progression and high ECV had an event rate of 69 versus 11 per 100 patient-years in those without (adjusted HR 6.22, 95% CI 3.13-12.32). Faster AS progression is independently associated with greater diffuse myocardial fibrosis, irrespective of stenosis severity, and their combination identified patients at higher risk of adverse events. These findings suggest that AS progression rate and myocardial tissue characterization carry complementary prognostic information in severe AS.

Faster AS progression is independently associated with greater diffuse myocardial fibrosis, irrespective of stenosis severity, and their combination identified patients at higher risk of adverse events. These findings suggest that AS progression rate and myocardial tissue characterization carry complementary prognostic information in severe AS.

title: Transmitral flow analysis via valve tracking 4D flow MRI detects age- and sex-related diastolic changes.
abstract: To evaluate whether valve tracking 4D flow MRI can detect subtle age- and sex-related changes in left ventricular (LV) diastolic function in healthy adults. We retrospectively recruited healthy adults who had undergone cardiac MRI between October 2020 and March 2022, selecting those with whole-heart 4D flow MRI, 2D long-axis cine, and short-axis cine acquisitions. A dynamic plane at the mitral valve (MV) level was generated in 4D flow MRI using leaflet insertion points tracked on 2- and 4-chamber cine images. Through-plane velocities were computed from 4D flow data and corrected for MV motion. After contouring the transmitral region, early and late diastolic peak flow rates (E flow , A flow ), peak velocities (E vel, A vel ), and mitral forward flow volume (MFVol) were measured. Peak early LV relaxation velocity (E MV ) was defined as the peak through-plane velocity of MV plane motion. A total of 39 adults (age range: 46 ± 13; 20 women) were included. With age, both E flow /A flow (r = - 0.79, p < 0.0001, adjusted for HR) and E vel /A vel (r = - 0.70, p < 0.0001, adjusted for HR) were significantly decreased, while E vel /E MV increased (r = 0.53, p < 0.001, adjusted for EDV). Early diastolic changes were sex-specific; women showed decreased E flow and increased E vel /E MV with aging, whereas men showed no significant associations. Additionally, the normalized E flow /MFVol decreased with aging, significantly in the sex-combined cohort (r = - 0.42, p = 0.008) and in women (r = - 0.68, p = 0.004), but not in men. Transmitral flow rates and peak velocities assessed by 4D flow MRI with cine-based valve tracking effectively detected physiologic age-related declines in diastolic function, exhibiting sex-specific differences.

title: Progress in multimodal imaging assessment of the correlation between perivascular adipose tissue and atherosclerosis.
abstract: Cardiovascular disease remains a leading cause of death and disability worldwide. Adipose tissue dysfunction is a key driver, and perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT) exerts location‑specific effects on the cardiovascular system. This review focuses on PVAT in atherosclerosis, with particular attention to pericoronary PVAT, epicardial adipose tissue (EAT), carotid PVAT, and peri-aortic adipose tissue (PAAT). PVAT homeostasis relies on UCP1‑mediated thermogenesis for metabolic modulation and on paracrine signaling via adiponectin and apelin. Under aging, obesity, or diabetes, PVAT switches from an anti‑inflammatory to a pro‑inflammatory phenotype, accelerating plaque formation through bidirectional inflammatory crosstalk. For clinical assessment, this review highlights progress in multimodal imaging technologies, including CT fat attenuation index, MRI water‑lipid separation, PET/CT, and echocardiography, for noninvasive quantification of PVAT density, composition, and metabolic activity, and compares their advantages and limitations. This review further discusses artificial intelligence (AI)-driven radiomic and radiotranscriptomic approaches that extend PVAT assessment beyond conventional single-parameter metrics. We systematically review the research progress of these techniques in evaluating dynamic PVAT changes and their correlation with atherosclerosis, aiming to clarify the intrinsic correlation between imaging‑derived PVAT functional status and AS development.
