title: Different diffusion priors and their ensemble for sparse-view CT reconstruction.
abstract: Purpose Diffusion models have shown strong potential for medical image reconstruction, but their use requires careful balancing between data fidelity and learned diffusion priors. This study proposes an ensemble-based sparse-view CT reconstruction method that automatically optimizes this trade-off. Methods We develop an ensemble framework that combines reconstructions obtained from multiple time steps of a pre-trained denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM), corresponding to different noise levels. Reconstructions at small time steps emphasize measurement consistency and preserve fine anatomical details but tend to retain artifacts, whereas those at large time steps rely more strongly on the diffusion prior, reducing artifacts at the expense of structural fidelity. The proposed method integrates these complementary reconstructions using spatially adaptive weights optimized during reconstruction. Results Experiments on sparse-view CT reconstruction show that the proposed ensemble approach effectively reduces artifacts while preserving anatomical structures in moderately sparse acquisition settings. Quantitative evaluations using SSIM and PSNR demonstrate improved performance compared with iterative reconstruction (IR), IR with total variation regularization (IR+TV), diffusion posterior sampling (DPS), and decomposed diffusion sampler (DDS). However, in extremely sparse conditions (e.g., 25 views), the advantage of the ensemble becomes limited due to severe information loss. Conclusions The proposed framework enables effective balancing of data fidelity and diffusion priors in sparse-view CT reconstruction when a moderate level of measurement information is available. By leveraging complementary information across different diffusion priors, the method improves reconstruction quality and structural consistency, indicating potential utility for radiation dose reduction in CT imaging.

title: Recent advances in photoacoustic imaging for breast reconstruction using the abdominal flap.
abstract: Recent advances in diagnostic imaging have significantly impacted surgical planning and options. In breast reconstruction using abdominal flaps, a method employing flaps from the lower abdomen allows for a high-quality reconstruction with a morphology and texture resembling those of the contralateral breast. Understanding microvascular patterns is crucial in this surgery to prevent volume deficiencies and contribute to successful tissue transplantation while maintaining the softness of the tissue. While the location and number of "perforators"-arteriovenous bundles penetrating the anterior sheath of the rectus abdominis-have traditionally been the focus, recent studies have further emphasized the importance of selecting appropriate perforating vessels to maintain the vascular network within the superficial adipose tissue and subcutaneous tissue and to elevate a high-quality flap with extensive and stable blood flow. Clinical studies using contrast-enhanced CT have drawn attention to the midline-crossing arterial network, demonstrating its relationship with a wide range of hemodynamic areas. Preoperatively, clearly identifying the blood vessels linking the left and right sides of the abdominal midline provides valuable information for planning free DIEP flaps for breast reconstruction, ensuring stable blood flow to the flap. However, clear visualization with contrast-enhanced CT requires high volumes of contrast agents, and color Doppler ultrasound has difficulty visualizing horizontally; therefore, a non-invasive and superior imaging method is required. Photoacoustic imaging can comprehensively and noninvasively visualize the subcutaneous vascular network and is attracting attention as a new preoperative examination technique. We conducted clinical research using newly developed medical photoacoustic imaging and reported the results and future challenges in several publications. We have also recently reported the impact of abdominal surgical scars on the midline-crossing artery. This review summarizes the current trends in preoperative vascular studies for breast reconstruction using abdominal flaps and discusses the current state of evolving photoacoustic imaging technology.

title: A Cohort Study of Lung Cancer Screening and Size at Diagnosis 2017-2023: Trends Among US Veterans.
abstract: Background Lung cancer, the leading cause of cancer death in the USA, is an important indicator to track effects of the COVID-19 pandemic on cancer diagnosis trends. Objective Evaluate pandemic impact on lung cancer screening, diagnosis, and cancer size at diagnosis. Design Cohort study (January 2017-June 2023). Participants Veterans who were users of Veterans Affairs (VA) healthcare system, and subgroup of Veterans eligible for lung cancer screening. Exposures Pandemic (March 2020-June 2023) versus pre-pandemic period (January 2017-February 2020). Main measures Among lung cancer screening eligible Veterans: expected screening rates compared to observed rates and cancer size at diagnosis. Among users of VA: cancer size at diagnosis, lung cancer diagnosis rates, CT scan utilization. Key results Among 1,867,387 screen eligible Veterans, annual screening fell from 7.3% in January 2020 to 5.7%, recovering to pre-pandemic rates by March 2022, ending at 11% (June 2023). Among screen eligible but non-participating Veterans, median cancer size decreased from 20 mm (95% CI 19, 20) to 18 mm (95% CI 16, 19) after pandemic onset. Among screening participants, cancer size was smaller (15 mm) and did not change with pandemic. Among VA users regardless of screening eligibility, lung cancer diagnosis rates were lower than expected based on pre-pandemic data. Conclusions The pandemic was associated with a prolonged disruption in lung cancer screening; recovery exceeded 2 years and screening remains low. The pandemic may have caused forward displacement of mortality: rates of lung cancer diagnosis decreased among older adults and median size at diagnosis got smaller among some groups. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

title: Comparative Diagnostic Accuracy of Point-of-Care Ultrasound for Detecting Reduced Left Ventricular Systolic Function: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Objective To assess the diagnostic accuracy of point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) for detecting reduced left ventricular systolic function (LVSF) using visual qualitative assessment (VQA), E-point septal separation (EPSS), and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted assessment, compared with transthoracic echocardiography (TTE). Methods We searched PubMed, Ovid MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library from January 1, 1985, through July 8, 2025. Eligible studies compared POCUS-assessed LVSF with left ventricular ejection fraction measured by TTE (or cardiac MRI in one study). Data were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis to determine the diagnostic odds ratio (DOR) and likelihood ratios (LR) for each of the three methods. Results Twenty-eight studies, including 4,647 participants, met inclusion criteria. Nine studies evaluating VQA yielded a DOR of 40.53 (95% CI, 15.07 to 109.00; P < 0.001) and a positive LR (LR + ) of 6.90 (95% CI, 3.75 to 12.69). Seven studies evaluating EPSS resulted in a DOR of 21.77 (95% CI, 10.25 to 46.28; P < 0.001) and a LR + of 5.70 (95% CI, 2.89 to 11.22). Five studies evaluating AI-assisted POCUS resulted in a DOR of 47.35 (95% CI, 16.87 to 132.93; P < 0.001) and a LR + of 8.37 (95% CI, 4.40 to 15.93). Meta-regression analyses revealed no statistically significant differences in diagnostic performance among the three methods. Subgroup analysis by operator experience level also showed no statistically significant difference between novice and experienced operators for each method. Conclusions VQA, EPSS, and AI-assisted POCUS all demonstrate moderate-to-high diagnostic accuracy for identifying reduced LVSF, with no significant differences among methods on meta-regression or by operator experience level. Moderately strong LR + across all three methods supports the use of POCUS for ruling in reduced LVSF. EPSS cutoffs at the lower and upper ends of the reported range showed higher sensitivity and specificity, respectively, suggesting utility as a rule-in or rule-out tool where formal echocardiography is not readily available. Registration PROSPERO CRD42024626542.

title: Development and Validation of a Bedside Sarcopenia-Nutrition Score to Predict Mortality in Cirrhosis: A Prospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Background Sarcopenia is a common but often overlooked complication of advanced liver cirrhosis and is independently associated with decompensation and mortality. Because CT-based muscle quantification is not always feasible in resource-limited settings, we developed and validated a bedside Cirrhotic Sarcopenia-Nutrition Score (CSNS) incorporating anthropometric, ultrasonographic, and metabolic variables to predict 12-month morbidity and mortality in patients with end-stage liver disease. Methods This prospective observational cohort study included 350 adult patients enrolled from December 2023 to April 2026. Patient selection was sequential and prospective into a development cohort (n = 250) and an independent temporal validation cohort (n = 100). All participants met sarcopenia criteria based on gait speed and handgrip strength. Six bedside parameters: triceps skinfold thickness, mid-upper arm circumference, mid-arm muscle circumference, mid-thigh circumference, ultrasound-derived psoas muscle thickness, and nitrogen balance were combined via penalized logistic regression to generate the CSNS on a 0-100 scale. Model performance was evaluated using AUROC and compared with MELD-Na and Child-Turcotte-Pugh (CTP) scores. External validation was performed in the independent cohort. Results Nitrogen balance and psoas muscle thickness contributed most strongly to the final model. At an optimal cutoff of 61.2, the CSNS showed good discrimination for 12-month mortality in both the development (AUROC 0.816) and validation (AUROC 0.803) cohorts, with higher AUROC values than MELD-Na and CTP. High CSNS remained an independent predictor of mortality (adjusted HR 1.023; p = 0.002) and was significantly associated with major cirrhosis-related complications, including hepatic encephalopathy, acute kidney injury, refractory ascites, and upper gastrointestinal bleeding (all p ≤ 0.003). Conclusion The CSNS is a simple, radiation-free bedside tool that improves prognostic assessment beyond conventional scores and may support risk stratification in resource-limited settings.

title: Fracture risk in 85-year-old women: associations with volumetric bone mineral density, physical performance and falls.
abstract: This prospective study demonstrates associations of volumetric BMD (vBMD) by pQCT, areal BMD (aBMD) by DXA, physical performance (one-leg balance, gait speed, and knee extension force), and fall history with fracture risk in 85-year-old women. A failed one-leg balance test was associated with both hip and any fracture independent of femoral neck aBMD. Total radial vBMD was associated with any fracture. Gait speed and previous falls showed associations with fracture risk of similar magnitude as femoral neck aBMD. These findings suggest that functional performance measures may enhance fracture risk assessment in older women. Purpose This prospective study evaluates associations between fracture risk and volumetric bone mineral density (vBMD) by peripheral quantitative computed tomography (pQCT), physical performance tests, and fall history, in comparison with femoral neck areal BMD (aBMD) by DXA, in 85-year-old women. Methods In the Osteoporosis Prospective Risk Assessment (OPRA) study, 382 women aged 85 years were followed for a mean of 4.3 years. Participants underwent pQCT of the radius and tibia and DXA of the hip and lumbar spine, performed physical performance tests (one-leg standing balance, considered failed if balance could not be maintained for 5 s; gait speed, analyzed continuously; and knee extension force, measured by isometric dynamometry), and reported fall history. Cox proportional hazards models estimated fracture risk, adjusting for BMI, previous fracture, smoking, and use of vitamin D, glucocorticoids, and bisphosphonates. Results During a mean follow-up of 4.3 years, 116 women (30%) sustained a fracture. Trabecular vBMD at the radius and tibia was associated with lower risk of any fracture (HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.55-0.85 and HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.55-0.86, respectively). Radial trabecular vBMD was also associated with lower hip fracture risk (HR 0.64, 95% CI 0.42-0.98). Femoral neck aBMD was associated with lower risk of any fracture (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.62-0.90), but not hip fracture (HR 0.71, 95% CI 0.50-1.00). A failed balance test and low gait speed was associated with higher risk of any fracture (HR 1.55, 95% CI 1.04-2.29 and HR 1.22, 95% CI 1.01-1.48, respectively). In multivariate analyses, a failed balance test remained associated with any fracture (HR 1.70, 95% CI 1.12-2.56) and hip fracture (HR 2.30, 95% CI 1.05-5.02). Total radial vBMD remained associated with any fracture (HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.63-0.996). Conclusion Volumetric BMD by pQCT was associated with fracture risk independent of commonly recognized clinical risk factors in 85-year-old women. Physical performance tests were associated with fracture risk in unadjusted analyses, and the one-leg balance test additionally remained associated after adjustment for clinical risk factors and femoral neck aBMD.

Radial trabecular vBMD was also associated with lower hip fracture risk (HR 0.64, 95% CI 0.42-0.98). Femoral neck aBMD was associated with lower risk of any fracture (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.62-0.90), but not hip fracture (HR 0.71, 95% CI 0.50-1.00). A failed balance test and low gait speed was associated with higher risk of any fracture (HR 1.55, 95% CI 1.04-2.29 and HR 1.22, 95% CI 1.01-1.48, respectively). In multivariate analyses, a failed balance test remained associated with any fracture (HR 1.70, 95% CI 1.12-2.56) and hip fracture (HR 2.30, 95% CI 1.05-5.02). Total radial vBMD remained associated with any fracture (HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.63-0.996).

Conclusion

Volumetric BMD by pQCT was associated with fracture risk independent of commonly recognized clinical risk factors in 85-year-old women. Physical performance tests were associated with fracture risk in unadjusted analyses, and the one-leg balance test additionally remained associated after adjustment for clinical risk factors and femoral neck aBMD.

title: Development of subcortical nuclei volume in utero over the second and third trimester.
abstract: Subcortical nuclei are important structures in the brain. Previous MRI evaluation of fetal brain development mostly focused on cerebral cortex and the myelination process, but few of them explored the developmental pattern of subcortical nuclei. The aim of this study is to analyze the developmental characteristics of fetal subcortical nuclei and their relationship with gestational age and cortical development. In this retrospective study, the precise axial, sagittal, and coronal views of T2-weighted brain MRI sequences in 47 fetuses with normal brains in the gestational age (GA) range of 22 to 36 weeks were obtained. A single 3D motion-corrected high-resolution brain volume was reconstructed from the 2D SSTSE imaging stacks using a slice-to-volume reconstruction (SVR) method. The volumes of the subcortical nuclei, i.e., amygdala, caudate, pallidum, putamen, hippocampus, subthalamic nucleus, thalamus, and cortex were segmented and corrected based on the above 3D images. We drew the developmental curve of each subcortical nucleus with age. The Pearson correlation coefficients were calculated between volumes of subcortical nuclei, as well as between volumes of cortical and subcortical regions, to explore how cortical regions and subcortical nuclei matured cooperatively. We illustrated the developmental trajectory curves of volumes of six subcortical nuclei and one of subcortical structure (thalamus, amygdala, hippocampus, caudate, putamen, subthalamic nucleus, and pallidum) according to the changes in GA to show the development trajectory of subcortical nuclei at 22-36 weeks. We further illustrated that volumes of subcortical nuclei and subcortical structure increased nonlinearly with GA, and the velopmental trajectories indicated laterality in the subcortical nuclei of the fetal brain. In addition, we found insignificant maturational coupling between subcortical nuclei and cortical regions, whereas the degree of maturational coupling between subcortical nuclei was relatively high. We found the volume of subcortical nuclei increased nonlinearly with the increase of GA, and the trajectory of nuclear mass development was lateral. The patterns of nuclear cluster development could expand our understanding of the brain growth. Reference ranges of fetal intracranial structures across gestational ages can serve as a valuable adjunct to prenatal counseling when interpreted in conjunction with clinical context and ultrasound findings.

title: Conventional Preoperative Prediction of MASLD-Compatible Histologic Abnormality, Fibrosis, and Higher-Grade Steatohepatitis, and Exploratory Machine-Learning Classification of MASH Severity in Patients Undergoing Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass.
abstract: Introduction Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is highly prevalent in patients with severe obesity undergoing metabolic/bariatric surgery. Noninvasive preoperative stratification of histologic liver abnormalities remains incomplete. We evaluated conventional regression models and a separate exploratory machine-learning analysis of MASH grade 1 versus grades 2/3. Methods This retrospective single-center cohort included patients undergoing Roux-en-Y gastric bypass between March 2000 and March 2025. Of 1,350 surgical patients, 745 underwent intraoperative wedge liver biopsy and 375 had complete data for conventional modeling. Conventional endpoints were MASLD-compatible histologic abnormality, any documented fibrosis, and higher-grade steatohepatitis, defined as biopsy-reported grades 2/3. The machine-learning analysis included 284 patients with steatohepatitis and used routine preoperative variables, ultrasound-reported steatosis, NFS, the AST/ALT ratio, and FIB-4. Model development used RandomizedSearchCV and repeated stratified cross-validation within the training set, followed by training-based threshold selection and held-out test evaluation. Results BMI and triglycerides were associated with MASLD-compatible histologic abnormality, BMI with any fibrosis, and age, BMI, triglycerides, and AST with higher-grade steatohepatitis. The latter conventional model had an apparent AUC of 0.737 and a mean cross-validated AUC of 0.692. L2-penalized logistic regression had the highest machine-learning test ROC-AUC point estimate (0.730; 95% CI, 0.585-0.864), with sensitivity 0.739 for MASH grades 2/3 at a threshold of 0.49. Test Brier score was 0.242; calibration was unsatisfactory (ECE 0.203; calibration slope 13.469), and decision-curve findings remained exploratory. Conclusion Routine preoperative information showed moderate discrimination for selected histologic outcomes. Both the conventional score and the machine-learning severity classifier require further validation before clinical implementation.

Introduction

Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is highly prevalent in patients with severe obesity undergoing metabolic/bariatric surgery. Noninvasive preoperative stratification of histologic liver abnormalities remains incomplete. We evaluated conventional regression models and a separate exploratory machine-learning analysis of MASH grade 1 versus grades 2/3.

Methods

This retrospective single-center cohort included patients undergoing Roux-en-Y gastric bypass between March 2000 and March 2025. Of 1,350 surgical patients, 745 underwent intraoperative wedge liver biopsy and 375 had complete data for conventional modeling. Conventional endpoints were MASLD-compatible histologic abnormality, any documented fibrosis, and higher-grade steatohepatitis, defined as biopsy-reported grades 2/3. The machine-learning analysis included 284 patients with steatohepatitis and used routine preoperative variables, ultrasound-reported steatosis, NFS, the AST/ALT ratio, and FIB-4. Model development used RandomizedSearchCV and repeated stratified cross-validation within the training set, followed by training-based threshold selection and held-out test evaluation.

Results

BMI and triglycerides were associated with MASLD-compatible histologic abnormality, BMI with any fibrosis, and age, BMI, triglycerides, and AST with higher-grade steatohepatitis. The latter conventional model had an apparent AUC of 0.737 and a mean cross-validated AUC of 0.692. L2-penalized logistic regression had the highest machine-learning test ROC-AUC point estimate (0.730; 95% CI, 0.585-0.864), with sensitivity 0.739 for MASH grades 2/3 at a threshold of 0.49. Test Brier score was 0.242; calibration was unsatisfactory (ECE 0.203; calibration slope 13.469), and decision-curve findings remained exploratory.

title: Navigated robotic guidance for minimally invasive bertolotti resection technical feasibility and workflow evaluation.
abstract: Bertolotti syndrome is characterized by symptomatic lumbosacral transitional vertebral anatomy in which an enlarged transverse process articulates or fuses with the sacrum or ilium. Diagnosis can be difficult because transitional anatomy is common, symptoms may overlap with other spinal disorders, and the pain generator may arise from the pseudoarticulation, adjacent disc or facet, instability, or nerve compression. When targeted nonoperative treatment fails, surgical options include resection, nerve decompression, or fusion depending on anatomy and the dominant pain mechanism. Published evidence supports image guidance for localization and confirmation of resection and describes early robotic assistance for incision planning; however, evidence specific to robotic Bertolotti resection remains limited. This original article evaluates the technical feasibility and workflow of a preoperatively planned, navigated robotic workflow to perform minimally invasive Bertolotti resection. A technical framework is presented for preoperative computerized computed-tomography planning, convergent access through a minimally invasive incision, and navigated robotic trajectory-controlled drilling of bone-cut trajectories across the transverse processes and pseudoarticulations, osteotomy, fragment removal and verification of complete decompression or resection. Feasibility was assessed by completion of the planned navigated robotic steps, intraoperative confirmation of registration and resection, and review of technical, perioperative, and imaging outcomes. These concepts may improve reproducibility and reduce challenges related to limited visualization and complex three-dimensional anatomy, but they should not be interpreted as proof of superior outcomes. This initial paper outlines a novel technique, however; further comparative studies using standardized measures of pain, disability, operative time, blood loss, radiation exposure, navigation accuracy, resection quality, and reoperation rate are needed before the clinical value of robotic guidance can be established.

title: Image-guided decision-making in complex robot-assisted partial nephrectomy: vascular control, resection precision, and functional outcomes.
abstract: During robot-assisted partial nephrectomy (RAPN), image-guided techniques provide increasingly detailed patient-specific information; however, their incremental clinical value for complex renal tumours remains unclear. This narrative review examines how 3D reconstruction, virtual reality or augmented reality, intraoperative ultrasound, indocyanine green fluorescence, and computational perfusion modelling influence vascular control and tumour resection. The review focuses specifically on patients with high nephrometry scores (R.E.N.A.L. or PADUA ≥ 10), completely endophytic or hilar lesions, and limited renal reserve. The evidence was synthesised using a RAPN-specific decision-to-outcome framework that distinguishes between anatomical information, documented changes in surgical planning, actual operative actions, preservation of viable and perfused renal parenchyma, and patient-level outcomes. Observational comparative studies suggest that image guidance may facilitate selective vascular management, adjust resection strategies, and reduce excessive parenchymal resection as reflected by certain metrics. Multiple cohort studies have reported positive associations with renal function, including postoperative renal parameters based on radionuclide imaging. However, randomised imaging trials have not yet demonstrated consistent or sustained functional benefits, particularly in highly complex tumours. Interpretation of study results is limited by the following factors: heterogeneity of the control groups, historical and surgeon-related confounders, potential cohort overlap, and the non-interchangeability of functional or surrogate endpoints. Future studies should quantify the incremental value of imaging techniques beyond standard of care, document planned versus actual decisions, and independently assess ipsilateral renal function while evaluating oncological safety, workflow requirements, and costs. Currently, image guidance is best viewed as an optional decision-support tool, based on actionable anatomical uncertainty rather than hypothesised long-term functional benefits.

title: A useful robotic approach for a large posterior mediastinal tumor adjacent to the Adamkiewicz artery.
abstract: Robotic approach for posterior mediastinal tumors enables operating in the narrow mediastinal space while providing a three-dimensional (3D) magnified view. However, few reports have described robotic surgery for posterior mediastinal tumors adjacent to the Adamkiewicz artery (AKA). Injury to the AKA may cause serious neurological complications due to its role as the blood supply for the spinal cord lower two-thirds. We present a case of robotic resection of a large posterior mediastinal tumor adjacent to the AKA, offering an intraoperative field of view comparable to preoperative 3D-computed tomography (CT).

title: Coexistent tracheal bronchus and azygos lobe: surgical planning and operative technique for robotic-assisted right upper lobectomy.
abstract: Tracheal bronchus and azygos lobe are individually uncommon congenital anomalies arising from independent embryological mechanisms. Their simultaneous occurrence is exceptionally rare, with fewer than five cases identifiable in the published literature. We report an adult patient in whom a displaced apical segmental bronchus arising directly from the tracheal wall, a bifid right upper lobe bronchus comprising only the anterior and posterior segmental bronchi, and an associated azygos lobe. Elective robotic-assisted right upper lobectomy was undertaken for a biopsy proven primary lung cancer. Final histopathology confirmed grade 2 adenocarcinoma with clear surgical margins without lymph node involvement. Preoperative three-dimensional reconstruction was helpful for surgical planning and we describe the operative principles required to safely manage this unusual anatomical combination.

title: Impact of examination geometry on radiation dose to patient and operator during interventional procedures.
abstract: Background In interventional radiology, staff radiation exposure mainly originates from patient-scattered radiation. While standard protective tools are used, examination geometry, especially detector positioning and X-ray field size, critically influences both patient and operator doses. Quantitative data on these effects under controlled experimental conditions are limited. Aims To quantify the influence of examination geometry on patient and operator radiation doses and identify configurations minimising radiation exposure. Methods Measurements were performed using an Artis Q angiography system and polymethyl methacrylate phantoms measuring 17 cm and 25 cm in thickness, positioned at a height of 95 cm above the floor to simulate abdominal geometry. Kerma-area product (P KA ), air kerma at the interventional reference point (IRP), and operator personal dose equivalent Hp(10) measured at heights of 105, 135, and 165 cm above the floor, were recorded for different phantom-to-detector distances and X-ray field sizes. Operator dose was measured using the RaySafe i3 system. Results Increasing phantom thickness increased operator dose by an average factor of 4.0 (range, 1.8-6.8). For the large phantom and large X-ray field, air kerma at the IRP increased from 9.8 to 12.9 mGy per acquisition as the phantom-to-detector distance increased. Operator dose increased by up to 77% with a larger X-ray field and by more than 60% with increasing phantom-to-detector distance. Identical P KA values were obtained for different examination geometries, despite markedly different operator doses. Dose readings measured on top of the detector were below the detection limit of the dosimetry system in all measurements. Conclusion Examination geometry influences both patient dose indicators and operator dose. Reducing X-ray field size decreases P KA and operator dose, although air kerma at the IRP may increase slightly. Within the geometries investigated, a shorter patient-to-detector distance was associated with lower operator dose. Identical P KA values do not necessarily imply identical operator doses.

title: Advancements in Artificial Intelligence for Enhanced Diagnosis and Prognosis in Cardiac CT: a Comprehensive Review and Future Perspectives.
abstract: Purpose of review Cardiovascular disease, with coronary artery disease (CAD) as its main culprit, remains a leading cause of death worldwide. Traditional diagnostic methods that focus on the degree of arterial narrowing (percent diameter stenosis, or %DS) can miss early signs of disease or the specific plaque features that indicate high risk. The purpose of this review is to examine how artificial intelligence (AI) can enhance the diagnostic and prognostic capabilities of cardiac computed tomography (CCT), and to address where AI can most meaningfully improve diagnostic accuracy, workflow efficiency, and patient care. Recent findings AI is transforming cardiac CT across the entire imaging pathway. By applying AI algorithms, recent studies have refined the assessment of coronary artery calcium (CAC), improved plaque characterization, and detected subtle lesions that might evade traditional detection methods. AI further enables non-invasive assessment of ischemia (reduced blood flow), aids in the evaluation of myocardial infarction, analyzes adipose tissue surrounding the heart, improves image quality, and provides valuable prognostic insights for risk stratification. This comprehensive review explores the transformative potential of AI in cardiac CT, highlighting its role in accurate diagnosis, precise risk stratification, and personalized management of cardiovascular disease. Through collaboration between AI technology and clinical expertise, we envision a future where cardiac CT imaging is more powerful, efficient, and patient-centered, ultimately leading to improved outcomes in cardiovascular medicine. Continued standardization, external validation, and clinician education will be essential to realize this impact in routine practice.

title: Intraoperative Transrectal Ultrasound Guidance in Radical Prostatectomy: Balancing Cancer Control and Functional Preservation.
abstract: Purpose of review To examine the utility of intraoperative transrectal ultrasound (TRUS) during radical prostatectomy, specifically investigating when it is beneficial and how it can improve radical prostatectomy. Recent findings Intraoperative TRUS enables visualization of anatomical landmarks including cancer focus, in which the surgeon's intervention is blinded by endoscopic only, assistance with nerve-sparing, reduction of positive surgical margins, and precise dissection of the apex, bladder neck, and urethra. It is helpful particularly for beginners and in high-risk cases where extracapsular extension is suspected. Combining TRUS with preoperative multiparametric MRI and biopsy results could yield an even more accurate intraoperative navigation tool. Whereas preoperative MRI indicates "where the cancer is," intraoperative TRUS shows "where the surgeon is intervening" in real time. The fusion of real-time intraoperative TRUS images with prostatectomy helps to achieve precision surgery, leading to complete resection of the cancer while preserving function and maintaining quality of life.

originalAbstract:
Purpose of review

To examine the utility of intraoperative transrectal ultrasound (TRUS) during radical prostatectomy, specifically investigating when it is beneficial and how it can improve radical prostatectomy.

Recent findings

Intraoperative TRUS enables visualization of anatomical landmarks including cancer focus, in which the surgeon's intervention is blinded by endoscopic only, assistance with nerve-sparing, reduction of positive surgical margins, and precise dissection of the apex, bladder neck, and urethra. It is helpful particularly for beginners and in high-risk cases where extracapsular extension is suspected. Combining TRUS with preoperative multiparametric MRI and biopsy results could yield an even more accurate intraoperative navigation tool. Whereas preoperative MRI indicates "where the cancer is," intraoperative TRUS shows "where the surgeon is intervening" in real time. The fusion of real-time intraoperative TRUS images with prostatectomy helps to achieve precision surgery, leading to complete resection of the cancer while preserving function and maintaining quality of life.

title: Interchangeability of PSMA PET Tracers and Theranostic Target Efficacy in Prostate Cancer.
abstract: Purpose of review Three prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) positron emission tomography (PET) tracers hold FDA approval, and the theranostic agent, 177Lu-PSMA-617, given with an androgen receptor pathway inhibitor (ARPI) is now indicated for PSMA-positive metastatic hormone-sensitive disease, in addition to its use in metastatic castration-resistant disease. Our aim is to summarize the PSMA PET tracers in clinical use and their cross validity for 177Lu-PSMA-617 target efficacy. Recent findings Ga-68 PSMA-11, F-18 piflufolastat, and F-18 flotufolastat differ marginally in half-life, production, and urinary excretion, but none have shown diagnostic superiority. Pivotal trials, including VISION, PSMAfore, and PSMAddition determined eligibility with centrally read Ga-68 PSMA-11. American Society of Clinical Oncology guidance nevertheless accepts any of the three PSMA PET tracers for candidacy, and the 177Lu-PSMA-617 product label concurs. The rationale is physiologic and consensus-based: VISION defined positivity relative to liver uptake, and joint European American nuclear medicine guidance applies this rule to all tracers. Additionally, tumor/liver and tumor/salivary gland ratios are scanner-independent surrogates, supporting this cross validity. Quantitative predictors of prostate-specific antigen (PSA) response and overall survival were derived using Ga-68 PSMA-11, but emerging fluorine-18 data are supportive, though there's a lack of standardization. The approved tracers appear cross-valid for liver-referenced eligibility and quantitative metrics predicting treatment response, but the strongest evidence remains tied to Ga-68 PSMA-11. Tracer interchangeability rests on consensus, rather than companion-diagnostic trials. Future randomized intra-patient comparison could potentially establish whether tracer choice alters eligibility or predicts benefit, and whether thresholds are tracer specific.

title: Plasma metabolic signatures preceding incident type 2 diabetes mellitus: a prospective cohort study.
abstract: Purpose This study aimed to identify circulating plasma metabolic biomarkers associated with incident type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), construct a composite metabolic risk score (CMRS), and evaluate its incremental predictive utility beyond conventional clinical risk factors. Methods A total of 224,874 diabetes-free participants from the UK Biobank were randomly allocated into a derivation cohort (70%, N = 157,411) and a locked internal validation cohort (30%, N = 67,463). A two-stage feature selection framework combining regularized Elastic Net Cox regression with age- and sex-adjusted multivariable Cox models under Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) control was applied in the derivation cohort to build the CMRS. Incremental predictive capacity was evaluated in the validation cohort by comparing a comprehensive clinical base model incorporating baseline glucose, glycated hemoglobin (HbA 1c ), and lipid profiles with and without CMRS. Results During a median follow-up of 13.6 years, 12,150 incident T2DM cases occurred. A core signature of 52 nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) metabolites was identified. In the locked internal validation cohort (N = 67,463), continuous standardized CMRS was independently associated with incident T2DM (fully adjusted hazard ratio [HR] per 1-standard deviation [SD] increase = 1.71, 95% CI: 1.61-1.82, P < 0.001; subdistribution HR accounting for competing mortality = 1.70, 95% CI: 1.59-1.83, P < 0.001). Segmented linear regression identified an exploratory inflection threshold along the continuous standardized score at CMRS scaled = -​1.474 (95% CI: -​1.638 to -​1.309, P < 0.001), below which approximately 7.0% of the cohort resided, with risk slopes of β 1 = -0.141 below versus β 2 = +0.905 above the threshold. Adding CMRS to the fully adjusted clinical base model yielded modest discriminative gains, increasing Harrell's C-index from 0.8603 (95% CI: 0.8542-0.8665) to 0.8660 (95% CI: 0.8600-0.8719; ΔC = +​0.0056, P < 0.001) and 10-year time-dependent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) from 0.878 to 0.883 (ΔAUC = +​0.005, 95% CI: 0.004-0.007, paired bootstrap P < 0.001). In 1000-iteration nested bootstrap internal validation, model optimism was negligible (optimism-corrected C-index = 0.8674). Although continuous Net Reclassification Improvement (NRI = 30.55%, 95% CI: 27.21%-33.89%, P < 0.001) and Integrated Discrimination Improvement (IDI = 0.859%, 95% CI: 0.751%-0.967%, P < 0.001) metrics showed statistical gains, overall incremental prognostic impact was modest, accompanied by a 10-year Brier score error reduction from 0.0298 to 0.0295 (index of prediction accuracy improvement [ΔIPA] = +​0.82%). Conclusions The 52-metabolite CMRS is independently associated with incident T2DM and provides modest incremental predictive discrimination and precision beyond comprehensive clinical models incorporating standard glycemic and lipid measures.

title: Latent Representation Learning from 3D Brain MRI for Latent Analysis and Prediction in Multiple Sclerosis.
abstract: Background Neurological diseases can lead to significant cognitive impairment. Linking magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-derived measures of brain structure with clinical assessments of cognitive function remains challenging, as conventional statistical methods and traditional machine learning approaches may struggle to capture complex relationships between brain structure and cognitive outcomes, hindering the development of reliable imaging biomarkers. Although deep learning methods offer greater predictive capabilities, their black-box nature limits interpretability, posing a major obstacle to clinical translation. New method Latent representation learning via generative models can provide informative representations and support deeper analysis and cognitive biomarker prediction. While standard generative adversarial networks and diffusion models primarily focus on generating images from random noise, variational autoencoders offer compact, probabilistic latent representations that are well suited for downstream tasks. In this study, we propose InfoVAE-Med3D, an adaptation of the InfoVAE framework for three-dimensional brain ​MRI to learn informative latent representations. By explicitly relaxing the mutual information regularization penalty between inputs and latent representations, our method aims to capture richer information from input MRI data, facilitating the analysis of brain-related characteristics and downstream prediction. Results We evaluate InfoVAE-Med3D on two datasets: a healthy control dataset ([Formula: see text]) containing chronological age and sex information, and a Multiple Sclerosis (MS) dataset ([Formula: see text]) collected from the Multiple Sclerosis Center of the First Medical Faculty, Charles University, Prague, containing chronological age, sex, and Symbol Digit Modalities Test (SDMT) scores. The learned latent representations capture information related to sex and brain volumetric features, including grey and white matter volumes, as reflected in sex-related clustering and smooth transitions in brain volume measures in two-dimensional visualizations. Through comprehensive evaluations, we demonstrate that InfoVAE-Med3D learns more informative latent representations, especially when the mutual information regularization penalty is completely removed. In this setting, the model generally outperforms other variational autoencoder variants in both MRI reconstruction and prediction of brain age and SDMT scores using support vector regression, while remaining competitive with deep learning-based predictive models, particularly on the MS dataset. Conclusion InfoVAE-Med3D provides informative latent representations from brain MRI data of both healthy controls and patients with MS. By improving predictive performance and providing interpretable insights into the learned latent representations, the proposed framework offers a promising approach for advancing biomarker discovery and the analysis of cognitive impairment in neurological diseases, particularly ​MS.

title: Metabolomic Biomarkers in Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Haemorrhage: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Aneurysmal subarachnoid haemorrhage (aSAH) carries a mortality of approximately 40% and causes significant long-term disability. Delayed cerebral ischaemia (DCI) affects approximately 30% of survivors and is a major determinant of poor outcome, yet no validated biomarker exists for its early prediction. Metabolomics-high-throughput profiling of small-molecule metabolites-offers a window into early metabolic disruptions that precede structural injury, but no systematic review has synthesised this evidence. MEDLINE (PubMed), Scopus and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched from inception to 28 May 2026 following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020, including studies that applied metabolomic profiling (≥ 16 unique metabolites, or a validated untargeted nuclear magnetic resonance or mass spectrometry platform) to blood or cerebrospinal fluid in adult patients with aSAH and reported associations with DCI or functional outcomes. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data and assessed risk-of-bias using the Quality in Prognostic Studies (QUIPS) tool. Thirteen studies (733 patients; 2005-2026) were included. Four biological themes emerged-a systemic glycolytic shift with tricarboxylic acid cycle disruption; disruption of the arginine-nitric oxide axis, with plasma arginine depletion preceding DCI by 24-48 h (OR 0.22, 95% CI 0.08-0.55%); alterations in taurine and excitatory amino acid metabolism, with plasma taurine predicting good 90-day modified Rankin Scale outcome (OR 3.41, 95% CI 1.28-11.4%); and sphingolipid and oxylipin dysregulation-each mechanistically coherent with aSAH pathophysiology, though cross-study replication of specific metabolites is limited. A 20-metabolite panel predicted DCI with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.968. Risk-of-bias was high in 7 of 13 studies, and only 3 reported adjusted effect estimates. Metabolomics in aSAH is a growing but early-stage field: the evidence base is predominantly exploratory, with most metabolites reported in single cohorts only. Plasma arginine and taurine have the strongest adjusted evidence. Prospective multi-centre studies with standardised protocols, adjusted analyses and external validation are required before clinical implementation.

title: From Radical Resection to Organ Preservation in Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer: A Narrative Review of Risk-Adapted Management.
abstract: Purpose To synthesise evidence informing risk-adapted treatment and organ preservation in locally advanced rectal cancer. Methods This narrative review used targeted English-language searches of PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library through 31 March 2026, supplemented by targeted source verification in September 2026. Results Magnetic resonance imaging, mismatch repair status, recurrence risk, and patient preferences inform treatment selection. Total neoadjuvant therapy is established for higher-risk mismatch repair-proficient/microsatellite-stable disease. Chemoradiation followed by consolidation chemotherapy can improve organ-preservation probability compared with induction sequencing, without a demonstrated disease-free survival advantage. Selected lower-risk surgical candidates may receive chemotherapy with selective chemoradiation. Both short-course radiotherapy and long-course chemoradiation remain evidence-based options; the long-term locoregional failure signal in RAPIDO cannot be attributed to fractionation alone. Watch-and-wait requires multimodal confirmation of clinical complete response, intensive surveillance, and access to salvage surgery; oncological equivalence to immediate resection is unproven. Prospective dostarlimab data support non-operative management in selected mismatch repair-deficient rectal cancers, while long-term durability requires further evaluation. Conclusion Management should integrate tumour anatomy, biology, treatment response, and patient priorities. Organ preservation requires careful selection and structured follow-up, with treatment intensity individualised rather than applied uniformly.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Gallbladder Carcinoma: A Review of Research Studies and Clinical Evidence.
abstract: Background Gallbladder carcinoma (GBC) is the most common biliary tract malignancy and is usually diagnosed at an advanced stage. Artificial intelligence (AI), including radiomics, machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), is increasingly applied to its diagnosis, surgical management and prognostication, but how far the reported performance can be trusted is unclear. Methods PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library and Google Scholar were searched to 5 May 2026 using database-specific search strategies. Each primary prediction-model study was characterized separately by design, number of centers and validation type (internal, temporal or external). Results Of 31 primary AI studies in GBC, 29 were retrospective, 22 were single-center and 24 reported internal validation only. In independent test or external cohorts, DL and ML models discriminated benign from malignant gallbladder lesions with areas under the curve (AUCs) of approximately 0.80-0.89; a multicenter model distinguishing xanthogranulomatous cholecystitis from GBC achieved an external AUC of 0.88, and automated computed tomography (CT) segmentation an external Dice score of 0.76. The best recurrence model achieved an AUC of 0.76 on internal (random-split) validation; none of the reviewed prognostic models reported a quantified external-validation estimate. Intraoperative AI is technically feasible but has no outcome data, and federated learning has been tested only in simulation. Conclusion AI could plausibly assist several steps of GBC care, but the evidence is dominated by retrospective, single-center, internally validated studies from Asia, and metrics from different studies are not directly comparable. originalAbstract:
Background

Gallbladder carcinoma (GBC) is the most common biliary tract malignancy and is usually diagnosed at an advanced stage. Artificial intelligence (AI), including radiomics, machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), is increasingly applied to its diagnosis, surgical management and prognostication, but how far the reported performance can be trusted is unclear.

Methods

PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library and Google Scholar were searched to 5 May 2026 using database-specific search strategies. Each primary prediction-model study was characterized separately by design, number of centers and validation type (internal, temporal or external).

Results

Of 31 primary AI studies in GBC, 29 were retrospective, 22 were single-center and 24 reported internal validation only. In independent test or external cohorts, DL and ML models discriminated benign from malignant gallbladder lesions with areas under the curve (AUCs) of approximately 0.80-0.89; a multicenter model distinguishing xanthogranulomatous cholecystitis from GBC achieved an external AUC of 0.88, and automated computed tomography (CT) segmentation an external Dice score of 0.76. The best recurrence model achieved an AUC of 0.76 on internal (random-split) validation; none of the reviewed prognostic models reported a quantified external-validation estimate. Intraoperative AI is technically feasible but has no outcome data, and federated learning has been tested only in simulation.

Conclusion

AI could plausibly assist several steps of GBC care, but the evidence is dominated by retrospective, single-center, internally validated studies from Asia, and metrics from different studies are not directly comparable. Prospective multicenter external validation, shared annotated datasets and standardized reporting are required before clinical adoption.

title: Postoperative ctDNA in Resectable Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma: From Molecular Residual Disease Detection Toward Risk-Adapted Adjuvant Therapy and Surveillance.
abstract: Background Postoperative circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) is emerging as a marker of molecular residual disease (MRD) after curative-intent treatment for esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). This review evaluates its ability to refine recurrence-risk assessment beyond pathological response and its potential role in guiding adjuvant therapy and surveillance. Methods A structured narrative review of studies evaluating perioperative and postoperative ctDNA in resectable ESCC was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE through August 17, 2026, supplemented by citation tracking and clinical trial registry searches. Evidence was synthesized across treatment pathways, assay platforms, and postoperative management settings. Results Across ESCC cohorts using digital PCR, fixed next-generation sequencing panels, and personalized tumor-informed assays, postoperative ctDNA positivity consistently identifies patients at increased risk of recurrence, although estimates remain imprecise in small cohorts. Serial testing can detect molecular relapse months before radiographic recurrence. Integrated pathology-MRD models demonstrate additional risk stratification within both pathological complete response and non-completeresponse groups. Observational findings suggest, but do not establish, that MRD-positive patients may derive greater benefit from adjuvant immunotherapy. Conversely, MRD negativity alone does not justify omission of indicated adjuvant treatment. Conclusions Postoperative ctDNA provides complementary molecular risk information beyond conventional pathology in resectable ESCC. However, prospective MRD-guided trials are required before postoperative treatment or surveillance strategies can be routinely modified on the basis of ctDNA results alone.

title: Prognostic Value of Pre- and Post-Treatment PET-CT Metrics After Definitive Chemoradiation for Anal Canal Cancer.
abstract: Purpose Although post-treatment FDG-PET/CT is frequently obtained following definitive chemoradiation (CRT) for locally advanced anal canal cancer (LAACC), its prognostic utility remains uncertain. We hypothesized that quantitative PET/CT metrics would be associated with overall survival (OS) and that pre-treatment metabolic parameters would provide greater prognostic information than post-treatment metabolic response. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients with LAACC who underwent definitive CRT and both pre-treatment and post-treatment fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) PET/CT. Quantitative PET metrics were extracted, including mean SUL, total lesion glycolysis (TLG), metabolic tumor volume (MTV), maximum SUL, and peak SUL. OS was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method. Associations between PET-derived variables and OS were evaluated using univariable Cox proportional hazards regression, with optimal cutoffs identified using maximally selected rank statistics (MaxStat). Results Forty-five patients were included (median age 57.7 years), with post-treatment PET/CT performed at a median of 4.4 months following CRT. Lean body mass (HR 3.10, 95% CI 1.01-9.50; p = 0.049) and pre-treatment primary tumor mean SUL (HR 4.93, 95% CI 1.40-17.37; p = 0.013), size (HR 4.01, 95% CI 1.22-13.17; p = 0.022), TLG (HR 3.68, 95% CI 1.11-12.14; p = 0.033), and peak SUL (HR 3.31, 95% CI 1.02-10.72; p = 0.046) were associated with OS in exploratory univariable analyses. Post-treatment, higher weight (HR 4.94, 95% CI 1.06-22.96; p=0.041; cutoff 60.42 kg; N=45) and lean body mass (HR 4.82, 95% CI 1.06-21.90; p=0.042; cutoff 44.50 kg; N=44) were associated with worse OS. No post-treatment PET-derived metabolic parameters met the nominal threshold for statistical significance. Among patients with higher baseline metabolic activity, greater reduction in mean SUL following CRT demonstrated a nonsignificant trend toward improved OS. Conclusion Pre-treatment FDG-PET/CT metabolic parameters demonstrated stronger associations with OS than post-treatment metabolic parameters in this exploratory cohort. Baseline tumor metabolic activity may provide useful prognostic information in patients with LAACC, warranting validation in larger prospective studies.

title: The prognostic value of sequential PSMA-PET/CT in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer: a study of response assessment in patients receiving systemic therapy and cytoreductive prostatectomy.
abstract: Metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC) carries inferior prognosis. Although incorporating cytoreductive radical prostatectomy (cRP) into systemic therapy is safe, patient outcomes are variable. Prostate-specific membrane antigen positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PSMA-PET/CT) demonstrates superior lesion detection compared to conventional imaging, yet its role in serial monitoring for mHSPC remains undefined. This study prospectively enrolled 48 men with PSMA-PET/CT-confirmed mHSPC to evaluate sequential imaging for response assessment and prognostication. Patients received six cycles of androgen deprivation therapy with novel hormonal agents ± docetaxel, followed by optional cRP. PSMA-PET/CT, multiparametric MRI, and PSA were obtained at baseline, post-systemic therapy, and six weeks after cRP. Blinded reviewers assessed imaging response using RECIST 1.1 and EAU/EANM criteria, while pathological response and biochemical status were independently evaluated. Following systemic therapy, both primary and metastatic lesion SUVmax decreased significantly (from 18.15 to 4.05 and 13.95 to 3.93, respectively; both P < 0.0001), while ADC values increased (0.725 to 0.955 × 10 - 3 mm 2 /s; P < 0.0001). EAU/EANM response classifications (7 complete, 31 partial, 10 stable/progressive disease) correlated strongly with RECIST (Spearman's R = 0.79, P < 0.0001) but weakly with post-therapy PSA. Notably, PSMA identified residual disease missed by conventional imaging in nine discordant cases. Among 25 patients undergoing cRP, six (24%) achieved favorable pathological response, with significantly lower post-therapy primary SUVmax (2.400 vs. 4.800, P = 0.047). The average SUVmax of metastatic lesions after systemic therapy was a strong predictor of detectable PSA following cRP (OR = 1.640, 95%CI = 1.214-2.995, P = 0.019, AUC-ROC of 0.965). These findings underscore the value of sequential PSMA-PET/CT for monitoring therapeutic response and informing treatment decisions in mHSPC.

title: Deciphering intratumoral heterogeneity: An interpretable radiopathologic framework for lymph node staging in early-stage cervical cancer.
abstract: Preoperative assessment of lymph node metastasis (LNM) informs treatment planning in early-stage cervical cancer (CC). Traditional radiomics (TR) may obscure intratumoral heterogeneity. We developed multiparametric MRI habitat radiomics (HR) for LNM prediction and explored its histopathologic context. Patients underwent radical surgery and lymphadenectomy. Part I comprised 148 training and 63 test patients; Part II comprised 14 for spatially matched histopathology. Intratumoral voxels were clustered into habitats by K-means using T2-weighted imaging (T2WI), diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), and contrast-enhanced T1-weighted imaging (CE-T1WI) signals. The number of habitats was selected using validation AUC. HR/TR scores and clinical-radiological predictors were integrated by logistic regression. AUC and accuracy were compared by DeLong's and χ² tests. Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) assessed contributions. Subregion-matched histopathology quantified Ki-67, CD3, CD31, and tumor-stroma ratio (TSR). LNM prevalence was 27.1% (61/225). The four-habitat HR model achieved a test AUC of 0.841 with 14 DWI/CE-T1WI-derived features. Test AUCs for clinical model (CL), TR, and HR + CL were 0.804, 0.784, and 0.890. HR + TR+CL achieved the highest AUC (0.902) and accuracy (87.30%), without a significant AUC difference from HR + CL (P = 0.277). SHAP ranked HR score above clinical lymph-node status, tumor diameter, and TR score. HR-3 exhibited highest Ki67 and lowest TSR, CD3, and CD31; HR-1 had highest TSR and lowest Ki67; HR-2 showed higher CD31 than HR-4. MRI-based HR may support preoperative LNM assessment in early-stage CC, with HR + CL representing a parsimonious candidate model for further evaluation. Spatially matched exploratory histopathology suggests possible regional tissue differences across MRI-defined habitats.

title: Proteomic and Metabolomic Profiling in Moyamoya Disease: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Moyamoya disease (MMD) is a progressive cerebrovascular disorder characterized by stenosis and occlusion of the internal carotid artery branches, leading to chronic ischemia and aberrant collateral vessel formation. Despite its clinical significance, the pathophysiology is not fully understood, and identification of MMD-related biomarkers may supplement invasive digital subtraction angiography, the current gold standard for diagnosis, as well as provide additional insights into prognosis and disease progression. High-throughput metabolomics and proteomics offer potential to elucidate disease mechanisms and identify diagnostic markers. Our goal is to systematically review the current literature on metabolomics and proteomics in MMD using high-throughput methods, identify candidate biomarkers, characterize implicated pathways, and assess the diagnostic and prognostic value of molecular signatures. We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus databases through April 13, 2026, for studies analyzing serum or CSF from MMD patients using mass spectrometry, nuclear magnetic resonance, or immunoassays. Studies were included if they employed case-control, cohort, cross-sectional, or RCT designs in human subjects. Two reviewers independently screened titles, abstracts, and full texts, with disputes resolved by a third reviewer. Quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. We extracted the top differentially expressed proteins or metabolites, results of any enrichment pathway analyses, and demographics information from each study. From 3071 studies identified, 31 were included after removing 1558 duplicates and excluding 1482 irrelevant studies. Recurrent differentially expressed proteins implicated inflammatory signaling (CRABP-I, PDGF-BB, IL-7, complement proteins), angiogenesis (VEGF, Ang-2, MMP-9), and cytoskeletal remodeling (FLNA, ZYX, keratins), while consistent metabolomic signatures highlighted BCAA elevation, urea cycle disruption, and lipid remodeling. Pathway analyses recurrently implicated immune activation, endothelial dysfunction, cytoskeletal reorganization, hypoxia signaling, and metabolic reprogramming. Demographically, cohorts were predominantly adult, East Asian, and bilateral MMD, with a sample-size-weighted mean age of 40.0 years. High-throughput proteomics and metabolomics identified recurring molecular alterations in Moyamoya disease, commonly identifying inflammatory signaling, pathological angiogenesis, and cytoskeletal remodeling as potential pathophysiological mechanisms. Despite predominantly good-quality studies (mean Newcastle-Ottawa Scale 6.77 ± 0.67), major limitations included small sample sizes, single-center designs, and regional specificity. Validation in larger, ethnically diverse, multicenter cohorts is essential before clinical translation of candidate biomarkers and therapeutic targets.
originalAbstract: Moyamoya disease (MMD) is a progressive cerebrovascular disorder characterized by stenosis and occlusion of the internal carotid artery branches, leading to chronic ischemia and aberrant collateral vessel formation. Despite its clinical significance, the pathophysiology is not fully understood, and identification of MMD-related biomarkers may supplement invasive digital subtraction angiography, the current gold standard for diagnosis, as well as provide additional insights into prognosis and disease progression. High-throughput metabolomics and proteomics offer potential to elucidate disease mechanisms and identify diagnostic markers. Our goal is to systematically review the current literature on metabolomics and proteomics in MMD using high-throughput methods, identify candidate biomarkers, characterize implicated pathways, and assess the diagnostic and prognostic value of molecular signatures. We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus databases through April 13, 2026, for studies analyzing serum or CSF from MMD patients using mass spectrometry, nuclear magnetic resonance, or immunoassays. Studies were included if they employed case-control, cohort, cross-sectional, or RCT designs in human subjects. Two reviewers independently screened titles, abstracts, and full texts, with disputes resolved by a third reviewer. Quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. We extracted the top differentially expressed proteins or metabolites, results of any enrichment pathway analyses, and demographics information from each study. From 3071 studies identified, 31 were included after removing 1558 duplicates and excluding 1482 irrelevant studies. Recurrent differentially expressed proteins implicated inflammatory signaling (CRABP-I, PDGF-BB, IL-7, complement proteins), angiogenesis (VEGF, Ang-2, MMP-9), and cytoskeletal remodeling (FLNA, ZYX, keratins), while consistent metabolomic signatures highlighted BCAA elevation, urea cycle disruption, and lipid remodeling. Pathway analyses recurrently implicated immune activation, endothelial dysfunction, cytoskeletal reorganization, hypoxia signaling, and metabolic reprogramming. Demographically, cohorts were predominantly adult, East Asian, and bilateral MMD, with a sample-size-weighted mean age of 40.0 years. High-throughput proteomics and metabolomics identified recurring molecular alterations in Moyamoya disease, commonly identifying inflammatory signaling, pathological angiogenesis, and cytoskeletal remodeling as potential pathophysiological mechanisms. Despite predominantly good-quality studies (mean Newcastle-Ottawa Scale 6.77 ± 0.67), major limitations included small sample sizes, single-center designs, and regional specificity. Validation in larger, ethnically diverse, multicenter cohorts is essential before clinical translation of candidate biomarkers and therapeutic targets.

title: Illuminating the future: energy-based focal therapies for prostate cancer.
abstract: Energy-based focal therapy is an image-guided, organ-preserving strategy intended to ablate clinically significant prostate cancer while limiting treatment-related injury to surrounding structures. This review critically examines high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU), cryoablation, irreversible electroporation (IRE), vascular-targeted photodynamic therapy (VTP), focal laser ablation (FLA), histotripsy, and electrochemotherapy (ECT), with emphasis on mechanisms, treatment planning, patient selection, oncological control, functional outcomes, and translational readiness. Multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI), combined with targeted and systematic biopsy, is central to defining disease extent and assessing treatment response. Although prospective cohorts report encouraging medium-term outcomes for several established modalities, variation in eligibility criteria, ablation margins, surveillance protocols, biopsy requirements, and failure definitions limits cross-modality comparisons. Randomized evidence for padeliporfin-based photodynamic therapy demonstrates disease modification relative to active surveillance in selected men with low-risk disease, but does not establish equivalence to radical prostatectomy or radiotherapy. Residual and out-of-field cancer, repeat treatment, and the scarcity of long-term comparative data remain limitations. Radiomics, artificial intelligence, and molecular biomarkers, including DNA-repair and androgen-receptor alterations, may improve risk stratification and treatment personalization; however, their clinical utility requires external validation, reproducible workflows, and governance. Integration with systemic therapy, radiotherapy, or immunotherapy remains investigational, and evidence from advanced disease should not be extrapolated directly to localized cancer. Histotripsy and ECT require further prostate-specific clinical validation. Responsible implementation depends on multidisciplinary selection, transparent counseling, standardized oncological and patient-reported endpoints, prospective trials or registries, and predefined surveillance and salvage pathways. Focal therapy should therefore be regarded as a selective, evidence-developing treatment strategy rather than an established substitute for definitive whole-gland treatment.

title: Prognostic value of integrated dynamic NLR and [ 18 F]FDG-PET/CT parameters in resectable non-small cell lung cancer treated with neoadjuvant immunotherapy plus chemotherapy.
abstract: Objective This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic value of dynamic [ 18 F]FDG PET/CT metabolic parameters and the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), individually and in combination, in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) receiving neoadjuvant immunotherapy plus chemotherapy. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 168 NSCLC patients treated with neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy followed by surgery. Pre- and post-treatment PET metabolic parameters assessed by iPERCIST and peripheral blood NLR were collected. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis and Kaplan-Meier survival analysis with Cox regression were performed to identify predictors of disease-free survival (DFS). Results During a median follow-up of 25.2 months (95% CI, 21.0-29.3 months), 59 patients experienced recurrence. Post-treatment PET metabolic parameters, their changes, and post-treatment NLR were significantly associated with DFS. Among these parameters, ΔSUVmax and post-treatment NLR were identified as independent prognostic factors. Patients were stratified into three risk groups according to the combination of ΔSUVmax and post-treatment NLR, with significantly different DFS outcomes among groups (p = 0.001). Patients achieving iCMR/iPMR according to iPERCIST criteria showed longer DFS than those without favorable metabolic response (p = 0.005) . Conclusions Dynamic PET metabolic parameters, and post-treatment NLR hold significant prognostic value following neoadjuvant immunotherapy plus chemotherapy in NSCLC. A combined model integrating PET metabolic parameters and post-treatment NLR stratified patients into distinct risk groups, suggesting potential utility in postoperative risk assessment.

title: <sup>99m</sup>Tc-DTPA orbital SPECT/CT in thyroid-associated ophthalmopathy: current evidence and emerging applications.
abstract: Thyroid-associated ophthalmopathy (TAO), an autoimmune inflammatory disease of the orbit, requires objective assessment of disease activity and severity to guide management. The Clinical Activity Score (CAS) is widely used for this purpose, but its reliability is limited by subjectivity and interobserver variability, and conventional structural imaging cannot reliably distinguish early inflammation from fibrotic remodeling. Orbital single-photon emission computed tomography/computed tomography (SPECT/CT) using 99mTc-DTPA-a small hydrophilic tracer that extravasates in proportion to inflammation-induced microvascular permeability-provides a noninvasive means of visualizing and quantifying orbital inflammatory activity. This review summarizes the imaging principles and quantitative methods of orbital SPECT/CT, from semi-quantitative uptake ratios to corrected SUVmax-based absolute quantification and multiparametric models, and critically appraises the evidence for its clinical applications in TAO activity stratification, prediction of glucocorticoid response, and longitudinal treatment monitoring. Emerging applications, including SPECT/CT radiomics with external validation and artificial intelligence-based image analysis, are also discussed. Throughout, established evidence is distinguished from exploratory applications that require prospective validation, providing a balanced basis for the further evaluation and potential clinical incorporation of orbital SPECT/CT in individualized TAO management.

title: Monte Carlo-based three-dimensional dose evaluation for rotational cerebral angiography: peak dose to brain and skin and Dose-Volume Histogram (DVH) analysis of the brain.
abstract: Background and purpose Rotational cerebral angiography produces complex, nonuniform dose distributions; the mean brain dose may not sufficiently represent localized high-dose regions. This study aimed to visualize three-dimensional dose distributions in the brain and skin using PHITS, estimate peak brain dose (PBD) and peak skin dose (PSD), and evaluate the brain dose distribution using dose-volume histogram (DVH) analysis. Materials and methods X-ray spectra for 3D digital subtraction angiography (3D-DSA, 70 kV) and cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT, 109 kV) were generated using SpekPy and implemented in PHITS. A rotational irradiation model covering approximately 200° was constructed using a multisource approach based on projection-dependent tube current-time product values. The model was validated using a PMMA phantom. Three-dimensional dose distributions were calculated using the adult male mesh-type reference computational phantom; PBD, PSD, and brain DVH indices were evaluated. Results Calculated doses agreed with measured values within 5.2%. Dose concentrations were mainly observed in the occipital region. The PBD and PSD were 25.1 and 44.1 mGy for 3D-DSA and 101.3 and 139.1 mGy for CBCT, respectively. The PBD was 3.3 times higher than the mean brain dose for 3D-DSA and 2.3 times higher for CBCT. DVH analysis showed that CBCT shifted the brain-dose distribution toward higher-dose regions, with D10% values of 14.9 and 70.0 mGy for 3D-DSA and CBCT, respectively. Conclusions PHITS-based three-dimensional dose evaluation allowed localized high-dose regions in the brain and skin to be visualized and quantified. DVH analysis complemented the peak dose assessment by providing volumetric information on the brain-dose distribution.

title: Localisation and classification of preselected thyroid ultrasound nodules: cross-cohort performance of a public-dataset model with limited local data.
abstract: Public-dataset models are rarely characterised on local data. A YOLOv8m model trained on the fine-needle-aspiration-labelled public TN5000 thyroid ultrasound dataset was tested on two independent cohorts. Images were cropped to a preselected nodule. Mean average precision at intersection-over-union 0.5 (mAP@0.5) fell from 0.825 on TN5000 to 0.415 on the Stanford Artificial Intelligence in Medicine and Imaging (AIMI) cohort and 0.420 on the institutional cohort, indicating domain shift. Stepwise fine-tuning raised institutional mAP@0.5 to 0.630 (95% confidence interval, CI, 0.525-0.730) but degraded TN5000 performance to 0.323-0.421, indicating catastrophic forgetting; single-stage mixed retraining reached 0.611 (0.521-0.716) and 0.788-0.819 on TN5000 up to a 40% institutional proportion. Training each selected configuration three times gave standard deviations of 0.057 and 0.069, larger than any difference between adjacent fine-tuning sizes, and neither repeat of the 30% mixed model was separable from the baseline, so no configuration is identified as best. After multiplicity correction the only separable adjacent step was a decline, from 40% to 50% institutional data. Lesion-level detection exceeded 0.90 sensitivity at about one false positive per imaging study, but discrimination of the cytology-defined malignant class was weak (end-to-end area under the receiver operating characteristic curve 0.701, 95% CI 0.610-0.780), and its gain over the baseline did not survive multiplicity correction (adjusted p = 0.059). Positive predictive value was 0.19 to 0.24 at 10% prevalence. Under the training design evaluated, mixed public-plus-local training retained source-domain performance better than fine-tuning; these retrospective, exploratory findings do not establish clinical readiness.

title: Quantitative assessment of diaphragmatic motion in COPD using pixel-wise optical flow analysis of cine MRI.
abstract: Diaphragmatic dysfunction is a key determinant of dyspnea and impaired respiratory mechanics in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD); however, objective quantification remains limited. This study quantitatively assessed diaphragmatic motion in COPD using pixel-wise optical flow analysis of sagittal cine magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Sagittal cine MRI of the right hemidiaphragm during quiet breathing was performed in 35 patients with COPD and 9 healthy participants. Optical flow was computed within the diaphragmatic region of interest after semiautomatic segmentation. Three indices were derived during expiration: the direction agreement ratio (DAR; proportion of pixels showing upward motion), the proportion of motionless areas (PMA), and mean diaphragmatic velocity (MDV). These indices were compared between patients with COPD and healthy participants across Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD) stages and were stratified by the presence of visually assessed paradoxical motion. Pulmonary function associations were evaluated. Compared with healthy participants, patients with COPD showed a lower DAR, higher PMA, and reduced MDV (all p < 0.001). The DAR decreased and the PMA increased with advancing GOLD stages. Patients with paradoxical motion exhibited a lower DAR and higher PMA than those without paradoxical motion. DAR and PMA were correlated with FEV 1 %pred (ρ = 0.71 and - 0.71, respectively), whereas MDV correlated negatively with RV %pred (ρ = - 0.79). Pixel-wise optical flow analysis using cine MRI provides a potential quantitative framework for evaluating diaphragmatic dysfunction in COPD by capturing synchrony, regional immobility, and motion velocity.

title: Directional dependence of MRI geometric distortion under different receiver bandwidths.
abstract: MRI residual geometric distortion compromises stereotactic body radiotherapy accuracy, but distortion magnitude, directional dependence, and bandwidth (BW) effects across individual units remain insufficiently understood. To evaluate the magnitude, spatial distribution, and directional characteristics of residual distortion across five clinical MRI units under multiple receiver-BW settings for unit-level quality assurance (QA). A 3D phantom was scanned on five 1.5T or 3T units (three vendors) at BWs of 200-1000 Hz/pixel with vendor 3D correction enabled. Absolute residual distortion and its x-, y-, and z-components were evaluated relative to isocenter. Whole-volume distortion generally decreased as BW increased, but was non-monotonic in central regions. Distortion increased with distance from isocenter, with dominant displacement axes (x-axis for Skyra, z-axis for Optima) differing among units. Residual distortion varies among individual units and is not fully characterized by BW alone, supporting unit-level geometric QA.

title: Metabolomic Analysis of Patients with Coronary Artery Disease and Acute Myocardial Infarction by Using Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy.
abstract: This cross-sectional exploratory study investigates the potential of metabolomics to differentiate between stable coronary artery disease (CAD) and acute myocardial infarction (AMI) through Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) spectroscopic analysis. The study identifies distinct metabolic profiles for each condition, revealing significant variations in metabolite levels, particularly lactic acid, which is a key metabolic product of anaerobic glycolysis, emerges as a prominent marker in AMI patients, reflecting acute ischemic stress and providing insight into adverse outcomes associated with high lactate levels. Another metabolite found in the present study was hypoxanthine, which is key biomarker for myocardial ischemia. These findings underscore the potential of metabolomics in combination with pathway analysis in distinguishing between CAD and AMI and highlight the metabolic dysregulation that occurs in these diseases. Our results suggest that these metabolites could serve as potential biomarkers, paving the way for personalized prognostic and diagnostic strategies. Further large-scale studies are necessary to validate these findings and incorporate them into clinical practice.
