title: Integrating Intratumoral and Peritumoral Features via a Cross-Attention Transformer on Super-resolution MRI for Glioblastoma Survival Risk Stratification: A Multicenter Study.
abstract: Rationale and objectives To develop and validate a Cross-Region Transformer using super-resolution (SR) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to integrate intratumoral and peritumoral features for overall survival (OS) prediction in glioblastoma. Materials and methods This multicenter study included 362 patients (training, n = 228; internal test, n = 57; external validation, n = 77). Preoperative contrast-enhanced T1-weighted and T2-weighted MRI underwent generative adversarial network-based SR reconstruction. Intratumoral and 10-mm peritumoral features were extracted using 2.5D convolutional neural networks and fused by asymmetric cross-attention to generate a deep learning-based risk score (DLRS), which was combined with independent clinical factors. Performance was evaluated using C-index, time-dependent receiver operating characteristic analysis, calibration, decision curve analysis, Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping, and SHapley Additive exPlanations. Results The Cross-Region Transformer achieved C-indices of 0.787 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.734-0.840), 0.711 (95% CI, 0.593-0.829), and 0.726 (95% CI, 0.627-0.826) in the training, internal test, and external validation cohorts, respectively, with numerically higher discrimination than single-region and feature-concatenation models. The combined clinical-DLRS model, incorporating the Stupp regimen, number of lesions, Ki-67 index, and DLRS, achieved corresponding C-indices of 0.836 (95% CI, 0.788-0.884), 0.742 (95% CI, 0.628-0.855), and 0.754 (95% CI, 0.658-0.850). The DLRS significantly stratified OS in external validation (median, 7.5 vs 23.5 months; P < 0.001). Interpretability analyses highlighted enhancing margins within the necrotic core and the intratumoral-peritumoral interface. Conclusion The Cross-Region Transformer integrates complementary intratumoral and peritumoral representations from SR MRI. The resulting interpretable DLRS supports noninvasive survival prediction and risk stratification in glioblastoma.

title: Automatic Ultrasound Habitat Radiomics for Differentiating Henoch-Schonlein Purpura Nephritis from IgA Nephropathy in Children: A Multicenter Study.
abstract: Rationale and objectives To assess a noninvasive ultrasound habitat radiomics approach with automatic kidney segmentation for distinguishing pediatric Henoch-Schonlein purpura nephritis (HSPN) from immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN). Materials and methods This retrospective multicenter study included 592 biopsy-confirmed pediatric patients from three centers (HSPN, n = 338; IgAN, n = 254). The development cohort (n = 453) was split into training (n = 362) and internal validation (n = 91) cohorts, and an independent external validation cohort (n = 139) was used for final testing. Kidney regions of interest were automatically segmented using nnU-Net. K-means clustering defined three echogenic habitat subregions, and 408 radiomics features were extracted from the whole-kidney region and habitat subregions. Feature selection was performed in the training cohort, and three machine-learning classifiers were evaluated. The selected radiomics model was compared with clinical and combined models. Results nnU-Net achieved high kidney segmentation performance, with a mean Dice similarity coefficient of 0.957 and a mean intersection over union of 0.918 in the independent healthy-child test set. Fifteen radiomics features were retained, including six whole-kidney features and nine habitat-derived features. Logistic regression showed stable performance, with areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of 0.806 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.715-0.897) internally and 0.825 (95% CI, 0.758-0.892) externally. The combined model outperformed the clinical model in AUC in both cohorts (0.846 vs 0.717; 0.805 vs 0.733). Conclusion This deep-learning-assisted ultrasound habitat radiomics approach enabled automatic kidney delineation and showed encouraging performance as a reproducible imaging adjunct for differentiating pediatric HSPN from IgAN.

title: Atrophy-Robust Multiclass CNN Segmentation of Brainstem-Related Structures in Neurodegenerative Parkinson Syndromes.
abstract: Rationale and objectives Neurodegenerative Parkinson syndromes show regionally distinct tissue loss involving several brainstem and midbrain structures. Reliable volumetry is constrained by atlas-based segmentation in atrophy-affected brains. We developed a multiclass convolutional neural network (CNN) for the segmentation of 16 brainstem-related regions on routine magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Materials and methods In this retrospective single-center study, 200 manually annotated MRI datasets of patients with Parkinson's disease, atypical Parkinson syndromes, and healthy controls were used for model development and validation. A Deep Neural Patchwork model was trained on 150 datasets and evaluated in an independent test cohort of 50 participants against atlas-based segmentation using the Dice coefficient, 95% Hausdorff distance, and average symmetric surface distances (ASSD). In an extended validation cohort of 264 participants, CNN-derived regional volumes were analyzed across Parkinson's disease, progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP), and multiple system atrophy (MSA). Results CNN segmentation outperformed atlas-based segmentation across accuracy metrics. Overall medians were 0.75 vs 0.33 for Dice, 2.0 vs 5.0 mm for 95% Hausdorff distance, and 0.30 vs 1.02 mm for ASSD. CNN-derived volumetry recapitulated established disease-associated patterns, including predominant mesencephalic, superior cerebellar peduncle, and red nucleus atrophy in PSP and more marked pontine and middle cerebellar peduncle volume loss in MSA. Conclusion The principal contribution of this study is an atrophy-robust multiclass brainstem segmentation framework. This framework may enable anatomically more faithful extraction of quantitative MRI metrics than atlas-based approaches and may reduce contamination from adjacent CSF spaces, particularly in small atrophy-affected structures.

title: Preoperative Prediction of Lymph Node Metastasis in Rectal Cancer Using Multimodal Magnetic Resonance Imaging Radiomics Combined with Clinical Risk Factors.
abstract: Rationale and objectives This study aimed to investigate the preoperative predictive value of multimodal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) radiomics combined with clinical risk factors for lymph node metastasis in rectal cancer, and to construct and validate an efficient and reproducible preoperative prediction model. Materials and methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on 129 patients with pathologically confirmed rectal cancer who underwent surgery at our hospital between 2017 and 2023. Preoperative pelvic T2-weighted imaging (T2WI), contrast-enhanced T1-weighted imaging (T1CE), and complete clinical data were collected. Three-dimensional regions of interest were manually segmented on the tumors using ITK-SNAP software, and radiomic features were selected via variance filtering and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. Patients were randomly divided into a training cohort (n = 90) and an internal validation cohort (n = 39) at a 7:3 ratio. Five Logistic regression prediction models were constructed: single-sequence radiomics, multimodal radiomics, multimodal radiomics combined with clinical risk factors, and clinical factors alone. Using postoperative pathology as the gold standard, the diagnostic performance of each model was evaluated by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy. Results The multimodal radiomics combined with clinical risk factors model demonstrated the best predictive performance, with an AUC of 0.885 (95% CI: 0.819-0.937), sensitivity of 85.3%, specificity of 82.1%, and accuracy of 83.6% in the internal validation cohort. Its performance was significantly superior to that of the single-sequence models, the multimodal radiomics model, and the clinical model alone (all P < 0.05). Entropy from T2WI, peak enhancement from T1CE, tumor volume, tumor size, carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA), and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) were identified as independent predictors of lymph node metastasis. Calibration curves and decision curve analysis confirmed that the model was well-calibrated and provided substantial net clinical benefit. Conclusion Integrating multimodal MRI radiomics from T2WI and T1CE with clinical indicators such as CEA and NLR significantly improves the preoperative prediction of lymph node metastasis in rectal cancer, demonstrating promising clinical applicability. However, as this was a single-center retrospective study, further multicenter, large-sample external validation is warranted to confirm the stability and generalizability of the model.

Using postoperative pathology as the gold standard, the diagnostic performance of each model was evaluated by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy.

Results

The multimodal radiomics combined with clinical risk factors model demonstrated the best predictive performance, with an AUC of 0.885 (95% CI: 0.819-0.937), sensitivity of 85.3%, specificity of 82.1%, and accuracy of 83.6% in the internal validation cohort. Its performance was significantly superior to that of the single-sequence models, the multimodal radiomics model, and the clinical model alone (all P < 0.05). Entropy from T2WI, peak enhancement from T1CE, tumor volume, tumor size, carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA), and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) were identified as independent predictors of lymph node metastasis. Calibration curves and decision curve analysis confirmed that the model was well-calibrated and provided substantial net clinical benefit.

Conclusion

Integrating multimodal MRI radiomics from T2WI and T1CE with clinical indicators such as CEA and NLR significantly improves the preoperative prediction of lymph node metastasis in rectal cancer, demonstrating promising clinical applicability. However, as this was a single-center retrospective study, further multicenter, large-sample external validation is warranted to confirm the stability and generalizability of the model.

title: Intelligent Prediction of WHO/ISUP Grade in Clear-Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma Using CT-Based Fusion Delta Features: A Multicenter Study with Biological Interpretability Exploration.
abstract: Rationale and objectives Our study aimed to develop a delta deep learning radiomics model for predicting World Health Organization/International Society of Urological Pathology (WHO/ISUP) grade in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) and to find relevant biomarkers and explore the potential biological mechanisms. Material and methods This multicenter cohort of 754 patients with ccRCC from five hospitals was split into training and internal validation cohorts in a 7:3 ratio, along with an external validation cohort (n=221) from three other hospitals. Radiomics and deep learning features were extracted from the tumor regions on multiphase contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT). Delta features were calculated as the absolute differences between features from different imaging phases. The selected features were used to develop delta deep learning radiomics signatures using different classifiers. The diagnostic performance in each model was assessed. Furthermore, gene expression profiling was conducted to for exploratory analysis of biological correlates associated with the model's grade predictions. Results The delta model achieved AUCs of 0.736 (95% CI 0.671-0.801) and 0.701 (95% CI 0.635-0.768) in the internal and external validation cohorts, respectively, which were numerically higher than those of the original model based on traditional deep learning radiomics features and demographic baseline clinical model. Additionally, the delta model demonstrated good calibration and a higher net benefit. Bioinformatics and multiomics analysis revealed that high-grade risk-related differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were associated with inflammation-related pathways, providing preliminary exploratory biological insights into the model's predictions. Conclusion The delta model demonstrated promising performance in WHO/ISUP grade. DEGs in predicted high-grade ccRCC were associated with inflammation-related pathways.

title: Static and Dynamic Functional Connectivity Alterations of Medial and Lateral Entorhinal Cortex with Subjective Cognitive Decline.
abstract: Rationale and objectives Entorhinal cortex (EC), which is vulnerable in Alzheimer's disease (AD), comprises the medial (MEC) and lateral (LEC) regions encoding spatial navigation and olfactory information, respectively. However, it remains unclear whether static functional connectivity (sFC) and dynamic functional connectivity (dFC) of MEC and LEC are altered in subjective cognitive decline (SCD), a preclinical stage of AD, and how these changes relate to these functions. This study aims to explore the alterations in the sFC and dFC of LEC and MEC with the whole brain in the SCD population, and further to assess the relationships of these connectivity changes with olfactory and spatial navigation functions. Materials and methods We conducted neuropsychological evaluations, resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging, spatial navigation, and olfactory assessment in 77 healthy controls (HCs) and 106 individuals with SCD. Bilateral MEC and LEC were defined as separate seed regions to calculate their sFC and dFC with all other voxels in the brain. Nested cross-validation classification analysis was applied to evaluate the classification efficacy for distinguishing SCD from HC. Results SCD individuals exhibited decreased sFC between MEC/LEC and widespread brain regions, primarily within the visual, sensory motor, and default mode network. The dFC between the left MEC and right putamen, and between the right MEC and right middle temporal gyrus increased, while decreased dFC was observed between the right LEC and right triangular part of inferior frontal gyrus. The connectivity between the LEC and visual network was significantly correlated with the olfactory recognition function. The predictive model combining sFC and dFC features from bilateral MEC and LEC achieved an area under the curve of 0.863. Conclusion This study revealed that sFC and dFC alterations of MEC/LEC have occurred at the SCD stage, and these changes are correlated with spatial navigation and olfactory performance, demonstrating their potential as biomarkers for identifying individuals at risk for AD.

title: Imaging Subphenotypes of Thoracic Involvement in IgG4-Related Disease: A Latent Class Analysis.
abstract: Rationale and objectives Thoracic manifestations of IgG4-related disease (IgG4-RD) are heterogeneous. We aimed to identify distinct imaging subphenotypes using latent class analysis (LCA) of chest computed tomography (CT) features and assess their associations with clinical characteristics, radiologic outcomes, and relapse risk. Materials and methods We retrospectively included patients with IgG4-RD and CT-confirmed thoracic involvement. Baseline chest CT findings were independently assessed by two thoracic radiologists. LCA of binary CT features was performed to identify imaging subphenotypes. Clinical and serologic characteristics, extrathoracic involvement, radiologic outcomes, and relapse-free survival were compared across subphenotypes. Cox regression analyses were used to identify factors independently associated with relapse. Results Among 231 patients, bronchovascular bundle thickening was the most frequent CT finding (56.7%). LCA identified five imaging subphenotypes: bronchovascular bundle-lymph node (BVB-LN, 38.5%), nodular (13.9%), interstitial (13.0%), mediastinal-pleural (18.6%), and mixed (16.0%). These subphenotypes differed in age, respiratory symptoms, extrathoracic involvement, and immunologic profiles. The interstitial subphenotype had the lowest radiologic improvement rate (41.7%) and highest progression rate (37.5%). The mixed (hazard ratio [HR], 3.821; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.336-10.923; P = 0.012) and BVB-LN (HR, 2.804; 95% CI, 1.062-7.399; P = 0.037) subphenotypes were independently associated with higher relapse risk, whereas combined glucocorticoid and immunosuppressant therapy was associated with lower relapse risk (HR, 0.405; 95% CI, 0.223-0.735; P = 0.003). Conclusion In this single-center cohort, LCA identified five thoracic imaging subphenotypes of IgG4-RD with specific clinical profiles, radiologic outcomes, and relapse risk. External validation is required before broader generalization or adoption as a standard classification framework.

title: Impact of Image Bit Depth Reduction on Deep Learning Performance in Chest Radiograph Analysis: A Multi-institutional Study.
abstract: Rationale and objectives Medical imaging typically generates 12-bit to 16-bit formats, yet conversion to 8-bit is often required. While deep learning has been widely explored in medical imaging, the influence of image bit depth on model performance is not fully understood. This study evaluates the impact of conversion from 16-bit to 8-bit for sex, age, and obesity classification using deep learning. Materials and methods In this retrospective, multi-institutional study, we analyzed 100,002 chest radiographs from 48,047 participants across three institutions. Images were uniformly quantized from the fixed 0-65535 range to 256 levels (0-255) with no additional processing. Three convolutional neural network architectures (ResNet52, EfficientNetB2, and ConvNeXtSmall) were trained on both 16-bit and 8-bit versions of the images. Model performance was evaluated using internal test datasets, randomly split multiple times, and an external test dataset. Statistical analysis included paired comparisons of area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) values, with Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons. Results Across all architectures and classification tasks, differences between 16-bit and 8-bit model performance were minimal (mean differences ranging from -0.218%-0.184%). Statistical analyses revealed no significant differences in AUC-ROC values between bit depths for any model-task combination (all p values > 0.05 after Bonferroni correction). Effect sizes were small to moderate (Cohen's d ranging from -0.415-0.391). Conclusion No statistically significant differences were detected between models trained on 16-bit and 8-bit images in the three evaluated tasks. These findings suggest that conversion to 8-bit images may reduce data storage requirements and improve data processing efficiency. Further research is needed to assess their usefulness in clinical tasks.

title: Multichannel Deep Learning Radiomics for Predicting Chemoimmunotherapy Response in Gastric Cancer: Multicenter Validation and Chemotherapy-alone Specificity Assessment.
abstract: Rationale and objectives To develop and validate a computed tomography-based model integrating multichannel deep learning and radiomics for predicting pathologic significant response (PSR) to neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy (NACI) in locally advanced gastric cancer (LAGC), and to assess whether the model specifically captures immunotherapy-related phenotypes by testing it on a chemotherapy-alone cohort. Materials and methods This multicenter study included 455 patients with LAGC: 411 receiving NACI (split into training, internal validation, and external test set 1) and 44 receiving chemotherapy alone (test set 2). From three-dimensional (3D) segmentations, the largest axial, coronal, and sagittal slices were stacked as three-channel input for a pretrained ResNet50 to extract deep features; radiomic features were extracted from the 3D volume. Features were fused, reduced by the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator, and modeled with a support vector machine to construct a deep learning radiomics (DLR) signature. A combined model further incorporated mismatch repair status, programmed death-ligand 1 combined positive score, and tumor grade. Model performance was evaluated by area under the curve (AUC), calibration, and decision curve analysis, with SHAP for interpretability. Results The multichannel model outperformed single-plane models (AUCs: 0.783, 0.749, 0.706). The DLR model achieved the highest AUCs (0.827, 0.802, 0.776), surpassing radiomics-only (0.756, 0.712, 0.691) and multichannel deep models. Critically, its AUC dropped to 0.597 in the chemotherapy-alone cohort. SHAP provided global and individual feature attributions. Conclusion The multichannel DLR model accurately predicts PSR to NACI in LAGC. The substantial performance decline in the chemotherapy-alone cohort suggests that the captured imaging phenotypes may be more closely associated with immunotherapy-related response, rather than with general chemosensitivity, potentially offering a noninvasive, interpretable tool for pretreatment stratification.

title: A Study in Contrasts: A Head-to-Head Comparison of MRI Contrast Phases for Deep Learning Liver Segmentation.
abstract: Rationale and objectives This study aimed to systematically evaluate the optimal MRI contrast phase(s) for automated liver segmentation using single-phase and multiphase deep convolutional neural networks (DCNNs) employing both early- and late-fusion techniques. Materials and methods This retrospective study included 586 hepatocellular carcinoma patients with multi-phasic contrast-enhanced MRI from an institutional database. DCNNs were trained using identical 3D U-Net-derived architectures on single phases and all possible multi-phasic combinations, with early- and late-fusion techniques, resulting in a total of 26 models. The dataset was randomly split into 70/15/15% for training/validation/testing, and performance was quantified by the Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC). From a collaborating site, 16 scans were used for external testing. The public LiverHccSeg dataset (n = 17) was used for additional testing. Furthermore, co-registered multiphasic examinations from the public Duke Liver Dataset (DLDS) were used as a third external test set (n = 68). Friedman's test with Dunn-Bonferroni post-hoc tests were used to compare performance across models. The top-performing model of each fusion strategy was defined by the highest Friedman mean rank. Results The late-fusion DCNN combining arterial, portal-venous, and delayed-phase MRI achieved superior performance across all models in the internal test set (mean DSC: 0.971 ± 0.021, P <.001 for all pairwise comparisons). The best single-phase DCNN used portal-venous phase (mean DSC: 0.970 ± 0.017) and significantly outperformed the best early-fusion DCNN based on a combination of portal-venous-, and delayed phase (mean DSC: 0.966 ± 0.036) (P < .001). The developed DCNNs demonstrated generalizable performance to external data (late-fusion: 0.961 ± 0.014, early-fusion: 0.964 ± 0.009, single-phase: 0.956 ± 0.035), the public LiverHccSeg (late-fusion: 0.911 ± 0.070, early-fusion: 0.898 ± 0.112, single-phase: 0.889 ± 0.109), and DLDS data (late-fusion: 0.907 ± 0.120, early-fusion: 0.873 ± 0.200, single-phase: 0.898 ± 0.134). Conclusion Optimal deep learning liver segmentation performance was achieved through late-fusion of arterial, portal-venous, and delayed-phase MRI and demonstrated generalizable performance to external data. Single-phase segmentation on portal-venous phase remained a computationally efficient alternative with satisfactory performance. The numerical gain from multiphase late fusion was small in terms of mean DSC and was most apparent as reduced variability and improved worst-case performance on external data.

title: The Additive Value of 18 F-PSMA-1007 PET/CT in Assessing Outcomes in Patients with Biochemical Recurrence After Radical Prostatectomy.
abstract: Rationale and objectives In recent studies, prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) has shown accuracy in restaging patients with biochemical recurrence (BCR). Here, we aim to evaluate the impact of ¹⁸F-PSMA-1007 PET/CT-guided treatment escalation (GTE) on clinical outcomes and validate an integrated prognostic model for biochemical progression-free survival (bPFS). Materials and methods This retrospective study included patients who underwent 18F-PSMA-1007 PET/CT for BCR between April 2019 and October 2024. title: A Conventional T1WI-Derived Signal Ratio for Differentiating Granulomatous Prostatitis From Prostate Cancer: A Two-Center Study.
abstract: Objectives To evaluate whether a signal ratio derived from conventional T1WI can differentiate granulomatous prostatitis (GP) from prostate cancer (PCa) in patients with overlapping PI-RADS findings. Materials and methods This retrospective two-center study included 29 patients with GP and 58 patients with PCa, all pathologically confirmed. Clinical, laboratory, and imaging parameters were analyzed. Inter-reader agreement was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify independent predictors and construct a combined diagnostic model. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and comparisons were performed using the DeLong test. Results There was no significant difference in PI-RADS scores between patients with GP and those with PCa (p > 0.05), and all patients with GP were classified as PI-RADS 4-5. The T1 ratio was significantly higher in GP than in PCa and showed the best diagnostic performance among individual parameters, with an AUC of 0.769 (95% CI: 0.662-0.876). In contrast, the T2 ratio and ADC ratio showed limited performance, with AUCs of 0.581 (95% CI: 0.447-0.715) and 0.599 (95% CI: 0.469-0.730), respectively. In multivariable analysis including age, T1 ratio, T2 ratio, ADC ratio, neutrophil count, and PSAD, T1 ratio, neutrophil count, and PSAD remained independent predictors for differentiating GP from PCa. A combined model incorporating these three predictors achieved an AUC of 0.873 (95% CI: 0.797-0.949), significantly higher than that of T1 ratio alone (DeLong p = 0.024). Conclusion T1 ratio provides independent diagnostic value for differentiating GP from PCa in patients with overlapping PI-RADS findings. Combining T1 ratio with neutrophil count and PSAD further improves diagnostic performance, supporting the potential utility of routinely available clinical and MRI parameters for noninvasive diagnosis.

title: STAT Priority Labeling in a Large-Scale CT Cohort: Frequency, Predictors, and Turnaround Time Associations.
abstract: Rationale and objectives Indiscriminate STAT labeling can erode the priority system's ability to distinguish clinically urgent from nonurgent computed tomography (CT) examinations, straining radiologist worklists and delaying interpretation of genuinely urgent studies. Materials and methods This retrospective cross-sectional study assessed 500,000 STAT CT examinations performed in 2025 at RadPartners (Radiology Partners, El Segundo, California, USA) imaging centers. After exclusion of duplicate records and examinations with insufficient clinical documentation, 365,676 examinations across four cohorts (head, chest, abdomen/pelvis, and combined chest-abdomen-pelvis [CAP] CT) underwent indication-based STAT appropriateness classification. Associations with place of service, reporting shift, and day type were evaluated using chi-square tests and multivariable logistic regression. Report turnaround times were compared using the Mann-Whitney U test. Temporal trends from 2019 to 2026 were assessed using linear regression. Results Of 365,676 examinations, 85,958 (23.51%) were classified as potentially inappropriate STAT. Rates were highest for CAP CT (31.01%) and chest CT (29.61%), followed by head CT (26.84%) and abdomen/pelvis CT (15.45%). Outpatient setting was the strongest independent predictor, particularly for CAP CT (odds ratio [OR], 72.09; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 64.77, 80.23) and chest CT (OR, 30.57; 95% CI: 29.01, 32.21). Potentially inappropriate STAT cases had longer turnaround times than appropriate STAT cases across all cohorts, most pronounced for chest CT (median, 975 minutes vs 37 minutes). A significant upward temporal trend was identified (+0.47% points per year; R² = 0.57; P = 0.036). Conclusion Nearly one in four STAT CT examinations lacked a documented urgent indication, with overuse concentrated in outpatient settings and daytime workflows, supporting targeted STAT stewardship interventions.

title: Three-Dimensional T2-Weighted Variable Flip-Angle Turbo Spin Echo for Cervical Spine MRI at 0.55 T: A Feasibility Study.
abstract: Rationale and objectives To evaluate the feasibility of three-dimensional T2-weighted sampling perfection with application-optimized contrasts using different flip angle evolutions (SPACE) for cervical spine magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) at 0.55 T and to preliminarily compare image quality with conventional two-dimensional T2-weighted turbo spin echo (TSE) in healthy volunteers and post-anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF) subjects. Materials and methods Five healthy volunteers (26.6 ± 2.9 years) and five post-ACDF subjects with titanium implants (63.6 ± 7.2 years) underwent cervical spine MRI at 0.55 T using sagittal TSE, axial TSE, and sagittal SPACE. Quantitative analysis included signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) efficiency and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)-to-spinal cord (SC) contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) efficiency. Two board-certified radiologists independently evaluated perceived SNR, CSF pulsation artifacts, motion artifacts, visualization of ten anatomical structures, and metal artifact severity using a 5-point Likert scale. Quantitative sequence comparisons were performed using exact paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests at the subject level. Qualitative 5-point scores were analyzed separately by cohort and category using linear mixed-effects models that accounted for subject and reader clustering. Results 3D SPACE demonstrated higher SNR efficiency than 2D TSE for both CSF and SC in both cohorts. CSF-SC CNR efficiency was higher with SPACE. In healthy subjects, 3D SPACE received higher reader scores for intraspinal nerve root visualization and CSF pulsation artifact reduction. In post-ACDF subjects, 3D SPACE received higher reader scores for nerve root visualization, whereas metal-artifact scores and other qualitative metrics did not show clear sequence-related differences. Conclusion 3D SPACE at 0.55 T is feasible for cervical spine MRI in healthy subjects and post-ACDF subjects with titanium instrumentation. Although diagnostic performance was not evaluated, the preliminary findings suggest potential advantages of SPACE, including higher SNR/CNR efficiency, improved CSF signal homogeneity with reduced CSF pulsation artifacts, and improved nerve root visualization, supporting further evaluation.

title: Large Language Models and a Recently Revised Radiology Classification: Modified CIRSE Grading With and Without Current Criteria.
abstract: Rationale and objectives Recently revised professional classifications may create a version mismatch for large language models, as plausible responses can reflect a superseded rather than the current schema. The modified Cardiovascular and Interventional Radiological Society of Europe classification, which subdivided Grades 1 and 3, provided a controlled setting to examine this problem. We evaluated four large language models with and without the current criteria supplied in the prompt. Materials and methods Sixty-four purpose-written vignettes, eight per category, were independently graded by two interventional radiologists, with consensus serving as the reference standard. Four models (gpt-5.6-sol, claude-sonnet-5, gemini-3.8-flash, and deepseek-flash) were queried under closed-book and guideline-augmented conditions three times per vignette, yielding 1536 requests. The primary outcome was run-1 exact-grade accuracy, compared within models using Holm-adjusted McNemar tests. Results Closed-book exact-grade accuracy ranged from 15 of 64 to 31 of 64, whereas all four models achieved 64 of 64 with the criteria supplied. All Holm-adjusted p values were <0.001. In a post hoc descriptive analysis, exact-grade accuracy was 0 of 128 classifications in the newly subdivided grades and 99 of 128 in grades retaining established labels. None of the four new subclass labels appeared in any of the 256 run 1 closed-book responses. Across all three closed-book runs, superseded grades accounted for 36.5% of responses. Conclusion Exact-grade accuracy was higher in all four models when the current criteria were supplied. In a post hoc descriptive analysis, complete exact-grade failure was confined to newly subdivided grades. Current classification criteria should be supplied explicitly for model-based complication grading.

title: Bioelectrical and optogenetic modulation for neuroimmune therapeutics.
abstract: Neuroimmune interactions are emerging as key regulators of inflammation, immunity, immune homeostasis, and disease progression. Neural circuits do not merely sense tissue injury, but also actively shape immune-cell recruitment, cytokine production, vascular function, and organ-level inflammatory outcomes. Here, we overview bioelectrical and optogenetic systems for neuroimmune modulation in diseases via the defined neural and inflammatory pathway. First, we review systemic neuroimmune modulating pathway and local neuroimmune modulators, and identify established neuroimmune molecular interactions in diseases. After that, we explain bioelectrical and optogenetic systems employed to modulate neuroimmune interactions. We evaluate representative studies with advanced delivery systems in consideration of neural target, immune effector, disease-relevant outcome, and safety. Finally, this review highlights both positive and negative clinical evidence of electroceuticals, and ultrasound-mediated and optogenetic systems predominantly in preclinical development. In summary and perspective, we prioritize and discuss the requirements for their further clinical translation. The integration of neural targeting with advanced materials and adaptive gene and drug delivery would be successfully harnessed for programmable therapies to modulate disease-relevant immune circuits without broadly suppressing host defense systems.

title: Tenecteplase for isolated central retinal artery occlusion secondary to internal carotid artery dissection: A case report.
abstract: Central retinal artery occlusion (CRAO) is a blinding neuro-ophthalmologic emergency. Internal carotid artery dissection (ICAD) is a rare but underrecognized etiology of CRAO, frequently missed at initial presentation due to absence of pathognomonic clinical signs. While early intravenous thrombolysis confers benefit in CRAO, evidence for tenecteplase (TNK) in ICAD-associated cases remains exceedingly sparse. A 44-year-old previously healthy woman presented with isolated acute left CRAO after routine jogging. Intravenous TNK (0.25 mg/kg) administered within 3 h of onset achieved complete visual recovery the next day. Cervicocephalic vascular imaging confirmed left ICAD. Six-month follow-up after dual antiplatelet therapy demonstrated favorable recanalization, stable visual function, and no cerebral or ocular ischemic events occurred. This case suggests that intravenous TNK thrombolysis within the therapeutic window can yield favorable visual outcomes and acceptable safety in patients with ICAD-associated CRAO. For patients with acute visual loss occurring after exercise, ICAD must be actively suspected. Prompt cervicocephalic vascular etiological assessment alongside emergency care, delivered via multidisciplinary stroke pathways for improved long-term prognosis.

title: Integration of multimodal large language models into point-of-care ultrasound documentation: A pilot study.
abstract: Introduction There are no studies evaluating the potential to deploy artificial intelligence in the interpretation of cardiac point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) documentation. Telexy Health developed an image interpretation and documentation system using multimodal model extensions with video capabilities (MLLM) and deployed it on the POCUS manager QpathE. This study evaluated the MLLM's agreement to experts in identifying cardiac POCUS views and interpreting normal and abnormal examinations. Methods This was a retrospective pilot study using cardiac POCUS studies stored in QPathE. The MLLM was applied to POCUS examinations until 350 examinations were reached, 100 normal, and 250 with pathology. MLLM view identification and interpretation were recorded using Qualtrics, with expert image review serving as the gold standard. Results The MLLM was applied to 370 examinations, with 20 failures. View identification agreed with expert review in 151 examinations (43.1%). Cohen's kappa showed fair agreement for apical four-chamber views between expert and MLLM, with moderate agreement for parasternal long axis, parasternal short axis, subxiphoid, and inferior vena cava views. The MLLM agreed with expert interpretation 86 of 100 normal examinations; the agreement varied by pathology with pericardial effusion, ejection fraction, aortic outflow tract, chamber size, and inferior vena cava having an agreement of 8%, 4%, 70%, 0%, and 12% respectively. Conclusion While agreement in image interpretation was poor, this vendor agnostic workflow demonstrated the ability to integrate an MLLM model into image interpretation. While it should not be incorporated into clinical practice in this state, future model improvement may enable automated POCUS interpretation and documentation.

title: Optic Disc Features in Nonarteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy: Spatial Organization and Structure-Function Associations.
abstract: Purpose To determine whether funduscopic features in non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION) are spatially organized and associated with structural and functional measures at presentation and outcome. Design Cross-sectional and longitudinal secondary analysis of the multicenter, QRK207 NAION treatment trial (NCT02341560). Participants Trial participants with symptomatic NAION and gradable color fundus photographs at enrollment (n=728) and Month 6 (M6; n=547). Methods We quantified hemorrhage, hyperemia, axoplasmic stasis (cotton wool spots/micro-opacities), pallid edema, and chronic changes via manual annotation. Each feature was analyzed both as presence versus absence (prespecified primary) and as burden standardized to disc area (secondary). Peripapillary swelling was graded 0-4 by degree of vessel obscuration. Spatial distribution was mapped using modified Garway-Heath sectors. We assessed associations with VF, OCT-derived swelling, and symptom duration. Main outcome measures Global and sectoral VF sensitivity (average total deviation; avgTD) and best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) at enrollment and M6; OCT-derived peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer thickness, peripapillary optic nerve head volume, and rate of ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer (GCIPL) thinning. Results At enrollment, hyperemic swelling (88.9%) and hemorrhage (79.5%) predominated, and pallid edema was common (27.9%). Acute hyperemia clustered nasally. Hyperemic swelling area correlated with shorter symptom duration (r s = -0.12, p = 0.004). The presence of pallid edema was associated with faster GCIPL thinning (-1.12 vs -0.37 µm/day, p < 0.001), worse enrollment acuity in multivariable models (β = -6.69 letters; p = 0.002), and modestly longer symptom duration (median 11 vs 10 days; p = 0.03). Enrollment features weakly associated with VF but did not predict M6 avgTD. Inferior peripapillary swelling mildly correlated with worse enrollment superior field deviation (r s = -0.27, p < 0.001). At M6, pallor was most prevalent (86.7%), clustered temporally, and was independently associated with worse avgTD (Inferior ONH to superior VF: β=-2.07 dB; p= 0.007). Conclusions Funduscopic features in NAION exhibit distinct, topographically organized spatial and temporal patterns reflecting evolving tissue injury, but have limited standalone prognostic value for long-term visual outcomes. Notably, acute pallid edema is relatively common in NAION.

title: Baseline Macular OCT Thickness of Ocular Hypertensive Patients Improves Prediction of Glaucoma.
abstract: Purpose To determine whether baseline macular ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer (GCIPL) and circumpapillary retinal nerve fiber layer (cpRNFL) thickness add prognostic value for glaucomatous visual field (VF) damage in patients with ocular hypertension. Design Retrospective clinical cohort study. Participants 330 eyes of 235 patients with ocular hypertension, defined by intraocular pressure of 22 mmHg or higher or an International Classification of Diseases coded diagnosis, without repeatable glaucomatous VF damage at baseline. Eyes came from both the African Descent and Glaucoma Evaluation Study and a clinical cohort at the Shiley Eye Institute. Methods Baseline GCIPL and cpRNFL thickness were measured from the first good-quality Cirrus optical coherence tomography (OCT) macular and optic-disc cubes. Clinical predictors were assessed with the Ocular Hypertension Treatment Study (OHTS)-European Glaucoma Prevention Study (EGPS) Risk Calculator. Repeatable glaucomatous VF damage required a Glaucoma Hemifield Test outside normal limits or a pattern standard deviation at the 5% level or worse on three consecutive reliable Humphrey 24-2 examinations. Main outcome measures Hazard ratios per 1 standard deviation (SD) of thinner global and sectoral GCIPL or cpRNFL, and the change in the Harrell concordance (C) index (ΔC) after adding each measure to the Risk Calculator. Results Glaucomatous VF damage developed in 47 of 330 eyes (14%) over a median 4.4 years. Adjusted for the Risk Calculator, thinner macular GCIPL was associated with conversion (hazard ratio [HR] 1.89 per 1-SD thinner; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.50 to 2.37; P < .001), and every macular sector was significant (HR 1.71 to 2.02). The Risk Calculator alone showed modest discrimination (Harrell C-index, 0.57). Adding macular GCIPL improved discrimination (ΔC +0.101; 95% CI, +0.022 to +0.220). Global cpRNFL thickness did not improve discrimination (ΔC +0.004; 95% CI, -0.021 to +0.133); among cpRNFL quadrants, only the inferior quadrant was associated with conversion (HR 1.50; 95% CI, 1.02 to 2.22). Conclusions In patients with ocular hypertension, thinner baseline macular GCIPL was associated with glaucomatous VF damage and improved the discrimination of the OHTS-EGPS Risk Calculator, whereas global cpRNFL thickness did not.

title: Precursor lesions are associated with distinct growth kinetics after atrophy onset.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate whether atrophic lesions arising from different retinal precursors show distinct temporal growth kinetics in age-related macular degeneration (AMD). Design Retrospective longitudinal cohort study. Participants 109 eyes of 88 patients with intermediate AMD (iAMD) developing cRORA. Methods Consecutive eyes with iAMD progressing to complete retinal pigment epithelium and outer retinal atrophy (cRORA) were identified by retrospective back-tracking of serial spectral-domain OCT. Precursors, defined as lesions that progressed to cRORA at the site of onset, were classified as drusenoid, subretinal drusenoid deposit (SDD), or acquired vitelliform lesion (AVL). Atrophy was segmented automatically on en face projections and manually corrected when needed. Temporal kinetics during the first 3 years after cRORA onset were assessed using piecewise linear time with knots at 1 and 2 years, adjusting for atrophic area, eccentricity, and number of foci at onset. Main outcome measures Rate and temporal kinetics of square-root-transformed total atrophic area growth by precursor. Results Of 109 eyes progressing to cRORA, 66 arose from drusenoid, 31 from SDD, and 12 from AVL. After cRORA, the model-estimated growth rate was different according to the precursor lesions, with 0.197 mm/year in the drusenoid group, 0.383 mm/year in the SDD group, and 0.429 mm/year in the AVL group (P<0.001). Both SDD and AVL groups grew faster than the drusenoid group (both P<0.001), whereas SDD and AVL did not differ (P=0.44). Temporal kinetics also differed by precursor lesion (P<0.001). Compared with the drusenoid group, the SDD group did not differ in year 1 (difference, 0.041 mm/year; P=0.43) but grew faster in year 2 (0.306; P<0.001) and year 3 (0.237; P<0.001). AVL group showed faster growth in year 1 (0.396; P<0.001) and year 2 (0.248; P=0.002), but not year 3 (0.060; P=0.57). Differences persisted after adjustment for atrophy characteristics at onset. Parafoveal SDD burden provided no additional information once precursor lesion was accounted for (P=0.12). Conclusion The study finds distinct temporal trajectories: atrophy arising from drusenoid lesions grows more steadily, whereas from SDD accelerates later, and from AVL grows rapidly early then decelerates. SDD presence elsewhere may be less important than whether the atrophy arose from SDD. The findings may have prognostic implications, representing a stratification variable in clinical trials.

title: Retinal Structure Reflects Cumulative Blast Exposure and Blast-Related Mild Traumatic Brain Injury.
abstract: Objective U.S. military service members experienced a high rate of blast exposures during post-9/11 military conflicts. Though a growing body of literature suggests that these exposures have long term consequences for health, objective biomarkers of blast-related neurotrauma remain limited. We used optical coherence tomography (OCT) to determine whether blast-related mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) and cumulative blast exposure burden were associated with retinal microstructural changes. Design A retrospective, cross-sectional cohort study at VA Boston Healthcare System. Participants Seventy-three United States post 9/11 veterans enrolled in the Translational Research Center for TBI & Stress Disorders (TRACTS) longitudinal cohort study who underwent OCT imaging based on assessment availability. Methods Principal observations were blast-related mild traumatic brain injury and cumulative lifetime blast exposure burden. Main outcomes measures Retinal thickness as measured by high-resolution Spectralis OCT imaging, including 7 individual macular layers, combined macular layers (inner retina, outer retina, and total retina), and the peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer, using automated segmentation software. Results Among 73 participants (mean [SD] age, 40.8 [9.4] years; 63 [86%] male), 25 had a history of blast mTBI (blast mTBI+) and 48 did not (blast mTBI-). Participants with blast mTBI+ had significantly thicker retinal layers in the macula, specifically in the 3mm quadrants around the fovea. The peripapillary RNFL (pRNFL) was significantly thinner in the blast mTBI+ group (p = .009), with the most significant thinning occurring nasally, most notably superior/nasal (p < .001). Greater cumulative blast exposure burden was associated with lower pRNFL thickness (ρ = -.288, p = .013) and greater macular outer retinal layer thickness (ρ = .319, p = .007). In cross-validated predictive analyses, pRNFL, outer plexiform layer, and outer retinal layer thickness significantly predicted cumulative blast exposure burden (leave-one-subject-out correlation, r = .335; conditional Monte Carlo permutation p = .005, full discovery Monte Carlo permutation p = .021). Conclusions Retinal structural measures distinguished veterans with blast-related mild traumatic brain injury and predicted cumulative blast exposure burden. These findings support OCT as an accessible approach for identifying retinal biomarkers of blast-related neurotrauma and cumulative blast exposure.

title: Assessment of sequential distalization with aligners using cone-beam computed tomography merged with intraoral scans.
abstract: Introduction Sequential distalization with clear aligners, supplemented by Class II elastics, is commonly used to treat mild-to-moderate Class II malocclusions. Although favorable clinical outcomes have been reported, the underlying mechanism of tooth movement remains incompletely understood because of the methodologic limitations of conventional analyses. Methods This retrospective study included 30 adults treated with Invisalign sequential distalization combined with Class II elastics. Pretreatment and posttreatment cone-beam computed tomography images and intraoral scans were merged using segmentation and registration software. The fused models were superimposed on stable maxillary structures with computer-aided design/computer-aided manufacturing software, and the movement of the maxillary first molars was quantified in 3 planes of space using a 3-dimensional coordinate system. Results The mesiobuccal cusp tip of the maxillary first molar moved distally by a mean of 1.75 mm, whereas the mesiobuccal root apex moved distally by only 0.35 mm, representing 69.7% and 27.6% of the planned movement, respectively. The achieved distal crown tipping (7.14°) significantly exceeded the planned value, whereas the mesial-out rotation (8.22°) was only slightly greater than planned. Conclusions In patients treated with sequential distalization and Class II elastics, maxillary first molar distalization occurred primarily through distal crown tipping and mesial-out rotation. Cone-beam computed tomography- intraoral scan fused models enabled precise 3-dimensional assessments of these tooth movements.

title: Accuracy and efficiency of artificial intelligence 3-dimensional segmentation and construction of cone-beam computed tomography images for impacted maxillary canines compared with the manual method.
abstract: Introduction This study aimed to develop and validate an artificial intelligence (AI) framework for the automatic identification, segmentation, and quantitative measurement of impacted maxillary canines. Differences in time and accuracy for segmentation and in the linear and volumetric measurements were compared between AI and manual methods. Methods An AI model based on a mask region-based convolutional neural network (RCNN) with multihead attention (Mask RCNN-MA) was trained using cone-beam computed tomography images from 214 patients with impacted canines. The dataset was divided at the patient level into training (n = 150, 70%), validation (n = 21, 10%), and test (n = 43, 20%) subsets. Segmentation of the maxillary region of interest, canines, and lateral incisors was evaluated using Dice similarity coefficients, sensitivity, specificity, and Hausdorff distance. Linear measurements relative to the occlusal plane and midsagittal plane, volumetric measurements, and canine crown proximity to the lateral incisor root were assessed. Results AI segmentation required significantly less time than manual segmentation. This model showed good agreement with human reference standards for the metrics including Dice similarity coefficients, sensitivity, specificity, precision, accuracy, and Hausdorff distance. Linear measurements revealed no significant differences between methods, whereas volumetric measurements yielded good agreement with intraclass correlation coefficients above 0.90. Conclusions The proposed Mask RCNN-MA framework provides an acceptable and reproducible method for cone-beam computed tomography segmentation and for linear, volumetric, and proximity measurements. This AI approach enables standardized 3-dimensional evaluation of impacted canines and may serve as a practical adjunct to orthodontic diagnosis and treatment planning.

title: Root volume changes after maxillary dentoalveolar expansion with clear aligners: A retrospective cone-beam computed tomography study.
abstract: Introduction This study aimed to evaluate root volume changes in maxillary posterior teeth of patients undergoing dentoalveolar expansion with clear aligners (CA). Methods This retrospective study included 30 adult patients with Class I malocclusion and mild crowding (≤ 3 mm) treated with Invisalign CA. All cases involved planned dentoalveolar expansion greater than 0.5 mm in posterior teeth. Pre- and posttreatment cone-beam computed tomography scans were used to assess the root volume of maxillary canines, premolars, and first molars using a semi-automated segmentation approach. Changes over time and differences among tooth types were analyzed using a linear mixed-effects model. Age and sex were included as covariates, and treatment-related and clinical variables were evaluated for their influence on root volume changes. Results The sample predominantly underwent mild dentoalveolar expansion (mean transverse width changes ranging from 0.5 to 1.4 mm). A statistically significant reduction in root volume was observed after treatment (∼21.7 mm 3 ; P <0.001). The magnitude of root volume loss differed among tooth types (P ≤0.005), with first molars showing the greatest reduction, followed by canines and premolars. Most teeth exhibited limited resorption, with 77.1% showing <10% volume loss and only 5.0% exceeding 20%. Treatment duration, amount of expansion, root movement, and root-cortical bone contact did not significantly influence root volume changes (P >0.05). Conclusions CA therapy involving mild dentoalveolar expansion in patients with Class I malocclusion and mild crowding was associated with a predominantly limited reduction in the root volume of maxillary posterior teeth.

title: Surgical Management of Lower Uterine Segment Atony Using Compression Sutures.
abstract: Uterine atony remains the leading cause of postpartum hemorrhage, and patients with prior cesarean deliveries may be at risk for isolated lower uterine segment atony due to a very thin and flimsy lower segment. Repeated hysterotomy incisions and repairs may result in a lack of normal myometrial muscle that is unable to maintain tone after delivery. The abnormally thin lower segment may not respond to standard uterotonic medications, and it can be challenging to place a balloon tamponade or vacuum system through a non-labored cervix, especially if the uterine fundus is adequately contracted. We describe intraoperative identification of a very thin lower uterine segment and its surgical management. Three rows of monofilament suture are placed across the lower segment to compress and reinforce the tissue. This technique is intended to reduce the risk of lower uterine segment distension and hemorrhage and the need for escalating medical and surgical interventions.

title: Offering prenatal CFTR modulators to prevent cystic fibrosis-related organ damage in utero.
abstract: Background CFTR modulator therapy has drastically improved the prognosis and quality of life for those with cystic fibrosis (CF). CF complications begin to manifest in utero, including meconium ileus, and current regulatory approvals for CFTR modulator therapy does not have a pregnancy indication. Despite this, there have been several documented cases of women taking CFTR modulator therapy during pregnancy with promising results of potential CFTR correction in utero. Objective To report one center's experience offering CFTR modulator therapy to pregnant women for prenatal CF treatment. Study design Eight pregnant women carrying a fetus at risk of having CF were presented with the option of CFTR modulator therapy during pregnancy with extensive counseling on the potential benefits and risks. Records from routine clinical care from prenatal, birth, and perinatal period were collected. Results Of the eight pregnant women, three intended to take the CFTR modulator, elexacaftor/ tezacaftor/ ivacaftor (ETI), however only two were able, as the third was unable to obtain insurance authorization. In one case, the infant was homozygous for F508del(p.Phe508del, c.1521_1523delCTT, 1653delCTT) variant with signs of worsening bowel obstruction on fetal imaging, however after ETI initiation at 27 weeks he was born without meconium ileus. In the other case of CFTR modulator therapy treatment, the infant carried a CFTR variant of varying clinical consequence, Y1032C (c.3095A>G, p.Tyr1032Cys), and one disease causing CFTR variant. After ETI initiation, ultrasound findings suggestive of bowel obstruction improved and there was no meconium ileus at birth. The family who desired prenatal ETI therapy but was unable to obtain insurance coverage, also had one disease causing variant and one of varying clinical consequence, G622D (c.1865G>A, p.Gly622Asp). Despite fetal imaging concerning for bowel obstruction this infant had no meconium ileus at birth and was classified as CFTR related metabolic syndrome/CF Screen Positive Inconclusive Diagnosis. Of the remaining pregnant women, 3 declined prenatal CFTR modulator therapy, one ultimately had negative prenatal diagnostics, and another terminated the pregnancy. Conclusion Decisions to treat with prenatal CFTR modulators are complex and influenced by multiple factors including phenotype variability, inconsistent insurance coverage, and uncertain potential risks and benefits. Outcomes of these cases ranged from pregnancy termination to successful reversal of ultrasound findings suggestive of developing meconium ileus.

Of the eight pregnant women, three intended to take the CFTR modulator, elexacaftor/ tezacaftor/ ivacaftor (ETI), however only two were able, as the third was unable to obtain insurance authorization. In one case, the infant was homozygous for F508del(p.Phe508del, c.1521_1523delCTT, 1653delCTT) variant with signs of worsening bowel obstruction on fetal imaging, however after ETI initiation at 27 weeks he was born without meconium ileus. In the other case of CFTR modulator therapy treatment, the infant carried a CFTR variant of varying clinical consequence, Y1032C (c.3095A>G, p.Tyr1032Cys), and one disease causing CFTR variant. After ETI initiation, ultrasound findings suggestive of bowel obstruction improved and there was no meconium ileus at birth. The family who desired prenatal ETI therapy but was unable to obtain insurance coverage, also had one disease causing variant and one of varying clinical consequence, G622D (c.1865G>A, p.Gly622Asp). Despite fetal imaging concerning for bowel obstruction this infant had no meconium ileus at birth and was classified as CFTR related metabolic syndrome/CF Screen Positive Inconclusive Diagnosis. Of the remaining pregnant women, 3 declined prenatal CFTR modulator therapy, one ultimately had negative prenatal diagnostics, and another terminated the pregnancy.

Conclusion

Decisions to treat with prenatal CFTR modulators are complex and influenced by multiple factors including phenotype variability, inconsistent insurance coverage, and uncertain potential risks and benefits. Outcomes of these cases ranged from pregnancy termination to successful reversal of ultrasound findings suggestive of developing meconium ileus.

title: Ophthalmic Artery versus Uterine Artery Doppler in the prediction of preterm pre-eclampsia at 11-13 weeks' gestation.
abstract: Background Preterm pre-eclampsia (PE) is a leading cause of maternal and perinatal morbidity and mortality. First-trimester screening using maternal factors (MF), mean arterial pressure (MAP), uterine artery pulsatility index (UtPI), and placental growth factor (PlGF) allows early risk stratification and effective prevention with aspirin. However, UtPI measurement is technically demanding and operator dependent. Maternal ophthalmic artery Doppler, expressed as the ophthalmic artery peak ratio (Oph-PR), reflects early maternal cardiovascular changes and may serve as an alternative or complementary marker for PE prediction. Objective To compare the predictive performance of adding maternal Oph-PR versus uterine UtPI to the first-trimester prediction model for preterm PE that uses MF, MAP, and, PlGF. Study design This was a prospective observational study involving women attending first-trimester screening at 11 +2 to 14 +2 weeks of gestation. Maternal factors, measurement of MAP, serum PlGF collection, ultrasound examination for UtPI and Oph-PR measurement, were performed during the visit. Receiver-operating characteristics (ROC) curve analysis was used to determine the area under the curve (AUC), detection rates (DR), and positive screening cut-off from the Bayesian Accelerated Failure Time (AFT) survival models in predicting the occurrence of preterm PE (<37 weeks of gestation). De Long's test was performed to compare the superiority of the AUCs among models. Results Of 946 eligible participants, 71 (7.49%) were affected by PE, and 21 (2.2%) had preterm PE. The predictive performance of the UtPI-based model (MF + MAP + UtPI and MF + MAP + UtPI + PlGF) was similar to that of the Oph-PR-based models (MF + MAP + Oph-PR and MF + MAP + Oph-PR + PlGF) in the prediction of preterm PE (AUC 0.805 and 0.837 vs 0.789 and 0.830; p=0.584 and 0.687, respectively). The combination of MF, MAP, UtPI, Oph-PR, and PlGF in predicting preterm PE demonstrated the highest AUC compared to the other prediction models (AUC 0.919, 95% CI 0.875-0.963). Conclusion UtPI and Oph-PR are comparable for first-trimester prediction of preterm PE. Combining both Doppler indices in a prediction algorithm may improve predictive performance for preterm PE.

title: Immune checkpoint inhibitors-induced -induced vs. Conventional Myocarditis: Navigating Pathophysiological and Clinical Divergences.
abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed cancer therapy but have introduced immune-related adverse events, among which ICI-induced myocarditis (ICI-M) is one of the most severe cardiovascular complication. Compared with conventional myocarditis (CM), ICI-M is a distinct entity characterized by a hyper-acute, T-cell-mediated autoimmune response due to loss of immune tolerance. While CM typically follows a viral or autoimmune trigger and often evolves toward resolution, ICI-M occurs early after treatment initiation (within 30-60 days) and is associated with high mortality and a significant burden of major adverse cardiovascular events. Clinical presentation differs substantially. CM commonly presents with chest pain and progressive myocardial dysfunction, whereas ICI-M often manifests with non-specific symptoms such as fatigue and carries a higher risk of early conduction abnormalities and malignant arrhythmias. Diagnosis is challenging, as conventional imaging may underestimate disease severity in ICI-M: left ventricular ejection fraction is often preserved and late gadolinium enhancement may be absent in early stages. Advanced techniques, including global longitudinal strain and cardiac magnetic resonance parametric mapping, are therefore crucial for early detection. Diagnosis of ICI-induced myocarditis may also be challenging because of symptom and biomarker overlap with other immune-related adverse events, particularly myositis. Non-specific manifestations and concomitant elevations of troponin and skeletal muscle injury markers can complicate early recognition and differential diagnosis. Management strategies reflect these differences: CM is generally treated with supportive approaches, whereas ICI-M requires immediate discontinuation of ICIs and prompt high-dose immunosuppression. Despite advances, prognosis remains worse in ICI-M, underscoring the need for early recognition and dedicated cardio-oncology pathways.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Algorithm for Detection of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy Compared with a Standard Electrocardiogram.
abstract: Background Artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiography (AI-ECG) may facilitate detection of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), but its ability to identify higher-risk patients undergoing clinical evaluation for HCM remains uncertain. Objectives To evaluate the diagnostic and prognostic performance of a commercially available AI-ECG algorithm among patients undergoing cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) for suspected or established HCM. Methods We studied 102 patients with HCM and 302 age-, sex-, and year-matched controls without HCM who underwent clinically indicated CMR. An AI-ECG algorithm was applied to the first available ECG preceding CMR. Diagnostic performance, incremental value beyond standard ECG features, and associations with clinical outcomes were assessed. Results ECGs preceded CMR by a median of 1.1 years. AI-ECG demonstrated moderate sensitivity (51.1%) and high specificity (96.1%) for identification of phenotypic HCM and incrementally improved discrimination and reclassification beyond demographic and conventional ECG variables (net reclassification improvement 0.19, p<0.001). Within one year of CMR, a positive AI-ECG was independently associated with the composite outcome (adjusted HR 2.68, 95% CI 1.42-5.09; p=0.003), driven by ICD placement and septal reduction therapy. Among patients with HCM, while exploratory, an AI-ECG probability ≥ 0.99 identified those at highest risk for subsequent events (HR 2.92, 95% CI 1.59-5.35; p=0.011). Conclusion In conclusion, among patients undergoing clinical evaluation for HCM, AI-ECG provided incremental diagnostic value beyond conventional ECG parameters and identified individuals at increased risk for subsequent treatment-related clinical outcomes.

title: Rising Prevalence of Metabolic Dysfunction - Associated Steatotic Liver Disease in an urban South Indian screening cohort: a Retrospective Cross-sectional Study.
abstract: Purpose Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), redefined in 2023 from non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, is highly prevalent globally, but population-level data using 2023 AASLD criteria and FibroScan-based assessment remain scarce in South Asia, particularly among asymptomatic adults undergoing routine health screening. Methods We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional study of 1,103 asymptomatic adults (mean age 43.1±12.7 years; 64.1% male) undergoing FibroScan-based Master Health Check-up at a tertiary centre in Chennai, India (2023-2025). MASLD was defined as controlled attenuation parameter (CAP) ≥249 dB/m plus ≥1 cardiometabolic risk factor; fibrosis was assessed by liver stiffness measurement (LSM). Results MASLD was identified in 716 participants (64.9%; 95% CI 62.1-67.7%). Affected individuals were older, had higher BMI, and more frequently had diabetes, hypertension, and dyslipidaemia (all p<0.01). In multivariable analysis, age, male sex, BMI, and diabetes were independently associated with MASLD. Notably, 53.4% of cases occurred in adults under 46 years, and 45.3% had normal liver function tests while 31.3% had normal ultrasound, indicating conventional screening substantially underestimates disease burden. Conclusions Nearly two-thirds of asymptomatic urban South Indian adults screened met MASLD criteria, predominantly working-age individuals under-detected by conventional tools. FibroScan-based screening should be considered in preventive health programmes to enable earlier detection.

title: Circulating tumor DNA to direct adjuvant immunotherapy across mismatch repair-deficient solid tumors.
abstract: Background Detection of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) harboring mutations that match those identified in resected tumor tissue signals occult residual disease after curative-intent surgery. Such patients are considered minimal residual disease (MRD)-positive and at high risk for recurrence and death. Few studies have shown that therapeutic intervention can alter recurrence risk in MRD-positive patients. We evaluated whether PD-1 blockade could reduce recurrence in MRD-positive patients with mismatch repair-deficient (dMMR) tumors after curative-intent resection regardless of tumor site of origin. Patients and methods We initiated a prospective phase II interventional study in patients who had undergone curative-intent resection of early-stage dMMR tumors from any anatomic site. Postoperative MRD status was assessed by first identifying those patients who had detectable ctDNA and then confirming the ctDNA relevance to MRD by matching mutations detected in ctDNA to somatic mutations detected in resected tumor tissue. Confirmed MRD-positive patients received 6 months of PD-1 blockade and were evaluated for ctDNA clearance and 24-month recurrence-free survival (RFS). MRD-negative patients underwent observation. Results We screened 184 patients with early-stage dMMR solid tumors after curative resection and tumor sequencing with ctDNA testing for MRD assessment. Twenty-three patients (12.5%) were MRD-positive; after excluding one assigned to placebo and three with synchronous radiographic disease, 19 were eligible. Six developed recurrences before pembrolizumab initiation despite being disease-free at enrollment. The remaining 13 MRD-positive patients received 6 months of PD-1 blockade. ctDNA clearance at 6 months was achieved in 11 of 13 patients (85%). Five treated patients (38%) developed recurrence during follow-up. Median follow-up for the MRD-positive patients was 59 months (95% CI: 52-NR). Among 152 MRD-negative patients managed with observation, 14 (9%) developed recurrence during follow-up; 2-year RFS was 92%. Conclusions These findings provide evidence that ctDNA-guided adjuvant therapy may offer clinical benefit in dMMR tumors regardless of tissue of origin.

title: Rucaparib versus docetaxel or second-generation androgen pathway inhibitor therapy for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer: final overall survival and safety from the phase III TRITON3 study.
abstract: Background We report final overall survival (OS) from TRITON3, evaluating rucaparib versus physician's choice (docetaxel or androgen-receptor pathway inhibitor [ARPI]) in chemotherapy-naive men with BRCA/ATM-mutated metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) progressing after one prior ARPI. We previously reported that rucaparib significantly improved radiographic progression-free survival (PFS) for patients with BRCA mutations, including versus docetaxel and ARPI only. Patients and methods This open-label, phase 3 trial randomized 405 patients (302 with BRCA mutations) 2:1 to receive rucaparib or physician's choice. Crossover from physician's choice to rucaparib was allowed after confirmed radiographic disease progression. OS was a key secondary endpoint. The primary endpoint and other key secondary endpoints were reported previously. Results For rucaparib vs physician's choice, median OS was 23.2 versus 21.2 months (HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.68-1.20; median follow-up, 44 months; BRCA subgroup), was 22.8 versus 21.7 months (HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.78-1.26; ITT), and was similar vs docetaxel or ARPI alone. PSA response rates (BRCA subgroup) were 54.7% (rucaparib) versus 26.7% (physician's choice). Of the 76% eligible to crossover in the BRCA subgroup (n = 53), median radiographic PFS from rucaparib initiation was 6.2 months (n = 30) and 18.1 months (n = 23) for those receiving initial docetaxel or initial ARPI, respectively. With long-term follow-up, acute myeloid leukemia/myelodysplastic syndrome incidence was 1%. Conclusions Although rucaparib demonstrated significant increases in radiographic PFS and response rate, OS was similar in both arms, albeit most patients crossed over. Thus, rucaparib is a safe and beneficial treatment option against BRCA-mutated mCRPC.

title: [Indications for prophylactic mastectomies].
abstract: Prophylactic breast surgery is a major risk-reducing option for women at very high risk of breast cancer, particularly carriers of pathogenic variants in BRCA1, BRCA2, PALB2, or TP53. Indications rely on specialized oncogenetic assessment, considering the identified variant, family history, age, personal history, prognosis of a potential index cancer, and feasibility of enhanced radiological surveillance. Bilateral prophylactic mastectomy substantially reduces breast cancer incidence but should never be presented as mandatory. It must be part of a shared decision-making process, discussed in a dedicated multidisciplinary tumor board, after comprehensive information and psychological support. In patients previously treated or being treated for unilateral breast cancer, contralateral prophylactic mastectomy should be individualized according to the risk of contralateral breast cancer, prognosis of the index tumor, and acceptability of annual MRI-based surveillance. From a technical standpoint, skin- and nipple-sparing mastectomy is currently favored whenever breast morphology, tissue quality, and oncological conditions are appropriate. Immediate breast reconstruction is generally preferred, although delayed reconstruction or no reconstruction must also be discussed according to the patient's wishes. Reconstructive options should be tailored to breast morphology, skin quality, comorbidities, body habitus, and patient preference. Available techniques include implant-based reconstruction, adjunctive or exclusive fat grafting, and autologous reconstruction using free or pedicled flaps such as DIEP, PAP, gracilis, or latissimus dorsi flaps. In patients with large or ptotic breasts, a staged approach with initial breast reduction or mastopexy followed by prophylactic mastectomy and immediate reconstruction can reduce complications and optimize outcomes. Prophylactic breast surgery therefore requires a specialized, individualized, and multidisciplinary approach.

title: [Immediate autologous breast reconstruction by profund artery perforator flap at the expense of the profund femoral artery: Technique and results (IBR by PAP)].
abstract: The profunda artery perforator (PAP) free flap, introduced for breast reconstruction by Allen in 2012, has become an increasingly important autologous option, particularly in immediate breast reconstruction (IBR). Anatomy and technique The PAP flap relies on perforators from the profunda femoris artery, consistently present in 98.8% of cases, with a mean diameter of 1.9mm and a pedicle length of 10 to 12cm. The fasciocutaneous paddle is harvested from the posteromedial thigh, below the infragluteal fold, with the patient in the dorsal lithotomy position, an approach that enables a two-team setup with simultaneous flap harvest and mastectomy with preparation of the internal mammary vessels. Preoperative planning relies on CT angiography and Doppler ultrasound to select the optimal perforator based on caliber, location, and course. Microsurgical anastomoses are performed to the internal mammary vessels. Mean flap volume is approximately 325cm 3 , and secondary fat grafting is performed in nearly all cases to achieve the desired final volume. Clinical cases Two patients illustrate the technical variants: the first (42 years old, recurrence following lumpectomy and radiotherapy) underwent flat flap inset to replace the resected skin; the second (46 years old, similar oncological context) had a cone-shaped flap modeled to allow immediate nipple-areola complex (NAC) reconstruction, with stable outcomes at 3years following fat grafting and areola dermopigmentation. Outcomes and indications Recent meta-analyses report total failure rates of 2% and fat necrosis rates of 6.1%. Donor-site morbidity remains moderate, with wound dehiscence occurring in 10 to 21% of cases. With over 14 years of follow-up, the PAP flap represents the best autologous alternative to the DIEP flap in IBR, combining anatomical reliability, absence of functional muscle morbidity, and a well-concealed donor-site scar.

The profunda artery perforator (PAP) free flap, introduced for breast reconstruction by Allen in 2012, has become an increasingly important autologous option, particularly in immediate breast reconstruction (IBR).

Anatomy and technique

The PAP flap relies on perforators from the profunda femoris artery, consistently present in 98.8% of cases, with a mean diameter of 1.9mm and a pedicle length of 10 to 12cm. The fasciocutaneous paddle is harvested from the posteromedial thigh, below the infragluteal fold, with the patient in the dorsal lithotomy position, an approach that enables a two-team setup with simultaneous flap harvest and mastectomy with preparation of the internal mammary vessels. Preoperative planning relies on CT angiography and Doppler ultrasound to select the optimal perforator based on caliber, location, and course. Microsurgical anastomoses are performed to the internal mammary vessels. Mean flap volume is approximately 325cm3, and secondary fat grafting is performed in nearly all cases to achieve the desired final volume.

Clinical cases

Two patients illustrate the technical variants: the first (42 years old, recurrence following lumpectomy and radiotherapy) underwent flat flap inset to replace the resected skin; the second (46 years old, similar oncological context) had a cone-shaped flap modeled to allow immediate nipple-areola complex (NAC) reconstruction, with stable outcomes at 3years following fat grafting and areola dermopigmentation.

Outcomes and indications

Recent meta-analyses report total failure rates of 2% and fat necrosis rates of 6.1%. Donor-site morbidity remains moderate, with wound dehiscence occurring in 10 to 21% of cases. title: Evolution and impact of sarcopenia and myosteatosis in the context of liver transplantation.
abstract: Introduction and objectives Sarcopenia and myosteatosis have a well-documented adverse impact on survival in liver cirrhosis patients. This study aimed to assess the prevalence and risk factors associated with muscle impairment before liver transplantation (LT), their evolution after LT, and to determine their prognostic value. Patients and methods All cirrhotic patients listed for LT at our center between 2006 and 2010 were included. Sarcopenia and myosteatosis were assessed on transverse L3 CT images at LT listing and at 12 (M12), 60, 120, and 180 months after LT. Results The study population consisted of 198 patients, 75.3% of whom were men, and 149 underwent LT. At LT listing, sarcopenia was diagnosed in 45.5% of patients and myosteatosis in 36.5% and 20.1% had both sarcopenia and myosteatosis. One year after LT, 56.1% of patients had persistent sarcopenia and 15.3% had de novo sarcopenia. Sarcopenia significantly improved at M12 post-LT (p=0.034). Post-LT patient survival was 89.2%, 76.3%, and 59.3% at 1, 5, and 10 years respectively. In multivariate analysis, at LT listing, MELD score ≥ 25 (HR: 2.549; p=0.001), sarcopenia (HR: 1.749; p=0.004) and myosteatosis (HR: 1.630; p=0.012) were found to be independent risk factors for overall mortality. The effects of sarcopenia and myosteatosis were additive: overall survival was significantly reduced in patients with both sarcopenia and myosteatosis compared to patients with isolated sarcopenia/myosteatosis (p=0.001). Conclusions Sarcopenia and myosteatosis are common in cirrhotic patients listed for LT, persist after LT, and have a major and independent impact on overall mortality.
